The cuisine here is delicious, heart-warming and full of the strong flavours typical of this region.

Name: Gostilnica Ruj
Address: Dol Pri Vogljah 16, Dol pri Vogljah, 6221, Slovenia
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: Regional cuisine and making the most of local ingredients are the hallmarks of this restaurant near the Italian border, which resembles a private house from the outside. The restaurant’s passion for food will enhance your appreciation of the region, which is also well represented on the wine list.

Name: Jožef
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant, housed in a modern, comfortable hotel in the village centre, boasts an attractive, bright dining room on the first floor and attentive, friendly, almost entirely female staff. The cuisine is traditional yet reinterpreted with a contemporary twist.

Name: Gostilna Repovž
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: You drive through an enchanting landscape of rolling hills and small villages to reach this restaurant, which has been run by the same family for more than three centuries. Their warm welcome and desire to introduce their guests to the region’s superb cuisine is evident from the outset, with dishes offering an extraordinary culinary journey through local traditions.

Name: Mahorčič
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: A warm and friendly welcome awaits at this pleasant family-run restaurant offering excellent value for money. A combination of Slovenian ingredients and a skilful and talented chef results in often elaborate dishes of the highest quality. Not to be missed!

Name: TaBar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This simple, informal and friendly restaurant in the historic centre is perfect for a night out with friends. The cuisine is creative and imaginative, taking inspiration from a wide range of culinary styles. Guests have the option of choosing a variety of small courses tapas style or opting for the more traditional dishes on the à la carte menu.

Name: Anyukám Mondta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Anyukám Mondta is everything a good neighbourhood restaurant should be. It offers something for everyone – from homemade pizzas to refined modern Italian dishes and tempting daily specials – and prices cover a wide range to suit all occasions, so you can easily eat at a reasonable price. Excellent produce is prepared with care, resulting in hearty, flavoursome dishes, while service is smooth, well-paced and comes with plenty of personality.

Name: Kistücsök
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: If you’re coming for dinner, make the most of it and stay over at this small hotel, which comes complete with its own swimming pool. Well-regarded locally, the restaurant is known for its consistently good interpretations of classic Hungarian dishes, which have been modernised both in their composition and their look. Flavours are fresh, with the occasional global influence, and prices are reasonable. The ‘Taste of the Region’ menu is always a great choice.

Name: Morzsa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: ‘Crumbs’ is a new wave bakery-cum-bistro with a relaxed urban style, owned by a charismatic and exuberant designer. Sit inside to watch the making of the delicious loaves and pastries or head out to the terrace for some people-watching in the part-pedestrianised lane. Modern, flavour-packed small plates are served throughout the day and can be accompanied by something from the biodynamic wine list. Of course, a pastry is a must to finish – the lemon meringue cruffin is a hit.

Name: Sparhelt
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Set away from the lakeside, in a busy residential neighbourhood, this all-day bistro is run with honesty and integrity. The menu has a Hungarian heart and perfectly reflects the seasons, with the likes of chilled fruit soups in summer and hearty, warming dishes in winter; if the native Mangalitsa features, do order it. The smart terrace is always a popular place to sit.

Name: Casa Christa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Roads fringed by almond trees and terraced vines lead to this stunning hillside spot with far-reaching views over Lake Balaton. It’s a restful place and comes with seven restored wine press houses which now play host to designer bedrooms with private saunas. Within the grounds is this beautiful, orangery-style restaurant with a lovely terrace and a concise menu of dishes bursting with Hungarian, French and Italian flavours.

Name: Macok
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This bright, colourful bistro is known by food-lovers across the country, and it certainly deserves its reputation. It’s family-owned and professionally run by a friendly team, and the menu is an appealing mix of colourful Hungarian and Mediterranean dishes. Classic flavours are in abundance but the presentation is decidedly modern; the beef cheek goulash is not to be missed.

Name: AJ's Pit Bar-B-Q
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Owners Amanda and Jared Leonard and pitmaster Patrick Klaiber have a hit with AJ's Pit Bar-B-Q. From the white-washed facade and neon sign to the picnic tables and white metal chairs inside, this place smacks of a classic mom-and-pop BBQ spot. The menu is equally traditional, offering a feast of properly smoked meat. Cornbread leans inventive, and trust us when we say that you want the custard-stuffed version. Other items you'll want to try include plump and juicy sausage links stuffed with jalapeño cheddar. Beef belly ends are smoked for at least 14 hours before being cut into cubes, tossed in a citrus-chipotle sauce, and thrown back in the smoker to deliver these caramelized beauties. If you're so inclined, AJ's offers workshops with the pitmaster.

Name: Tavernetta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Tavernetta is an absolute stunner. Every detail has been considered and designed to encourage lingering and relaxing in this unique and beautiful space. The Italian menu nods to more well-known dishes from multiple regions, and the plates are refreshingly uncluttered. The classics are prepared with obvious care, as in a crostini primavera with a sourdough base layered with creamy stracciatella, heritage English peas and lovely spring greens. Crisp and fresh, it's simple but spot on. Spaghetti all'amatriciana is loaded with guanciale, tomato and pecorino romano for a wonderfully savory dish. To finish, tiramisu is a classic for a reason.Come at lunch for a delicious two-course deal, then spring for a dessert.

Name: Basta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Concrete floors, cream walls and an open kitchen with a wood-burning oven set an industrial-chic tone at Basta. Snag a spot at the bar and you'll have a front row seat to the culinary action, where family-style, contemporary Italian-American cooking is the name of the game. Start things off right with a shareable starter like burrata or the silky chicken liver mousse with peach mostarda that is sided by crusty bread from next-door sister bakery, Dry Storage. Definitely don't skip the smoked dark green olives—they're an unexpected delight. From there, entrees are satisfying, especially the half chicken. End on a sweet note with a plate of five beignet-style doughnuts dusted with powdered sugar and a dulce de leche Chantilly cream.

Name: The Ginger Pig
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The story here begins with Chef Natascha Hess's time as an exchange student in Beijing, where her host family taught her the fundamentals of Chinese home cooking, lessons that sparked a full-bore culinary passion. After several trips back to China, her travels broadened to include Shanghai, Singapore, Bangkok and more—a catalogue of flavors that she then translated into a hugely popular food truck, eventually becoming this lively, rustic brick-and-mortar location (though the truck can still be seen parked in front). It's clear that Chef Hess’s time abroad was well-spent: from hearty boiled pork and cabbage dumplings dressed with chili oil to stir-fried cabbage with Thai chili jam, the cooking bursts with flavor, including a healthy dose of heat.

Name: Glo Noodle House
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: The location in a run of the mill strip mall belies the cool interior at this spot named for Chef/owner Chris Teigland's mother. Inside, dark charcoal and dark wood are offset by pops of bright colors, while overhead, vibrant lanterns of different colors and sizes draw attention.  The kitchen delivers serious flavor on their noodle/ramen-based menu. Kick off with a sweet and savory skewer of marinated tofu skewer served with a miso peach jam and an almond and sesame candy crumble. Ramen options run the gamut from miso bacon and brothless versions to the death wish designed for spice hounds who want the heat without sacrificing flavor. Sweets worth saving room for include the sweet crispy rice cake with smoked caramel and kasu-lime ice cream.

Name: La Diabla Pozole y Mezcal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This Larimer Street spot from chef Jose Avila is no fuss and no frills but all heart. Inside, it's equal parts cozy and colorful with dark, unpolished wood floors and vibrant walls. In case the name didn't give it away, pozole is the star of the show. They feature the typical rojo and verde broths as well as white, black (with a smoky char from roasted chilies) and vegetarian—eschewing pork for mushroom and chayote. It's an impressive take on a Mexican staple. Customize the protein and opt for the tender and flavorful pork, and order a mezcal from their extensive selection. Should pozole not call your name, there are tacos and pambazos on offer, and on weekends, mornings are met with chilaquiles and a concha French toast that's worth an early wake-up call.

Name: Ash'Kara
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: At this brightly hospitable neighborhood spot, Chef Reggie Dotson offers up an exploration of contemporary Israeli cuisine, pulling in influences from the Mediterranean, North Africa and Middle East. The menu leads with mezze, featuring top-notch versions of familiar staples like hummus, babaganoush and falafel, paired with excellent wood-fired whole-grain pita made from heritage wheat. Dinner offers more substantial fare, as in savory tagines with eggplant or lamb tenderloin. The cooking is vegetable-forward, and takes pains to accommodate all dietary restrictions (there's even a gluten-free pita option), but there are no gimmicks here, just thoughtful, full-flavored dishes made with high quality ingredients and a bit of extra style.

Name: Hop Alley
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: Hop Alley refers to the original name for Denver's Chinatown, but there's nothing historic about this sleek restaurant. In keeping with the contemporary look, the Chinese menu with Sichuan leanings features modern adaptations of classics. There's plenty of originality and bold flavors, as seen in dishes like gai lan, a dynamic plate of grilled Chinese broccoli with schmaltz and oyster sauce finished with house-made duck salt and crispy shallots. Shrimp toast topped with whipped shrimp and chicken thigh is far from standard thanks to mustard gastrique and tiger vinaigrette. Dan dan mian noodles are set with ground pork in a Szechuan peppercorn broth that brings the heat.Cocktails, like the bees knees with chili-infused honey, also riff on the classics.

Name: Mister Oso
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: It's laid-back and lively at Mister Oso, a small but stylish spot with a creative menu and clever cooking. Chef/owner Blake Edmunds has a hit on his hands, with a second location opening in recent years. While tacos may be the main event, this isn't your typical taqueria menu. Instead, discover ceviches, salads and dishes bearing Latin American and international influences. Everything is served family style. Pick up a tortilla and start building a delicious treat, as in the mojo tacos with coconut-braised pork shoulder finished with a mojo salsa and pickled red onion served with crispy fried plantains. Coconut rice, served in a piping hot cast iron dish, bridges sweet and savory thanks to pickled shaved peppers and thin, shaved red onion.

Name: Zhuan Zhuan Hui (Lianhua South Road)
Address: 27 Lianhua South Road, Jinjiang, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: Despite its hard-to-find entrance, this flagship of the chain has earned solid fandom among locals with its no-frills, home-style Sichuanese cooking that is frugally priced. Instead of severe piquancy that can pack a punch, expect a more tamed heat that caters to the palate of most. Braised crucian carp with Chinese patchouli is aromatic and tasty, while Chengdu-style twice-cooked pork renders rich meaty flavours. The homely atmosphere is also a plus.

Name: Chen Mapo Tofu (Qinghua Road)
Address: 10 Qinghua Road, Qingyang, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Mapo tofu is a world-famous Sichuanese classic dating back to the Qing Dynasty. Word has it that this century-old shop is the true original source of this numbing, spicy dish, invented by Lady Chen. Silky tofu, ground beef and spices are cooked in a stone pot that stays hot for a long time, perfect with a bowl of steamed rice. Zhong dumplings and lotus leaf-wrapped steamed pork in spiced rice flour are also worth trying.

Name: Guan Jin (Wuhou)
Address: 4F, Block 5, Think Zone, 19 Chenghan South Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace
Description: The space is tastefully furnished in traditional Chinese style, with direct access from street level via lifts. The terrace is great for al fresco dining; private rooms offer tea master service. The signature braised fish in spicy bean sauce is made with the river fish of your choice, such as longsnout catfish, marble goby, or topmouth culter. The sautéed pork belly with green chillies packs a serious punch, perfect with a bowl of steamed rice.

Name: Yongle Restaurant (Wuhou)
Address: 36 Xiaojiahe Middle Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: You can't miss this shop – just look for the red lanterns, perforated wood windows… and the queue. Since 1985, it's been serving home-style Sichuanese dishes made the traditional way: stir-frying, steaming and shuizhu. The braised eel with eggplant has contrasting textures and the savvy use of Chinese patchouli elevates it to the next level. For non-spicy food lovers, the sticky rice pork ribs and meatball soup are both great choices.

Name: Yao Guai Mian
Address: 49 Longzhou East Alley, Jinjiang, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Tucked away in a longstanding residential area, this noodle shop has a loyal following. The noodles are either served in spicy or white broth, or tossed in various seasoning pastes. For noodle soup, try their signature eight-treasure white broth made with chicken, bamboo shoots and dried seafood including shrimps, squids and oysters. Or have your bouncy noodles tossed in the famous mala chilli pork sauce for heady, addictive aromas.

Name: Shudidanggui
Address: 34-25 Shiwuzhong Street, Wuhou, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Named after two Chinese herbs, the concept of a therapeutic diet is at the core of this establishment. Diners are greeted by an herbal tea sweetened with stevia, and the menu is built around Chinese medicines. The signature beef noodle soup is infused with dang gui, believed to improve blood circulation, making it a lunch time favourite for many. Yellow croaker with galangal and patchouli is also popular. Some dishes require pre-ordering.

Name: Dumpling & Drinks (Lanchao Road)
Address: 16 Lanchao Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: It doesn't take a rocket scientist to figure out the eponymous specialities of the house. Dumplings are freshly made daily in the open kitchen and varieties are served each day, each to be ordered in units of 5. Those filled with pork and mushrooms, or beef and Chinese celery are the highlights. Nestled in a quiet neighbourhood, the cosy room features a clean and modern décor with a light wood and dark green colour scheme.

Name: Organization South
Address: No. 209, Block 1, Pebble Walk, 669 Wanxiang South Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Though it moved from Kuanzhai Alley to this spot in the south of town, diners still come in droves. The playful, retro décor with fake tree trunks and red lanterns is aptly matched by a menu disguised as a martial arts instruction book. Besides famous Sichuanese wok-fried dishes such as green chilli ‘ruthless’ chicken, and braised swamp eel, cold appetisers and seasonal offerings are also worth a try. The generous portions are great for sharing.

Name: Ming Ting Xiao Guan (Jinjiang)
Address: No. 12, 54 Dacisi Road, Jinjiang, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: A spin-off from the local household name Ming Ting Restaurant, this compact eatery is always jam-packed with diners hungry for its traditional Sichuanese fare. The room is bright and airy, while the semi-open kitchen lets diners watch the chefs flaunt their skills. Signature dishes include the silky smooth douhua, the unmissable Dad’s twice-cooked pork loaded with wok qi, and novel items like the durian spring roll. Reservations not accepted.

Name: Lao Chengdu San Yang Mian
Address: No. 6-8, 46 Guojielou Street, Qingyang, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This ‘hole in the wall’ may lack bells and whistles, but it’s popular with locals. Soup and tossed noodles are divided into 3 trifectas, namely the ‘old’, ‘new’ and ‘more’. Blanched noodles tossed in spicy meat sauce with diced string beans in the ‘old’ category is the most popular item. Feel free to order wontons with chopped chillies on the side. And nothing cools your mouth better than a bowl of tofu dessert with red bean soup.

Name: Gan Ji Fei Chang Fen
Address: No. 1-3, 18 Ma'an North Road, Jinniu, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: With over 30 years of history, this tiny gem is no secret to locals in search of a bowl of hearty glass noodle soup with braised pork intestines. The toothsome, springy noodles are made in-house. Choose between mala spicy soup and rich white broth. Optionally, order intestine knots on top for an extra layer of texture. And don't miss the piping hot guokui – crispy flatbread with pork and Sichuan pepper filling.

Name: Hu Er Ge Yao Shan Ti Hua
Address: 146-19, Section 1, Yi Huan West Road, Qingyang, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The simple shop has little ambiance to speak of, but that hasn't put hungry locals off from flocking here since 1999. In fact, it's the favourite late-night spot for many who come for its famous pork trotter soup – simmered with Chinese herbs for eight hours until the connective tissues are gelatinous and the soup is loaded with collagen. Stir-fries such as spicy chitterlings, and green chilli pig snout fried rice are also brimming with wok hei.

Name: Rongrong Beida Pugaimian
Address: No. 2-4, Section 2, Jiefang Road, Jinniu, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Famous for flat noodle soup, this brand always attracts a long queue at the door. Diners can see the four chefs pulling a piece of dough to make the signature noodles – thin, soft, but with a lovely chew. There are two sizes and a few toppings to choose from, all boasting spot-on seasoning of the perfect amount of heat punctuated by a mild sweetness. Be prepared to share a table with strangers at peak hours.

Name: Mind
Address: 85 Longyang Street, Wuhou, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Serving just 4 types of noodles, along with a few sides during the day and a menu of home-style dishes at dinner, this shop urges diners to slow down and mindfully savour their clean, simple flavour. Freshly wrapped wontons are dressed in red oil or served in seafood broth. Also look for the hawker carts where steamed rice cakes with red bean filling are made. The complementary ‘Laoying’ laurel tea is perfect to round out their sweetness.

Name: Yu Jiu Xiang
Address: 4 Xingrong East Alley, Wuhou, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: This simple neighbourhood shop has been serving traditional Chengdu cooking since 2014. Signature items come in big portions enough for a few to share. Blanched pork belly dressed in garlic sauce strikes a fine balance between meaty and garlicky flavours. Spicy fried chicken cubes with chillies pack the typically Sichuanese numbing, fiery oomph. With only about 10 tables and 3 private rooms, reserve your table ahead of time or arrive early.

Name: The Woo's
Address: 39-17 Hongji Middle Road, Jinjiang, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: A quaint mansion obscured by a big tree is home to this restaurant run by the Woos. The cosy space shows hints of nostalgia; both cold appetisers and hot mains are based on tradition, but fine-tuned and modernised. The fried wild-caught yellow croaker in a mound of fried chillies has silky, moist flesh; with its bold flavour, it goes perfectly with alcohol. The sweet sticky rice dumplings with a runny filling round off your meal nicely.

Name: Yangboying Za Jiang Mian
Address: 19-13 Tongsi Road, Qingyang, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The owner-chef who used to work in a famous restaurant uses traditional techniques to make noodle soups and assorted toppings, each boasting a substantially different taste profile. Noodles dressed in meat sauce with sesame paste, red chilli oil and Sichuan pepper is a regional classic exuding intoxicating aromas. Those who prefer less heat may opt for dumplings in seafood soup that cooked with dried shrimp, cuttlefish and scallops.

Name: Mosnack
Address: Shop L101-1-A, Shimao 52+ Mini Mall, 99 Mengzhuiwan Bystreet, Chenghua, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted
Description: This simple shop is clean and bright, with a picture frame window looking into the kitchen. The menu has three sections: dumplings, wontons, and noodles, all handmade in-house. The pork and chive dumplings in sour soup stand out in particular – the soup imparts deep flavours of laver, dried shrimp and sesame. Try also the wontons in a flavourful pork bone broth that takes six hours to make. Ask for a table on the terrace on a fine day.

Name: Zhu Ji Zhi Mian Pu
Address: 194 Yixinqiao South Street, Jinjiang, Chengdu, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Surrounded by furniture shops, this noodle place has a retro feel to it. Wooden tables and bamboo chairs add to the overall rustic flair. The noodles are made fresh in-house, which explains their incredibly silky, bouncy texture. Zha jiang mian is the must-try here: blanched noodles are topped with a soybean-based ground pork sauce that is robust, savoury and mildly spicy. If you enjoy their noodles, you can buy some raw to take home.

Name: Ting Yuan 399
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: The entrance sign shows ‘garden’ in Chinese, priming guests for a pleasing experience as they soak up the verdant setting. It’s also no stranger to food lovers in the know who flock here for the river fish dishes. Plump swamp eels from inland rivers are poached in a flavourful broth loaded with spices and herbs. When served at the table, the eels are drizzled with sizzling hot oil, their flesh being tender and juicy, but with a crispy chew.

Name: Erge Shih Tang
Address: 145 Cinghai Road, Gushan District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The room isn’t particularly spacious, but it does exude a homely feel. Similarly, the menu features Taiwanese home-style cooking, that is lightly seasoned and in smaller portions. The signature grilled Pacific saury in honey sauce is braised until the bones are tender and edible, perfect with a bowl of steamed rice, pork lard rice, or braised pork rice. Or you can opt for steamed taro root cake with shiitake and dried shrimps as starch.

Name: Hsi Lo Tien Beef Soup
Address: 98 Gongyuan South Road, North District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Its hallmark beef soup is simmered with beef bones, brisket, fat and onion and thin slices of lean beef are added just before serving. Pour on a dash of rice wine for extra fragrance or dip the beef in the fiery home-made chilli sauce for a kick. The assortment soup offers a choice of cuts from beef tendon and brisket to liver and all the soups come with a bowl of steamed rice or braised pork rice. Stir-fries like beef with kale are also worth trying.

Name: Hou Chi Duck Rice
Address: 201 Zihciang 1st Road, Sanmin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: For over 40 years, Hou Chi has been attracting a loyal following with its tasty duck dishes. Its famously nourishing dang gui duck soup exudes deep herbal aromas; order it with noodles to make a complete meal. The signature duck rice comes with thickly sliced duck and pickled radish. Order an extra platter of smoked or braised duck if you fancy more protein. You can even specify which cuts you prefer.

Name: Lao Ye Mei Shi Guan (Fengshan)
Address: 54-56 Haiyang 1st Road, Fengshan District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The restaurant has been a landmark of Fengshan’s culinary scene for almost two decades. Its speciality, smoked duck glazed in cane sugar, is a masterclass of flavour and is particularly juicy and tender thanks to the duck breed from China. Pan-fried pork belly with lemongrass is another hit, featuring freshly slaughtered local pork and sustainably grown lemongrass from the owner’s farm, without forgetting the fish soup that cooks for four hours.

Name: Night School Braised Pork Rice
Address: 109 Jingcheng Road, West District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This favourite late night supper spot among many Taichungese stays opens late; in fact, the later it gets, the busier it is. Naturally, braised pork rice is the must-try speciality – slow-cooked pork belly in an amber sauce is melty, but also bouncy; top it with pickles or dried radish with chilli to cut through the richness. Other Taiwanese dishes, such as braised napa cabbage and fried tofu, are also worth a try.

Name: Cianjin Braised Pork Rice
Address: 26 Datong Street 2nd Street, Cianjin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This third-generation family business dates back to 1959 and its signature braised pork rice has been the favourite breakfast for generations of Kaohsiungese. Only the back cut is used, with pork skin and a layer of fat that give the dish a complex depth. Feel free to order shredded pork, dried fish floss, marinated tofu, or even a soft-boiled duck egg to go with the rice. It’s always busy and may close early when all food has sold out.

Name: Black-faced Spoonbill Canteen
Address: 17-18, Haipu, Shihfen Village, Cigu District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: A must for birdwatchers and seafood lovers, the Canteen is one of the best places to see the endangered black-faced spoonbills in Taiwan. From September to the following May, these migratory birds fly here and feed on the fish in the restaurant owner’s pond. Besides sustainably farmed milkfish and clams straight from his fish farm, the menu also includes other seafood classics, like deep-fried squid in salted egg yolk sauce.

Name: Feng Chi Goose
Address: 170 Pingxi Road, Shalu District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: For decades, this simple shop has been attracting hungry diners with its signature sliced goose platter boasting juicy flesh and wafer-thin skin. The second-generation owner intentionally leaves some bones and gristles in for diners to gnaw on. Goose offal, marinated meat and other sides are also popular. For starchier dishes, order plain noodle soup, or jazz it up with cuttlefish and thin, flat e-fu noodles.

Name: A Hsing Congee
Address: 289, Section 3, Minzu Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: A Hsing has been serving Tainan-style milkfish congee since 1965, attracting a queue as early as 5am every morning. You can specify the cut you want; the belly is the most prized part of the fish, boasting fatty, silky flesh. The congee base is flavoursome; fried garlic pieces on top add extra aroma. Feel free to order milkfish belly dressed in soy sauce as well. Unlike most simple shops in Tainan, air-conditioned seating is available inside.

Name: Traditional Tainan Feast (Anping)
Address: 152 Huaping Road, Anping District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: With red lanterns, spring couplets, red floral tablecloths and chair cushions, this nostalgic place embodies the Chinese festival atmosphere. Since 2010, it has been attracting diners with well-made Tainan snacks and century-old classics such as Danzai noodles and oyster omelette, best enjoyed with a glass of winter melon tea. Private rooms are decorated with maps of ancient Tainan and named after its different neighbourhoods.

Name: San Hao Yi Kung Tao Angelica Duck
Address: 2, Section 1, Fucian Road, Central West District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Circa 1949, it was a hawker stall in the Dongmen Traffic Circle before moving here in the 1960s. Now into the second generation, the family business still attracts a loyal fanbase thanks to its duck noodle soup made with the Chinese herb Dang Gui (a.k.a. Chinese angelica root). The amber broth has rounded flavours, a lingering aftertaste and a hint of bitterness. With freshly slaughtered duck and al dente noodles, it makes for a wholesome meal.

Name: Po Jen Tang
Address: 27, Lane 300, Section 2, Simen Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Visa credit card
Description: This century-old Chinese medicine shop was converted into a restaurant specialising in therapeutic food. The sixth-generation owner intentionally kept the apothecary cabinets and used some inscribed plaques as dining tables. Eight tonic soups are offered each day, all tasty and mild in herbal flavour – refer to the menu for their medicinal actions. Make it a complete meal by ordering a set – with noodles tossed in sesame oil, a drink and sweet soup.

Name: Ke Peh
Address: 76-1 Bade 2nd Road, Sinsing District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Its name means ‘Uncle Chicken’ in Taiwanese because the founder used to be a poulterer and older males are affectionately called uncles. Naturally, the menu is chicken-heavy, along with a small selection of stir-fries. Free-range chicken from Tainan is used in soups and prepared in a myriad of ways, such as braised in a tonic concoction of rice wine and Chinese herbs, or salt-baked to golden perfection. Reservations are recommended.

Name: Yuan Wei
Address: 2, Lane 227, Huanyin Street, Datong District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Tucked down a small alley behind the train station and without a proper sign, this eatery with over 70 years of history and just four tables is easy to miss. Even the interior feels more like a wood carving store than a restaurant. The menu is easy to navigate, with only 20-odd choices. Stir-fries are the must-try items – Yuan Wei fried rice, and pork jowl, characterised by remarkable wok-hei. Cash only and expect a long wait at peak hours.

Name: A Xing Shi Mu Yu
Address: 252 Wunsian Road, North District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This no-frills shop may lack glitzy décor but, for over 15 years, plenty of regulars have been coming here for its freshly slaughtered milkfish. Signatures include fried milkfish belly that boasts crispy skin and tender flesh. Milkfish soup is always served with braised pork rice everywhere in Tainan, but A Xing’s version comes with garlic rice instead. Fried fish intestines run out early in the morning. Come early or pre-order over the phone.

Name: Shang Hao Chih Beef Soup
Address: 6, Section 1, Beian Road, North District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The early bird gets the worm; you really need to come early to get a taste of this restaurant’s famous beef soup – it tends to sell out before 11 am. Local gourmets fall in love with the hand-sliced Tainanese beef in a beef bone stock that is amber-coloured and deeply flavoured. Dine-in guests ordering beef soup are also entitled to all-you-can-eat steamed rice, or braised pork rice with pork rind and peanuts. Try also beef or offal stir-fries.

Name: Kaiyuan Fried Spanish Mackerel Thick Soup
Address: 307 Kaiyuan Road, North District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The absence of both an obvious sign and air conditioning hasn’t deterred hungry locals from flocking here from 7am till late over the past four decades. With generous chunks of deep-fried Spanish mackerel in a stock made with halibut, bonito and fried garlic, the eponymous thick soup makes a great meal by itself or a snack between meals. If you’re lucky, you may even get to try the deep-fried mackerel skin that offers great seafood umami.

Name: Yi Wei Pin
Address: Shop 111 & 112, Yong Le Market, 177-179, Section 3, Guohua Street, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Splitting from Fu Sheng Hao, a household name in the realm of Taiwanese savoury rice pudding known as wagui, the owner started Yi Wei Pin in 2013 to amplify his grandpa’s culinary legacy. Much darker in colour than its Taipei counterparts, the wagui is made with local rice milk, freshly slaughtered pork, velvet shrimps and house-braised ground pork sauce. Try it with washabi or minced garlic also. Their milkfish thick soup is also popular.

Name: A Ming Zhu Xing (Baoan Road)
Address: 72 Baoan Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Don’t be surprised if you see a queue even before this shop’s opening at 5pm – after all, its cellophane noodle soup with pork offal is one of the must-try Tainan delicacies for many travellers. Chef A Ming still cooks the offal like his father did almost 70 years ago – in a bain-marie to prevent overcooking. As well as the signature pork heart soup, try pork ribs or duck feet and wings braised in a garlicky herbal stock.

Name: Bei Gang Tsai Rice Tube (Yancheng)
Address: 166 Hesi Road, Yancheng District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This third-generation family business dates back to 1956 and many Kaohsiungese grew up with its ‘tube’ sticky rice, which is actually steamed with braised ground pork in a metal tub, turned out on a plate and topped with gravy. Do order a soy-marinated ‘iron egg’ on the side to go with the rice. There are also several soups on the menu, including steamed egg custard soup – the sponge-like custard sucks up the flavourful stock nicely.

Name: Mao Yuan
Address: 185, Section 2, Chang'an East Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Service is friendly and attentive at this home-style joint which has been serving the neighbourhood with old-time local delicacies since 1971. Most diners pick the catch of the day at the seafood stand; otherwise, a chalkboard menu next to it lists all their signature dishes, such as baby oysters with garlic and steamed seasonal fish with preserved winter melon. Portion sizes can be adjusted according to the number in your party.

Name: Jen Ho Yuan
Address: 2F, 112, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Since 1956, this restaurant has been attracting loyal fans with its authentic Yunnan fare. In 2022, it moved to this new address, with its bright, airy main dining room and private rooms. Rest assured the menu and food stay the same – try the steam pot chicken, the sliced pork cheek cold appetiser, or the green peas in chicken fat. The true showstopper is string beans stuffed with minced shrimp, for the intriguing contrast of textures and layered flavours.

Name: Yun Lai Fang
Address: 463 Zhongshan 2nd Road, Lingya District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted
Description: For over 20 years, many Kaohsiungese have considered this homely restaurant the venue of choice for all sorts of banquets and family dinners. Home-style classics like scrambled egg with shrimps, and stir-fried beef with Manchurian wild rice stems may lack showy plating, yet always bring comfort with their familiar flavours. As the shop is always busy, the owner kindly asks diners to order all dishes at once; additional orders won’t be entertained.

Name: Yeh Jia Calamari Rice Noodle Soup
Address: 142, Section 2, Guohua Street, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Founded in 1935, this shop claims to be the creator of calamari rice noodle soup. Into the third generation, the owner still insists on making thick rice noodles with brown rice for its fragrance and firm texture. Calamari from Indonesian waters are cooked in a clear broth with intense flavour, a hint of peppery aroma and a sweet aftertaste. The shop is a bit congested, but clean and air-conditioned. Expect to queue for a table on holidays.

Name: Wang Shih Fish Skin Dishes
Address: 612 Anping Road, Anping District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The owner used to be a milkfish farmer and is extremely picky when he shops for milkfish. Customers come here for the freshest milkfish, shipped from Qigu daily in the small hours. As the name suggests, the signature is his milkfish skin with 0.3 mm of flesh attached, served either in a soup made with onion, fish, chicken and pork bones, or dressed in braised minced pork sauce. His Tainan-style congee and braised pork rice are also popular.

Name: Hung Chi Rice Shop
Address: 96 Liwun Road, Zuoying District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: As opposed to typical braised pork rice shops that can sometimes feel a little dated, this one boasts a bright, simple interior with full-length windows. The cartoon pig logo also makes it appealing to a younger audience. Despite its fresh look, the menu focusses on good old Taiwanese favourites. Braised pork rice is a must, and you have the option to top it with an over-easy egg. Do also order sides like braised cabbage, and pork tendon.

Name: Hang Zhou Xiao Long Bao (Da'an)
Address: 17 & 19, Section 2, Hangzhou South Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This popular soup dumpling shop was born over 20 years ago after its owners were taught how to make xiao long bao by a Shanghainese chef. Only the freshest pork hind leg cuts are used as the filling and the dumpling ‘skin’ is made simply with flour and water. Their soup-squirting dumplings are also known for their lightness. The red bean pancake uses two kinds of red beans in its silky filling which is complemented by a crisp sesame pastry crust.

Name: Tsui Feng Yuan
Address: 5, Lane 8, Section 3, Bade Road, Songshan District, Taipei, 105, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: At this sister restaurant to Peng Family, the chef insists on cooking Cantonese food exactly the way his great uncle did. Lamb belly hot pot is a winter speciality made with Australian lamb, red bean curd, sugarcane and ginger. Equally popular is crispy duck stuffed with mashed taro, steamed egg white custard with scallops and fish head hot pot. Service is friendly and warm and reservations are recommended on holidays.

Name: Cigu Yang Ke Yuan Chia
Address: 96 Jhongcing Road, Rende District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The owner’s family has been running an oyster farm for almost 50 years. With unrivalled access to the best oysters in town, they decided to open this shop in 2019, specialising in made-to-order oyster dishes. The signature deep-fried oysters are lightly battered and boast crispy crusts and creamy centres. The oyster fritter with shredded cabbage and chives is also not to be missed, while oyster broth with a fish-based stock imparts much umami.

Name: Saka
Address: 7, Alley 9, Zhongshan Road, Daya District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: At the end of a meandering alley stands this quaint shop with over 40 years of history. The second generation of the family business prides itself on its signature dish – chicken braised in rice wine with Chinese herbs. No water is added and the broth bursts with deep umami. The chicken tastes especially good after being dipped in chilli soy sauce and ground pepper. Parking is available, but the thoughtful servers advise diners to take public transport after sampling the dish.

Name: A Wen Rice Cake
Address: 74 Boa-an Road, Central West District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Amid century-old shops on the same street, A Wen opened its doors only in 2016. But it has quickly won the hearts of many with their rice cake made from scratch. Rice milk is mixed with three sweet potato starches for the right consistency before steamed, sliced and fried till golden. Try the Zhao Pai variety for rice cake in bamboo shoot pork sauce. The over-easy egg is the icing on the cake (pun intended); try also their house-made chilli sauce.

Name: Lao Shih Kuan Noodles
Address: 81-12 Zhennan Street, Qingshui District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The owner’s father was a sergeant major who learnt to make hand-rolled noodles in a village for military dependents. Noodles are still made like they were decades ago, retaining a lovely chew and dressed in sesame sauce with braised ground pork. Order a soft-poached egg on top; let the yolk run and stir the noodles before eating. Try also sour and spicy tofu with peanuts, or wontons in paper-thin skin tossed in a special sauce

Name: Hao Nung Chia Migao
Address: 66, Section 2, Jiankang Road, South District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: In 1946, this rice cake joint opened its doors in South District, away from the city’s busy tourist spots. It has ever been a hit with the locals who can’t get enough of its addictive migao, topped with braised pork sauce, fish floss, cucumber and peanuts. The second-generation owner insists on making migao just like his father did: the sticky rice is soaked, steamed and kept warm in a woven reed tub next to the stove to keep it moist and chewy.

Name: Hsiao Cho Chih Chia
Address: 420 Jilin Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This little gem with only five tables opened its doors in 1995 and moved to this address in 2010. The chef has been cooking professionally for over 40 years and he excels in making additive-free, simple but delicious Taiwanese dishes with the freshest catch from the sea. Regulars also come for abalone silkie chicken soup, double-boiled with Chinese herbs for two hours. Grilled pork trotter with gelatinous skin and juicy flesh is also unmissable.

Name: Jai Mi Ba
Address: 159-1 Bao-an Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Its full-length windows and open kitchen may not look like your typical noodle shop. The owner-chef has honed his skills in French cuisine for over 10 years and opened this minimalistic shop in his hometown for Taiwanese noodles to mingle with French techniques and sauces. The short menu shows promising creativity and it changes every week, except seared ox tongue with noodles in truffle sauce, and cheese caramel flan that are always available.

Name: Mi Yuan Tzu Steamed Glutinous Rice
Address: 30 Nanhai Street, Sinsing District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: After selling sticky rice in a market for 10-plus years, the owner couple opened this shop in 2021. Tables are set on a plant-adorned porch with tiled floor and walls; the cartoon duck and handwritten logo create a strong visual identity. The signature boneless duck sticky rice entices with its sesame oil and ginger aromas, while taro pork rib soup boasts starchy tuber infused with meaty flavours. Honey black tea from Taitung makes the perfect pairing.

Name: Ibu Kitchen
Address: 635, Section 2, Jhongshan Road, Meinong District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Right next to Meinung Folk Village, Ibu Kitchen specialises in Aboriginal Taiwanese cuisine made with produce from the Bunun owner-chef’s hometown in Mount Tengzhi. The menu is dominated by healthy options like fried egg tofu in plum sauce, steamed millet dumpling with pork and sakura shrimps, and free-range chicken braised in plum sauce with shiso leaves. The room is generously adorned with greenery, with commanding and gorgeous mountain views.

Name: Monsoon
Address: 3F, 126 Wenlin Road, Shilin District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The room with bare concrete, exposed bricks and reclaimed furniture adjoins a terrace generously adorned by potted plants. Having spent 20 years with Western cuisine, the chef revisits his roots and tells captivating culinary stories with refined vegan neo-Hakkanese cooking. All ingredients are sourced from Miaoli County where he hails from. The dish ‘Rebirth’, for example, is smoked cabbage wrap with a mashed potato and salted mustard greens filling.

Name: Hello VietNam
Address: 92 Chenggong Road, Central District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This cheerful restaurant is run by its Vietnamese owner. The menu tips towards the Northern end of her home country, and cilantro is used sparingly to cater to local taste. The speciality bun dau mam tom consists of rice noodle squares, pork intestines, pork feet, blood sausage, deep-fried tofu and leafy greens, alongside fermented shrimp paste, or a fish sauce dip. Nem ran (fried spring rolls) and pork skewers are also worth trying.

Name: Le Pont
Address: 39-6 Rensyong Road, Renwu District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: At first sight, this restaurant, famous for roast goose, may have little to do with its name but semantically, its first shop was next to a bridge. And that name was in French because the owner was inspired to add fried scallion to goose fat for a now-popular condiment – just a drizzle can make any blanched leafy green a gourmet dish. Try steamed rice with goose fat, marinated goose egg with red yeast rice, and goose fat French fries.

Name: A Kuo Lu Wei
Address: Raohe Street Night Market, 226 Raohe Street, Songshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: It sells a range of items braised in a spiced marinade. Try their duck wings, pork uterus and baby sweetcorn.

Name: Unnamed Clay Oven Roll
Address: Nanjichang Night Market, Stall 74, Lane 311, Section 2, Zhonghua Road, Zhongzheng District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This push cart near the end of the market always attracts a queue. Try their sweet pastry and long shaobing.

Name: Good Friend Cold Noodles
Address: Shilin Night Market, 31 Danan Road, Shilin District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Noodles dressed in sesame sauce impart a hint of lemony fragrance, a perfect match for egg drop miso soup.

Name: Ciao Zai Tou Huang's Braised Pork Rice (Ciaotou)
Address: 106 Ciaonan Road, Ciaotou District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Ciaotou was the centre of Taiwan’s sugar production and this 6-decade-old joint fascinates its fans with terrific braised pork rice boasting a savoury-sweet taste. Pork shoulder and belly in a specific ratio are hand-diced and braised till melting before being drizzled over steamed rice. Pork thick soup, and assorted pork offal make perfect companions with the signature rice. Expect to queue any time of the day. It closes on major holidays.

Name: Yung Tung Milkfish
Address: 60 Minquan Road, Syuejia District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Syuejia District is among the top five milkfish farming areas in Tainan, attracting foodies from all over the island. Yung Tung’s signature milkfish congee uses a fish stock that bursts with umami. Various parts of milkfish are served fried, braised or blanched. The braised fish head, and fish floss rice are especially popular. It also carries grass carp, tilapia and common carp, alongside hot dishes such as braised pork sinew.

Name: Bo Home
Address: 167-2, Cingnian 1st Road, Lingya District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The founder opened Bo Home in 1969 to feed hungry workers away from home with nutritious comfort food – braised pork rice, and giant grouper soup. Over time the menu grew bigger, but the drool-worthy signature rice topped with amber, luscious diced pork remains the key draw. On top of that, order stir-fried squid in salted egg yolk sauce, or stir-fried whelks if you want variety. Open till midnight, so it’s perfect for late night snacks.

Name: Zhu Xin Ju
Address: 69 Xinyi Street, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This quaint red-brick mansion built circa 1846 has been home to an omakase restaurant serving traditional Taiwanese banquet dishes since 2015. The room was carefully restored to its former glory, befitting the old-time recipes the head chef got hooked on. For a flat fee per person, your party will be served seven dishes and one soup, all made with local seasonal ingredients like milkfish from Cigu and rice from Houbi. Reservations are mandatory.

Name: Little Tree Food (Da'an Road)
Address: 17, Lane 116, Section 1, Da'an Road, Da'an District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: There’s no shortage of vegetarian restaurants in Taipei, but not many position themselves as a vegetarian equivalent of an American bistro. The head chef has experience in Sichuan and western cuisines, so his menu shows eclectic influences in addition to pastas and pizzas. Spicy dumplings with tofu filling are Sichuanese inspired; fried cauliflower is enrobed in Korean gochujang glaze; pad krapow burning bowl is a Thai-style salad.

Name: Kaiyuan Road No Name Milkfish
Address: 313 Kaiyuan Road, North District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: A firm favourite among locals, this shop doesn’t have a name, but regulars call it ‘the milkfish shop next to the big tree under a balcony’. Unsurprisingly, one can expect to find various cuts of milkfish on the menu: the fatty belly, skin, intestines and fish balls. Fish skin soup is especially popular; the skin is stuffed with minced fish, giving it a unique texture unlike others. Note that intestines tend to run out early in the morning.

Name: Fu Tai Table Third Generation
Address: 219, Section 2, Minzu Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Fu Tai Table began as a street vendor over 80 years ago; not until the 2nd- and 3rd-generation owners moved into this spot in 2015 did it have a permanent address. It’s the perfect place to experience the unique ‘fan zhuo zai’ culture – diners order a bowl of braised pork rice with a number of small plates which appear on the table stacked on top of each other in a tray. Only fresh ingredients get to the table. Popular choices include fried milkfish fillet.

Name: No Name Lamb Soup
Address: 144, Section 2, Fucian Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: After five decades of business in Guohua Street Market, the lamb soup stall shut its doors in 2013. Regulars lamented the loss but the owner’s nephew quit his job in Taipei to re-open the shop here. The famous soup made with freshly slaughtered local lamb meat and bones is the must-try item, but do order other lamb cuts and offal blanched in the soup and dressed in sesame oil. Come early – everything is sold out before 11 am.

Name: Small Park Danzai Noodles
Address: 321, Section 2, Simen Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Over 70 years ago, a stall opened by a small park and the owner would sit on a tiny stool to blanch the noodles, to be tossed in pork sauce or served in soup. Nowadays, the park no longer exists, but the owner still sits on a stool like the old days. Soup noodles are recommended – silky, al dente thin egg noodles in a flavoursome broth, topped with velvet shrimps and braised minced pork. Do order sides or braised dishes on top.

Name: Lo Cheng Migao
Address: 241, Section 2, Minzu Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The owner had been selling fried eels and squids for ages before he started serving migao by chance in 1985. Surprisingly, his sticky rice topped with braised pork, sliced cucumber, fish floss and peanut quickly surpassed his original offerings in popularity – and he has focused on migao and sishen herbal soup ever since. The gravy on his migao has a peppery aroma to go alongside the rich and deep flavours.

Name: Hsia Ta Tao Lan Migao
Address: 6 Kangle Street, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Since 1961, this simple shop hidden in a residential neighbourhood has been making its famous migao with aged glutinous rice, to be topped with sliced cucumber, dried fish floss, a fish ball, and slow-cooked pork sauce made with pork jowl, shallot, garlic, sugar and soy. In addition to Sishen soup, the classic companion to migao, feel free to pair it with other choices such as pork cartilage soup, fish skin soup, or deep-fried dough stick soup.

Name: Rong Rong Yuan
Address: 25, Section 4, Xinyi Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Valet parking,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The chef has been at the helm here for 30 years and each dish is prepared the same way as it was when the shop opened in 1965. The must-try braised pork ribs are slow-cooked in an onion broth for six hours until the meat falls off the bone – the perfect match for the guangbing flatbread. Other signatures include oxtail on a sizzling hotplate, dongpo pork with red yeast rice, and Beggar’s chicken. Most items need pre-ordering. Service is warm and homely.

Name: Da-Qiao-Tou Tube Rice Pudding
Address: 41, Section 3, Yanping North Road, Datong District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Though technically in a night market, this third-generation family business is only open from dawn till dusk. Since 1973, the regulars have been returning for its steamed sticky rice that is chewy but never mushy. Year-old aged rice is mixed with fried scallion and garlic before steamed with lean or fatty pork. It tastes best with homemade sweet chilli sauce and spicy radish sauce. Also try the oyster soup steeped in umami and plump oysters.

Name: Cabbage Rice and Pork Rib Soup
Address: Yansan Night Market, 2, Lane 17, Section 3, Yanping North Road, Datong District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Simple but addictive, cabbage rice and clear pork rib radish soup are the comfort food everyone craves.

Name: Do It True (Xinyi)
Address: 506, Section 4, Ren'ai Road, Xinyi District, Taipei, 110, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The menu at this 60-plus-year-old restaurant offers variations of dishes that the owner’s great uncle once cooked for Empress Cixi of Qing Dynasty. Crispy and juicy, the deep-fried pork balls made with hind leg cuts are an absolute must-try. Pork and cabbage pickle casserole, grouper fillet in distiller’s grain sauce, and giant inch-thick scallion pancakes are also recommended. It’s located on a tree-lined boulevard and comes with large windows and walnut wood furniture.

Name: Qin Yuan Chun (Central)
Address: 129, Section 1, Taiwan Boulevard, Central District, Taichung, 400, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Wheelchair access
Description: Run by fourth-generation owners, this 70-plus-year-old family business is usually full of regulars. The dining room is plainly furnished, but customers don’t come for the ambiance, but the authentic Jiangzhe classics such as pork trotter aspic, drunken chicken and stir-fried swamp eel. Steamed-to-order xiao long bao boast thin, translucent skin and soupy pork filling. The take-out counter offers quick service for those on the go.

Name: Xiao Chu Den
Address: 243 Daye Road, Nantun District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The owners opened a cosy shop in 2018, specialising in Taiwanese light meals and snacks, before moving to this spot in 2020. With just three tables inside and one outside, this tiny gem is always busy. Braised pork on rice boasts an addictive gelatinous texture and deep flavours, while thickly sliced braised beef noodle soup is another must-try for noodle lovers. Certain items tend to run out early so consider pre-ordering your food by phone.

Name: Dong Shang Taiwanese Seafood
Address: 217, Section 6, Anzhong Road, Annan District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: For over three decades, the owner-chef has been supporting charitable causes and cooking for the disadvantaged. Regulars come here not just for his classic banquet dishes, but also for his vision of using only local, eco-friendly ingredients. All dishes, including the array of signature milkfish items, and ‘herbal’ prawns farmed without antibiotics and harmful chemicals, are available in three different portion sizes.

Name: Thai Yuan
Address: 53 Lingya 2nd Road, Lingya District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This simple shop has generated lots of buzz on social media since it opened in 2020. Despite the lack of air conditioning, diners love the exotic street vibe in the bright blue setting adorned by Thai knickknacks. As its name suggests, Pad Thai is the signature item, a mildly spicy and tangy noodles dish. Thai coffee is also not to be missed. Order o liang for black, or café yen with milk and condensed milk. Check its Facebook page for days off.

Name: Joes (Gangshan)
Address: 111 Hehua Road, Gangshan District, Kaohsiung, 820, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only
Description: Gangshan is famous for its goat and you can’t leave without trying caprine dishes. Before opening Joes in 1955, the founder had long been selling goat in the market. With his connections, Joes always has access to the freshest goats. Signature dishes include Angelica goat hot pot, an herbal tonic with ribs and skin-on cuts. Stir-fried goat with bitter melon, and blanched goat slices with chilli bean sauce are also good. Bookings aren’t accepted.

Name: A Cheng Goose (Zhongshan)
Address: 105 Jilin Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Opened in 2010, this branch of the brand has been focusing on its take-out service since the COVID-19 pandemic. A new three-storey branch right across the street was launched to take care of dine-in customers. Its famous goose from Yunlin County is served two ways – boiled or smoked, the latter being the most popular. Diners can also choose the cut: the leaner, boneless breast or the tender, juicier leg. Try the braised gizzards or blood pudding, too.

Name: Peng Family
Address: 60 Dongfeng Street, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The owner-chef moved to Taiwan from Hong Kong over 35 years ago to bring authentic Cantonese cooking to the island. The décor of his family-run restaurant may be rather old-school but the crystal ceiling lamps, red carpet and Chinese paintings are welcoming and familiar. Seafood dishes, such as silky egg white custard with scallops, fried crab with glass noodles in a clay pot, and steamed seafood, are particularly prized.

Name: Din Tai Fung (Xinyi Road)
Address: 277, Section 2, Xinyi Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 110, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The story of the international chain famous for xiao long bao dates back to 1972 when its first shop opened on Xinyi Road. The former flagship eatery is now takeaway-only, but dine-in service is available on the other side of the street in a 330-seater four-storey venue inaugurated in 2020. Besides the aforementioned soup dumplings, also try the sweet and sour pork, bitter melon pork rib soup and steamed taro buns.

Name: Chi Chia Chuang (Changchun Road)
Address: 55 Changchun Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Valet parking,Visa credit card
Description: Chicken features heavily on the menu and the owner is picky about them – he uses only pullets from 5 to 6 months old for their tender meat. Specialities include the classic three-cup chicken that imparts rich aromas, perfect with the chewy pork blood cake. The crispy deep-fried chicken rolls, and the rich, flavourful chicken soup are also worth trying. Don’t forget to end the meal with their homemade egg pudding. Service is warm and friendly.

Name: Lao Shan Dong Homemade Noodles
Address: Shop 15, B1, 70 Xining South Road, Wanhua District, Taipei, 108, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This household name in the beef noodle scene has been attracting a loyal following with its ribbon noodles and beef broth since 1949. Beef bones and a blend of Chinese herbs give the broth its flavour and depth. Noodles are cut and cooked to order and local and Australian beef is simmered in the broth for hours until tender, so slurping up the broth gives you a burst of flavours. Cold sides such as pork ear in aspic and pickled cabbage are made fresh daily.

Name: Chung Chia Sheng Jian Bao
Address: Shilin Night Market, 38 Xiaodong Street, Shilin District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This stall sells pan-fried buns with crispy bottoms and fluffy tops. Choose between cabbage and pork fillings.

Name: Niou Jia Juang
Address: 19 Xinfeng Street, Dongshi District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This 60-year-old household name is undergoing an 18-month renovation and is temporarily operating at a spot 50 metres from the original shop. From the cartoon cow on the sign to cow-shaped decorations inside, beef is obviously the staple offering here. Local yellow beef is cooked nose-to-tail in traditional Hakkanese ways and the offal is unmissable – try scallion bone marrow, and cold beef tripe dressed in sweet and sour sauce.

Name: Ke Kou Beef Noodles
Address: 911 Dadun Road, Xitun District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Both the owner and his wife are beef lovers and Ke Kou is their brainchild. The signature noodle soup with red braised beef and sinew boasts a complex and rich broth – simmered for hours with 35 different Chinese herbs – that complements the springy noodles and tender Australian beef shin perfectly. Braised ox tripe perfumed with spices and herbs, and the seemingly simple kelp that imparts an intense savoury-sweet flavour are recommended.

Name: Luo Jia Food
Address: 65, Section 3, Xiangshang Road, Nantun District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Sesame oil lover alert: this no-frills shop is famous for dishes cooked with the earthy, nutty oil. The façade's familiar big yellow sign is gone in favour of a muted colour scheme, but the signature items remain as delicious as ever. Simmered for a whole day, the sesame oil chicken leg soup exudes aromas of wine and herbs; throw in noodles for a complete meal. Stir-fries such as pork kidney in sesame oil broth or braised pork rice are also impeccably made.

Name: Taichung Meatball
Address: 529, Section 3, Fuxing Road, South District, Taichung, 402, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: One of the best known places for frugal eats, this veritable institution has been around since 1933 and holds a special place in every Taichungese’s heart because of its no-frills tasty food. There are only three items on the menu – the meatball, fish ball soup and glass noodle soup. The meatball is something of a misnomer as it’s closer to a big translucent dumpling with peppery ground pork filling topped with thick soy and sweet sauces.

Name: Küisine
Address: 1, Lane 24, Mofan Street, West District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The unpretentious Küisine emphasises home-like cosiness and intimacy. It’s tucked away in a residential alley and the room feels serene and relaxing. Apart from Taiwanese classics such as plum chicken, and braised beef and fried tofu, Southeast Asian and Japanese influences are also evident in curry, shogayaki and miso dishes. Portion sizes are on the small side so that guests can sample more variety.

Name: Apis Grill
Address: 80 Baoyang East Street, Sanmin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted
Description: Tucked away down an alley with no visible signage apart from a triangle, diners are greeted by the awe-inspiring sight of a giant longan wood-fired kiln and rows of charcoal grills behind the counter. The veteran head chef is keen on straight-forward, back-to-basics cooking, in which meat, fish and veggies are grilled over a wood fire. The menu changes every few weeks, but New Zealand venison is a firm fixture. Order the abalone if available.

Name: Cheng Shi
Address: 12, Lane 702, Section 1, Simen Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Originally a hawker stall in a residential neighbourhood, Cheng Shi (‘honest’ in Chinese) took up this space in 2020 to serve health-conscious diners with all-natural egg noodle soup. Their clear broth made with kombu is a lot lighter than versions offered by their competitors and the variety generously topped with clams is especially popular. You can even specify how soft or firm you want your noodles. Expect to wait during peak hours.

Name: Huang Chia Shrimp Roll
Address: 268 Sihe Road, Central West District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Over 60 years old, this eatery has moved four times, but that hasn’t deterred its loyal followers who continue to queue up daily before opening time. Shrimp roll is a classic Taiwanese snack and a must-try for all visitors. Huang Chia’s version is stuffed with shrimp and cabbage and is dipped in a potato starch batter before being deep-fried to order, resulting in a fluffy airy crust, with thinly sliced radish on the side for contrast.

Name: Xie Shopkeeper
Address: 5, Lane 23, Yunhe Road, Anping District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This restaurant is a relative newcomer in this city swamped by century-old stalls, but it has made a name for itself since 2018 thanks to fresh seafood cooked to order. Its renowned milkfish and assorted seafood congee (more like soupy rice) is lavishly topped with fish skin, fish balls, fish meat, shrimps, clams and cuttlefish, imparting deep seafood umami. Steamed seafood in salt is also popular – try steamed giant grouper for its gelatinous texture.

Name: Chao Ming
Address: 53 Zihciang 1st Road, Cianjin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Now helmed by the second generation of the family, this well-known landmark of Taiwanese home-style cooking has been in business for over 60 years. Masterful control of heat and a dexterous use of sauces depict the food, most of which comes in three portion sizes. Hallmark dishes include stir-fried pork belly with garlic sprouts and stir-fried clams with mung bean sprouts. Wild-caught marine fish, braised or pan-fried, is also popular.

Name: Liao Chi Migao
Address: 119 Ciaonan Road, Ciaotou District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This no-frills shop near the train station has been famous for their migao, or rice cake, since 1955. Glutinous rice mixed with dried shrimps and shallot is steamed in ceramic ramekins as opposed to bamboo tubes. The rice cake is then turned out onto a serving plate, drizzled with braised pork sauce, topped with pork floss and pickled cucumber. Pair it with the herbal soup known as si shen tang, or pork intestine vermicelli soup as accompaniment.

Name: Mr. Good
Address: 29-8 Wulang Street, West District, Taichung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This simple eatery run by the owner couple opened its doors in 2019. The full-flavoured food is mostly Jiangzhe and Taiwanese in origin, perfect with steamed rice. Signatures include baby Napa cabbage with shiitake mushrooms and crab roe, and braised boneless chicken with taro. As the kitchen is manned by the husband only, allow some time for your food to arrive. Reservations via social media and pre-ordering of dishes are highly recommended.

Name: HUGH dessert dining
Address: 56, Lane 136, Section 3, Chongqing North Road, Datong District, Taipei, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Formerly a private dessert lab open by appointment only, Hugh turned into a sleek, minimalistic restaurant with regular hours in 2021. The 6- to 7- course dessert dining menu includes the best sweets in season, not only exquisitely plated, but also subverting preconceptions. Courses flow elegantly from one to another, presenting a variety of depth and textures. It’s also worth paying extra for the hidden improvised course. Booking is mandatory.

Name: Shian Jeng Shrimp Bawan
Address: 609 Yunong Road, East District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Bawan has been around for over a century in Taiwan – the savoury filling is wrapped in a translucent dough, steamed and served with a sweet-savoury sauce. This shop, opened in 2012, is a relative newcomer, but their smaller version stuffed with spear shrimps and pork shoulder butt have instantly won the hearts of gourmets in Tainan. Try it with a dribble of mustard, or pair it with Sishen soup or shiitake pork soup. Check their media page for closing.

Name: Yuan Zai Hui (Guohua Street)
Address: 99, Section 2, Guohua Street, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Shaved ice is mandatory for anyone spending a summer afternoon in scorching Tainan. But even in winter, shaved ice has its loyal fans. For over 50 years, Ice 8 Bao has been specialising in eight-treasure shaved ice, traditionally with eight toppings. But the owners serve a simplified version allowing customers to choose five toppings out of 10-plus house-made choices. Signature include mini mochi balls, candied taro and tapioca wedges.

Name: Hu Tung Beef
Address: 107, Section 1, Zhongshan Road, Hunei District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Right on the border between Tainan and Kaohsiung, just a stone’s throw from a train station, is this restaurant serving freshly slaughtered beef from Tainan daily. Customers come in droves for evenly marbled, hand-sliced beef to be blanched in a rich beef bone broth. The brisket boasts melting fat and gelatinous sinews, truly a must-try for meat lovers. Make sure you book a table and pre-order your beef. Additional orders are not taken on the spot.

Name: Amei
Address: 98, Section 2, Mincyuan Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: A household name for over 60 years, Amei was remodelled after moving to this spot. Red tablecloths pop amid the wood-rich interior with trophies and historic artefacts. The small menu is big on banquet classics and century-old recipes, combining the natural umami of ingredients with locals’ love of savoury-sweet dishes. Signatures include thick shrimp soup with shredded bamboo shoot and wisps of egg, and the duck casserole slow-cooked for 3 hours.

Name: Bao An Lu Migao
Address: 16 Baoan Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Over 50 years ago, the founder peddled his migao around town on a shoulder pole. Fast forward to the here and now, and his steamed sticky rice topped with braised pork, pork floss, a meatball, sliced cucumber and boiled peanuts attracts a loyal following for its great textures and deep flavours. Other specialities include sishen herbal soup, braised pork rice, e-fu noodles and milkfish skin soup. The sidewalk seating feels authentically local.

Name: Halal Chinese Beef Noodles (Da'an)
Address: 1, Alley 7, Lane 137, Yanji Street, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: For his restaurant with over 60 years of history, the owner insists on using only Taiwanese beef that has never been frozen for the best flavour and texture. The beef stock is simmered all day to develop deep flavours without any greasiness. Apart from their signature braised beef noodle soup, also try fried-to-order flatbread, which is stuffed with stir-fried shredded beef. The beef jerky is also good but is only available in strictly limited quantity.

Name: Mother's Kitchen
Address: 97 Tianmu East Road, Shilin District, Taipei, 111, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Terrace
Description: Décor lifted out of rustic farmhouses circa 1950s and memorabilia from the owner’s hometown provide the backdrop for classic comfort food. Only black pig slaughtered on the same day is used for the meltingly soft, traditional braised pork belly. The sizzling and aromatic three-cup frog is another speciality not to be missed - round it out with lard on steamed rice and marble soda. Bookings are recommended and there’s live music on Saturday nights.

Name: Mai Mien Yen Tsai
Address: 106 Anxi Street, Datong District, Taipei, 103, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This shop on the ground floor of a somewhat dilapidated apartment has over 80 years of history.
