Description: Lovers of regional Mexican food will swoon for this laid-back charmer, which offers full-throttle fare made with quality ingredients. The colorful little building has a strange layout (order at the counter, then pass through the kitchen to dine on the patio), but it still draws a large following—expect to chat with fellow diners hungry for intel on the day’s best dishes.Entrées shift with the seasons, but the preparations are always expert: try the halibut ceviche with house-made chips or the red mole tamales chockablock with chicken and just a touch of masa. The Bohemia beer-battered fish tacos featuring handmade tortillas are a must, as are the addictive poblano-tomatillo nachos verdes. Of course, spice fans can't get enough of the crispy chilaquiles.

Name: Flavors from Afar
Address: 1046 S. Fairfax Ave., Los Angeles, 90019, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: A kitchen on a mission, Flavors from Afar works with refugees, asylum seekers and immigrants to highlight recipes from their native countries. Eritrean, Lebanese, Navajo, Guatemalan, Haitian – the rotation is constant, and the culinary reach of the effort is vast. A recent feature on Indo-Fijian cuisine included a creamy onion and coconut milk stew followed by a finely spiced goat pulao enlivened with cardamom, cloves and star anise. This is authentic homestyle cooking in the best of ways, a spotlight on undiscovered talent and a striking reminder of the many flavors the world has to offer. A portion of proceeds benefit the Tiyya Foundation, which supports immigrants and displaced Indigenous communities.

Name: Bansang
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The name references the traditional style of serving a communal Korean meal, which dates back centuries to the Joseon royal court, but there's nothing remotely old-fashioned or stuffy about a meal here. The cooking is an unapologetically contemporary take on Korean cuisine, readily incorporating ingredients like parmesan cheese and chorizo into the likes of kimchi fried rice or crispy rice cakes, fitting together seamlessly beside more classic offerings like mulhwe, a dish of raw seafood with a chilled fermented chili broth. Appropriately, the tapas-style menu is geared toward shared plates, though a starter of sweet-tangy soy lime glazed fried chicken, boasting a craggy, ultra-crunchy exterior and juicy, tender meat, is so good you'll want to discard any idea of sharing.

Name: Hui Xing Yuan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted
Description: This three-storey building is the brand's first outlet, dating back to 1981. Known for traditional Cantonese food at bargain prices, the restaurant prides itself on meticulous cooking techniques and attention to detail. Their speciality of steamed chicken uses only free-range birds from Qingyuan for their firm, silky flesh and fine, springy skin. The goose intestines blanched in soy sauce are also impeccably made.

Name: Xiang Qun (Longjin East Road)
Address: 853-857 Longjin East Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card
Description: Enduring the test of time and loved by locals since 1988, this operation started out as an ‘ice parlour’ serving cold drinks and light meals. These days the menu features no-frills, home-style fare, including the signature steamed Qingyuan chicken, spring onion chicken, soy-marinated goose and deep-fried pork rolls. The made-to-order swamp eel claypot rice boasts a crispy crust and an oniony aroma. Seafood lovers should ask about the catch of the day.

Name: Huacheng Yuan (Jinsui Road)
Address: 5F, Grand Mercure, 62 Jinsui Road, Zhujiang New Town, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,China UnionPay,Diners Club credit card,Foreign credit cards not accepted,JCB,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Since 2018, Huacheng Yuan has been serving hotel guests and other gourmands with home-style Cantonese fare. The brightly lit space boasts a tasteful décor and there are a number of private rooms of varying sizes. Along with signature dishes such as double-steamed chicken, lotus root starch pancakes, and soy-marinated chitterlings, the milky white, rich and flavoursome slow-cooked pork tripe soup is a must-try. Reservations are recommended.

Name: Xing Fu Yi Zhan
Address: 8 Yulei Third Street, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Furnished like an ancient stage station, this restaurant is a step back in time. Feel free to join the servers and dress up in period costume for a selfie. The Sichuanese head chef feeds hungry patrons with rustic food, including a non-spicy option for most dishes. Braised river perch with pickled cabbage is tangy and appetising. Throw in udon noodles to make a complete meal. Nightly Chinese zither and dance performances add to the atmosphere.

Name: Xin Wen Ji (Yuexiu)
Address: 1-2F, Sino Trade Centre, 67 Panfu Road, Yuexiu, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: The room is divided into zones with different ambiances – satin tablecloths signal a chic, formal vibe, while distressed wooden tables feel hip and casual. The culinary highlight is undoubtedly the piping hot congee claypot loaded with fresh seafood, from sand shrimps to mud crab. You can also pick your own fish from the tank and ask servers the best way to have it cooked. Cantonese stir-fries and sizzling claypot dishes exude exceptional wok hei.

Name: Jia Yuan
Address: 7 Xingrenli, Guangxiao Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This restaurant with wood-rich finishes primarily serves dishes made with soybean products or mushrooms – no dairy, eggs, garlic or onion are used. Sweet and sour monkey head mushrooms and vegan meat with pickled cabbage are both tangy creations with layers of textures. The house-made mugwort-scented dumplings and plant-based yoghurt are also popular. Reservations recommended on the 1st and 15th day of every lunar month, when Buddhists go meat-free.

Name: Mamak
Address: Shop 082C, East 1 Street, B1F, Fashion Tianhe Plaza, 299 Tianhe Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted
Description: Named after hawker stalls in Malaysia, this small and cheerful spot in a big shopping mall is boldly decorated with bright yellow hues and Malaysian flags everywhere. Naturally, the menu is loaded with the country’s national dishes, such as laksa (seafood noodle soup) and nasi lemak (coconut rice) served with juicy fried chicken and house-made sambal. For drinks, try teh C special (three-layer milk tea) or teh tarik (hand-pulled tea).

Name: Xiguan Zhuyuan (Lizhiwan)
Address: C4, Phase 2, Lizhiwan Scenic Area, Huangsha Avenue, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: Not only is this a noodle shop – nestled in a picturesque park – but it’s also a factory that makes noodles for various restaurants in Guangzhou and Hong Kong. These famous strands made with duck eggs are dried on bamboo skimmers outside the shop. Dried plaice is toasted on charcoal before being added to the flavourful broth along with pork backbones and dried shrimp. Customers who wish to enjoy the same taste at home can buy their pre-packed noodles.

Name: Liang Jie Nanning Pumiao Shengzha Mifen
Address: 242 Yinghua Street, Xiaogang Bay, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This friendly neighbourhood shop specialises in sourdough rice noodles. While preserving her hometown culinary tradition, the owner also dials down the sourness to cater to local tastes. Noodles are made to order – fermented rice batter is squeezed into boiling water and then drenched in soup, or tossed with pickled string beans, ground pork and deep-fried tofu. You can also opt for the beef brisket version. Prepare to wait after placing orders.

Name: Pandan
Address: Shop B5, 4F, China Plaza, 33 Zhongshan Third Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Rest assured the food served here is authentic as the head chef and most of the kitchen team are Indonesian. In fact, all of the spices are also flown in from their home country. Grilled chicken satay delivers morsels of juicy meat with sweet peanut sauce on the side. Tender and succulent Rendang beef is braised in a spiced curry laced with coconut milk for extra aroma. Indonesian handicrafts in the dining room are an added pleasure to behold.

Name: Wen Ji Yixinji
Address: 10 Xuanyuanqiao, 76 Baohua Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card
Description: This joint expanded in 2020, adding a new dining room across from the original shop. Its signature Yixin chicken remains the key draw – juicy, silky flesh, springy skin and flavoursome down to the bone. Both the founder and kitchen team used to work for the now-defunct Qingping Restaurant, and the namesake bird is derived from the legendary Qingping chicken dish. To top it off, try their braised pork ribs with red dates, or chicken feet and lotus root soup.

Name: Stay Here
Address: Shop 2, 23 Xigang Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card
Description: After undergoing a renovation, there are only three tables left in this space. Diners may book one via an app, paying the deposit, and pre-ordering their food. The owner-chefs may also cater to special requests. This menu changes monthly and the same authentic Chaoshan cuisine is served both at lunch and dinner. Marinated raw blood clams pack tons of oomph, umami and should not be missed. Also try their homemade chrysanthemum wine and fruit-and-floral wine.

Name: Ease (Yuexiu)
Address: 112A, 289 Art Park, 289 Guangzhou Middle Avenue, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Nestled in a printing plant-turned-cultural park, the two-storey restaurant boasts an airy, high-ceilinged dining room. Faux-industrial elements work well with wood and bamboo accents for a relaxed ambience. The menu features simple dishes with Sichuanese touches, such as the must-try poached fish with peppercorns on the vine – layered flavours contrast nicely with the velvety fish. Friendly service and sensible prices are also reasons to visit.

Name: Enning Liu Fu Ji (Donghua East Road)
Address: 547 Donghua East Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The founder started a shop on Enning Street in the 1940s and invented a unique way to make noodles. Fast forward to present day and his successors still honour his heritage by making bouncy noodles just like the old days – with duck eggs and flour only. The must-try blanched noodles tossed in lard is simple but addictive. The shrimp wontons are big and bursting with seafood flavours. Don’t miss their deep-fried wontons, available on weekends only.

Name: Hai Xian Jie Cai Guan
Address: 152-2 Haizhu South Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Nestled in an old neighbourhood, this shop has kept regulars coming back for almost three decades with their no-frills, tasty food at frugal prices. Come early for their double-boiled soups which tend to run out early. Fish head soup particularly entices with succulent flesh and a hint of Chinese herbs; brace yourself for the heady aromas when you lift the paper lid. Steamed chicken, roast goose and steamed pork patties are also popular choices.

Name: Ze 8
Address: 174 Binjiang West Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Despite the Song Dynasty-inspired décor and faux-antique stoneware, this place feels young and trendy. On its menu are about 30 dishes served in sizzling claypots complemented by an array of homemade sauces. Out of respect for Cantonese classics, the owner avoids food combinations that are overly fancy. The claypots with wider bottoms are tailor-made in Guangxi province to offer more surface area, thereby preventing the food from burning.

Name: Lao Xiguan Laifen (Wenming Road)
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: As its name suggests, Laifen noodle soup is the key item on offer in this rustic shop – you can have it alongside ingredients, such as barbecue pork, beef balls or octopus. The old-time dish ‘water caltrop’, which is rice noodles shaped like bite-size buffalo nuts topped with shredded omelette, preserved cabbage and barbecue pork, is hard to find elsewhere. Also try homemade preserved radish.

Name: Chuang Fa
Address: 512-2 Guangfu North Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Diners Club credit card,Foreign credit cards not accepted,JCB,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Since opening in the 1990s, this has been a popular place among locals who can’t seem to get enough of the kitchen's Cantonese home-style cooking, especially the double-boiled tonic soups. The signature “real-taste” chicken is free-range from Shunyi and is prized for its firm, flavoursome meat and silky, gelatinous skin. Large fried pork intestines with basil, and live seafood cooked-to-order are also excellent. Reservations recommended.

Name: Cheungloi Cook (Huacheng Avenue)
Address: Shop 420-421, 4F, G.T. Land Plaza Spring, 85 Huacheng Avenue, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Diners Club credit card,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: After moving to this location, the interior was updated with tables on a terrace. The menu is smaller, but prices remain approachable. The signature “rolling” goose is fried over low heat before being braised in a spiced sauce. It is flipped continuously throughout the process, and fried once more prior to plating. Pork intestines braised in soy also stand out. Only reservations before 12 pm and 6:30 pm are accepted for lunch and dinner respectively.

Name: Dayang (Wenming Road)
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Among locals, its name is synonymous with double-boiled soups, which dominate the menu here. Apart from the top-selling silkie chicken soup in whole coconut, other popular selections, such as free-range chicken soup with goji berries and yam as well as quail soup are trickier to order as they change every few hours. That means you'll never quite know what exactly is available in advance. Adventurous eaters may also try the turtle jelly with milk and honey.

Name: FT · Bak Kut Teh
Address: Wonderful Life Mansion, 36-48 Wenming Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: You can’t miss the long line at the door, but that doesn’t stop avid chowhounds from coming here. The signature bak kut teh is simmered for three hours with pork ribs, garlic, white peppercorns and herbs until the meat falls off the bones. Char-grilled skate in sambal, seafood laksa and grilled durian also stand out. Reservations are not accepted. Join the queue on the mobile app ahead of time; or walk in and expect to wait for up to three hours.

Name: Yao Ji
Address: 15 Long Yuan Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Yao Ji has been a household name in Panyu District for over 40 years. On the menu, classic Cantonese flavours work their magic in painstaking recipes that are a rarity these days. The sweet, steamed lotus root puree is sticky and chewy and well complemented by briny dried shrimps and aromatic scallion. Oyster sauce chicken is nicely browned and boasts an inimitable umami flavour thanks to scallion and ginger.

Name: Hunan Cuisine
Address: 2842-39 East Xingang Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card
Description: This design-forward restaurant is located within an industrial park of remodelled factory buildings. Aptly, the décor exudes an industrial chic that complements the origami art hung from the ceiling. Trained as a designer, the owner took care of the décor and furnishings, whereas the Hunanese chef recreates classics from his home province. Dongting fish head, wotou cornbread and sweet fried dumplings are cooked with acumen and dexterity.

Name: Temple Street
Address: 10 Dongdi Second Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Since opening in 2018, this tiny shop has been jam-packed with diners, so expect to share a table with strangers at peak hours. It’s named after Temple Street in the owner’s native Hong Kong and focuses on 20+ types of clay pot rice in dai pai dong style, alongside three kinds of double-boiled soups. Try their claypot rice topped with assorted traditional preserved meats, beef loin with perilla leaves or satay beef with onion.

Name: Zijin Shi Fang
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Though Zijin occupies two adjoining ground-floor units, there is barely an empty seat throughout the day. For over 10 years, locals have been fans of the impeccable barbecue meats, which are displayed in all their glory at the front of the shop. The signature goose braised in premium soy boasts velvety meat and deep flavours. Double-boiled soups, stir-fries and claypot dishes are also popular. Come early, as certain items tend to run out.

Name: Lingnan Haiyanlou (Binjiang East Road)
Address: 2-3F, Jiangpan Huating, 1040 Binjiang East Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: The two chefs in this kitchen once worked at a prestigious hotel and their skills are unquestionable – which is why it’s so hard to get a table here. Try their ‘premium trio’ which was usually saved for state banquets only – rich and buttery foie gras, plum-scented squab with crispy skin, as well as springy goose webs and wings in white marinade. Barbecued meat is grilled daily in limited servings. Arrive early to nab a seat or risk disappointment.

Name: Hai Men Yu Zi Dian (Yanling Road)
Address: Jinyan Mansion, 120 Yanling Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Next to a glass-walled kitchen where a veritable army of chefs may be seen at work, this high-ceilinged bi-level dining room was remodelled to have entrances on both ends, thereby making it feel even more comfortable than before. It’s essentially an up-market hawker stall experience in an air-conditioned space. Diners pick their food at the entrance, where fresh seafood delivered daily from Swatow is laid out neatly on ice. First-timers may also refer to the menu for recommendations.

Name: Wei Shi Jia
Address: 598 Jiefang North Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Shi shi chicken – steamed chicken served with fermented clam dip – ranks among the top 10 chicken dishes in Guangzhou, but it’s hard to come by these days. The chef, who once worked in a prestigious hotel, uses Qingyuan birds for this dish because of their bouncy skin and silky flesh. Besides the clam dip, it comes with soy sauce and ginger scallion dip. Also try the rice noodles made from scratch in-house and dressed in a secret soy blend.

Name: Tong Ji
Address: 3 Fuguangli, Changshou East Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Tucked away in an alley, this two-storey, no-frills joint has been in business for over 30 years. You're not here for the ambience, but for the steamed chicken – only free-range pullets before they lay their first egg are used because of their springy skin, oily richness, silky flesh and robust flavour. Boiled chicken intestines, stir-fried ribbon rice noodles and creamy congee are also sound reasons to visit.

Name: Xiguan Zhuyuan (Shiba Fu)
Address: 107 Shiba Fu South Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: It lacks the views of its Lizhiwan counterpart, but the food here tastes just as good. Duck egg noodles are kneaded with a traditional bamboo pole for a springy texture, before being blanched and tossed in shrimp roe, or in a broth made with dried plaice, pork bones and dried shrimp. Apart from the classic shrimp wonton, there is also the crab roe variety. Don’t miss the beef offal soup, fried savoury dough, beef brisket and pork intestines.

Name: Rong Yi Fa Niu Za Dian (Shishu Road)
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: For over 40 years, the owner has been insisting on shopping for fresh beef offal daily, painstakingly preparing and braising it in a rich stock made from scratch with beef and lamb bones. His beef bone marrow boasts a creamy texture and is a perfect match with the house-made radish pickles. Beef tripe tip is another premium cut, available only after 11am. As well as beef offal, also try wonton noodle soup, braised beef brisket and tendon.

Name: Dai Yong Town
Address: 59 Tianhe East Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: It’s hard to miss the back-lit illustrations on the ceiling of this clean and cosy dining room. The menu pays homage to the kaleidoscopic Chao Zhou food culture: marinated raw crabs burst with umami and winey aromas, while deep-fried Bombay duck in peppered salt literally melts in your mouth. Classics such as marinated meats, and stir-fried pork tripe with salted mustard greens also stand out. But, be sure to pre-order the chilled steamed fish.

Name: Nan Yuan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: This is a long-standing institution that boasts a classical landscaped garden complete with pavilions, bridges and water features. Dining rooms are adorned with colourful Manchurian windows that frame the views nicely. The food is mostly Cantonese, with occasional offerings from other provinces. The charge depends on the grade of the room you dine in. If you want more comfort, privacy, and are willing to pay more, talk to the front desk.

Name: Da Ge Fan (Tangxiayong West Road)
Address: 1F, Tian Hui Building, 69 Tangxiayong West Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Now boasting many branches in Hunan and Guangdong provinces, Da Ge Fan started right here from not-so-humble beginnings – this flagship founded in 2013 has enough acreage to incorporate a landscaped garden with a stream running through. The namesake signature dish is rice cooked in pigeon- and pork bone-broth topped with steamed pigeon. Of course, the salt-baked and deep-fried pigeons are must-tries. All fowl offered are 22-days-old and slaughtered on the day.

Name: Xin Tai Le (Yuexiu)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Since 1989, this household name for its signature swamp eel rice has attracted a loyal fan base. Of all the branches, this two-storey one in the old part of town is the flagship. Apart from its famous rice dish topped with crisp, flavourful eel that imparts a robust wok-qi, the kitchen also recommends fatty roast char siu, all sorts of stir-fries and seafood dishes. Private rooms of varying sizes are available on the second floor.

Name: Hua Ge Si Chu
Address: 443 Guangfu North Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The owner was behind a legendary, now-shuttered restaurant and opened this much smaller spot, keeping some of the menu’s most popular items. The chef has decades of experience and his Hakkanese cooking is a pure delight. The signature salt-baked chicken uses birds from Qingyuan, dry-rubbed in a droolworthy secret seasoning blend. House-made pickles, and winter special, white radish pork balls, are also recommended.

Name: Jian Ji (Liwan)
Address: 299-303 Changshou East Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Shops that sell homemade E-fu noodles can be hard to come by. For over 50 years, this one has attracted a faithful following with not only E-fu, but also freshly made raw and cooked egg noodles. The ladies working in the open kitchen show off their swift moves as these particular strands are notorious for their finicky cooking process. The flavourful broth made with dace, pork bones, shrimp roe and dried shrimp matches the noodles perfectly.

Name: Ya Yuan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: The three-storey room is furnished with orange tables and leather chairs that evoke 1980s nostalgia. For over three decades, Ya Yuan has been feeding hungry locals with classic home-style dishes such as slow-boiled soups and claypot rice. With its velvety flesh and gelatinous skin, the poached Qingyuan chicken dressed in scallion oil is addictively aromatic. Even the post-meal complimentary mung bean or red bean sweet soups are made with care.

Name: Soodle
Address: Shop 309, 3F, Adjoining Building, Kingold Century, 62 Jinsui Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Valet parking,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: This stylish vegetarian restaurant caters to a well-heeled business clientele and commands spectacular city views. The menu is Western-centric, focused on fresh vegetables and fruits, as opposed to Chinese vegetarian cuisine that is based heavily on soy products. The signature 200-gram oyster mushroom steak with basil black pepper sauce or brine sauce appeals thanks to its crispy texture and vibrant flavours. Also try their black truffle, porcini and peach resin.

Name: Zhu Zai Ji Shi Fu (Jiangnan Avenue)
Address: 429 Jiangnan Avenue South, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: A hawker-stall-turned-restaurant now with two branches – this casual and bustling three-storey joint is prized for its authentic Cantonese food. The juicy and flavoursome roast goose is a big hit among diners for the past 20 years. Other specialities include salted pork trotters; Zhu Ji steamed chicken; and blackened barbecue pork.

Name: Xin Tai Le (Haizhu)
Address: 2-4F, 93-99 Jiangnan West Road, Guangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This is not just a restaurant, but a gastronomical institution known for its signature eel dishes. Though this three-storey branch is not the original, it has been serving the neighbourhood for over a decade. Swamp eel rice is cooked in eel soup and topped with eel juices and oil. Swamp eel casserole boasts chunks of fresh fish that are springy and tender, coated in a self-made sauce. Their fatty char siu is also worth trying.

Name: Sa Er Ta Dongxiang Shou Zhua
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Tucked in an alley filled to the brim with halal restaurants, this two-storey establishment has a dining room on the ground floor and five private rooms upstairs. Lamb is big on the menu, such as the juicy boiled premium version, which is chopped into chunky pieces with skin on and bone in. Pair it with garlic for extra pungency. Heyan flat noodles and Dongxiang stir-fried chicken are also worth savouring. For drinks, the eight-treasure tea is a must.

Name: Kotuwa
Address: Wanderlust Hotel, Level 1, 2 Dickson Road, 209494, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: This Sri Lankan restaurant specialises in seafood dishes from Colombo, especially crab prepared in myriad ways. With its balanced, layered flavours and the subtle warmth of cinnamon, the crab curry really stands out. Hoppers – crispy pancakes made with fermented rice – are perfect for mopping up the delicious curry sauce. Pair your food with a cocktail infused with fruit, herbs or Sri Lankan spirits, and named after Sri Lankan mythical creatures.

Name: Du Du Shou Shi
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-19, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This stall carries two varieties of tu tu kueh – coconut and peanut. The steamed rice cake is chewy and springy on the outside; both fillings are nutty, sweet and aromatic. Best enjoyed piping hot!

Name: Tai Seng Fish Soup
Address: Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre, #03-145, 3 Yung Sheng Road, Jurong West, 618499, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This third-generation family business prides itself on its flavoursome fish soup made from scratch and served with sliced fish, deep-fried fish or fish head. Order noodles, rice or congee on the side for a complete meal.

Name: Spinach Soup
Address: Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre, #01-12, 69 Geylang Bahru, 330069, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This is the place to come for a comforting bowl of soup. The broth is flavourful and sweet; the spinach is crisp and fresh. You can also order stuffed tofu or seafood on top, or add mee tai mak for some starchiness.

Name: Soh Kee Cooked Food
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-44, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Serves porridge with chicken, fish or cuttlefish. Sets for one to three people are also available.

Name: Outram Park Fried Kway Teow Mee
Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #02-17, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: The Kway Teow is fried with a dark sauce you can add cockles to the noodles. Always a long queue.

Name: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice
Address: Maxwell Food Centre, #01-10/11, 1 Kadayanallur Street, 069184, Singapore
Description: Don't be surprised to see a long queue - their Hainanese chicken rice is hugely popular.

Name: Tai Wah Pork Noodle
Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #02-16, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: Noodles served with soup meat balls, dried fish and pork liver.

Name: Hoo Kee Bak Chang
Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #01-18, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: Glutinous rice mixed with salted duck egg yolk pork and chestnut wrapped with bamboo leaf.

Name: Ar Er Soup
Address: ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, #01-141, Blk 6 Jalan Bukit Merah, 150006, Singapore
Description: Offers 8 kinds of MSG-free long-boiled soups, served with pumpkin rice.

Name: Sin Huat Eating House
Description: Rice noodles with crab and fishcakes are the signature dishes.

Name: Chuan Kee Boneless Braised Duck
Address: 20 Ghim Moh Road Market & Food Centre, #01-04, Blk 20, Ghim Moh Road, 270020, Singapore
Description: Juicy and flavoursome braised duck is served with rice, congee, kway teow or noodles, plus optional extras such as duck gizzard, duck liver or marinated egg. The "set" comes with a bowl of bak kut teh.

Name: Un-Yang-Kor-Dai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Though its name means ‘anything goes’, this restaurant is exceptionally specific about the food it serves – Isan cuisine hailing from north-eastern Thailand and famous for its infernal heat. The PenLaos signature chicken is marinated with white peppercorns and coriander for three days before being grilled to perfection. Leng zaab is pork ribs in a spicy sour broth that is simply addictive. Ask for the house-made Isan tamarind dip to dunk the pork in.

Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Address: 115 Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre, #01-51, Blk 115 Bukit Merah View, 151115, Singapore
Description: This spot has mastered the art of cooking mutton, with dishes like mutton soup, mutton meatballs and mutton offal.

Name: Hong Kong Yummy Soup
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-51, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: Offers six kinds of soups, like lotus root pork ribs & winter melon pork ribs. Also try steamed pork patty with pumpkin or steamed spare ribs.

Name: Bahrakath Mutton Soup
Address: Adam Food Centre, #01-10, 2 Adam Road, 289876, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted
Description: Since 1973, this stall has been serving its secret mutton soup recipe. The broth is rich, dense, and full of herbal flavours. Apart from the popular leg, also try other lamb cuts. Order bread to mop up the broth.

Name: The Coconut Club
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This whitewashed traditional shophouse evokes unmistakably tropical vibes – wicker back chairs, wallpaper with banana leaf prints and cheerful blue-and-white tiled flooring. On the menu, the coconut theme is also obvious – the nasi lemak set is the best seller, but other dishes deserve equal attention too, such as ayam goreng berempah (spiced fried chicken with crispy rempah crumbs), and sago pudding with pandan, palm sugar and coconut cream.

Name: Kwee Heng
Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-13, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: With over 40 years of history, Kwee Heng makes boneless braised duck that is tender, juicy and flavoursome; it can be served with rice, congee or noodles. Other dishes such as Hainanese chicken and char siew are also available.

Name: Heng
Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-28, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: The owner has 50+ years-experience serving sweet and savoury carrot cakes. Fried oysters and oyster omelettes are also worth a try.

Name: Fool
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This lively wine bar concept is another brainchild of the chef-owner behind Cloudstreet and Kotuwa. The décor is on trend with a retro 1970s look. The wine list is extensive and well-choreographed, with a slight bias towards older vintages. Pair your wine with snacks and small plates hallmarked by precise execution, beguiling presentations and pronounced flavours. In particular, the chicken liver éclair with date and Madeira is not to be missed.

Name: Yhingthai Palace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: Founded in the ’90s by a couple passionate about Thai cuisine, this restaurant is spread over three colourful rooms decorated with Thai artefacts. Added authenticity comes courtesy of the helpful waitresses in their delightful traditional dress. The Thai and Thai-Chinese dishes are prepared with fresh ingredients that are sourced on a daily basis, with choices like Thai Otah. Prices are reasonable, both for this neighbourhood and for the quality of the food.

Name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (New Bridge Road)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Much has changed since Mr Yeo started selling bak kut teh from his pushcart in Johor Road back in the late ’60s – nowadays it’s the second generation of the family who are running the show. They are still selling their celebrated pork ribs and peppery broth but are now doing so from 10+ shops – and this one, the simplest, seems to be the best. Queue, order, pay, and then tuck into your soup – when you’ve finished they’ll top it up for you.

Name: Eminent Frog Porridge & Seafood (Lor 19)
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: It serves cze char dishes like kung pao frog, sweet and sour pork and fried crab with pepper.

Name: Heng Kee
Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #01-58, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This stall, founded in the 1970s, is now run by the second-generation owner. Its hallmark dishes are mild, well-balanced curry broth, custom-made tofu puffs and fish cakes, as well as generous helpings of velvety chicken.

Name: Lian He Ben Ji Claypot
Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-198/199, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: It takes 30 minutes to cook but is more than worth the wait. The rice, cooked in a claypot over charcoal, exudes smokiness with a crispy scorched crust on the bottom. For toppings, choose between chicken, preserved pork and/or sausage.

Name: Heng Heng Cooked Food
Address: Yuhua Village Market and Food Centre, #01-12, Blk 254, Jurong East Street 24, 600254, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Both the laksa and prawn mee are made to order and come in three sizes. Their hallmark laksa is doused in a rich aromatic broth and topped with prawns, fried fish cake, fried tofu and cockles.

Name: Nam Sing Hokkien Fried Mee
Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-32, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This stall has been serving just one item since opening its doors in 1960 – Hokkien fried mee with prawns. The egg noodles and rice vermicelli are tossed in a rich broth made with prawn shells and tomalley to impart deep umami.

Name: Soon Huat
Address: North Bridge Road Market & Food Centre, #01-105, 861 North Bridge Road, 198783, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Choose between "dry" and soup noodles topped with butterflied prawns, fish cake, bean sprouts and fried garlic. The flavoursome prawn soup on the side is also a treat. Not a fan of prawns? Try the pork ribs noodles instead.

Name: Hui Wei Chilli Ban Mian
Address: Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre, #01-58, 69 Geylang Bahru, 330069, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Ribbon noodles made in the stall are served in soup or "dry" – tossed in home-made chilli sauce and topped with minced meat, meatballs, poached egg and fried lard. You can also opt for e-fu or ramen noodles instead.

Name: Selamat Datang Warong Pak Sapari
Address: Adam Food Centre, #01-09 , 2 Adam Road, 289876, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Into the third generation, this family business is famous for mee soto and mee rebus, the former served in broth, the latter in a thicker gravy soup. Bold flavours are authentically Malaysian; add more coriander for extra fragrance.

Name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
Address: Adam Food Centre, #01-27, 2 Adam Road, 289876, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The prawn mee cooked à la minute is a recipe from the owner’s father. Opt for “dry” noodles tossed in prawn paste of your desired level of heat, alongside a bowl of prawn soup. Toppings like pig skin add contrasting textures.

Name: Shi Hui Yuan
Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-33, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: Thin, smooth rice noodles and gravy - with chicken, duck or chicken feet toppings.

Name: Zhi Wei Xian Zion Road Big Prawn Noodle
Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #04, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: The soup has a rich prawn flavour. Fresh prawns, chili and pork rinds combine to make a great bowl of noodles.

Name: No.18 Zion Road Fried Kway Teow
Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #017, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: Kway teow noodles are fried to order and topped with fish cake and cockles. The wok hei impresses with its robust flavours and a hint of spiciness, while the cockles impart extra umami. The wait can be long, but is well worth it.

Name: Zai Shun Curry Fish Head
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The fish head curry boasts velvety flesh loaded with umami and is hot and spicy, perfect with steamed rice. Besides its eponymous dish, other equally stunning fish dishes and stir-fries are also available.

Name: Da Shi Jia Big Prawn Mee
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Guests are spoiled for choices here. First, pick between prawn noodle soup and fried prawn bee hoon. For prawn mee, specify the size of these wild-caught marine crustaceans – from regular to XXL. Then pick your noodles –the yellow variety, kway teow, bee hoon, or any combination of those. For real big eaters, choose extra toppings of fish cake, pork ribs or sliced pork. Don’t forget about snacks like tofu skin prawn rolls and fried prawn balls on the side.

Name: Hai Nan Zai
Address: Chong Pang Market and Food Centre, #01-129, 105 Yishun Ring Road, 760105, Singapore
Description: Singaporean food such as oyster omelettes, fried prawn mee and carrot cakes. Fried kway teow with cockles and Chinese sausage are cooked-to-order.

Name: Chen's Mapo Tofu (Shenton Way)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: This is the more affordable fast-food version of Shisen Hanten, managed by the same chef. The famous namesake dish is reincarnated as mapo don, literally mapo tofu on a bowl of Japanese rice. It’s more numbing than spicy, with silky tofu and ground pork. Dan dan mien is another favourite, with the choice between soup and dressed noodles. Szechwan popcorn chicken with a crispy crust and juicy centre packs serious oomph and is also worth trying.

Name: Whole Earth
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: “Vegetarian cuisine for non-vegetarians” is how Phyllis and Wood describe their longstanding Thai and Peranakan restaurant. They wanted diners to feel they were eating meat even though they weren’t and this they achieve through an understanding of textures and flavours and the clever use of soy product and tofu. With dishes like tom yam soup and classic assam pedas, the food is full of flavour as well as being good for you – and it’s great value too.

Name: Hawker Chan Soya Sauce Chicken Rice & Noodle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: What started at a stall in Chinatown Food Centre lead inevitably to Chef Chan going into partnership and opening a restaurant. Equally inevitable is the size of the queue – it forms well before opening time, such is the reputation of his delicious soy sauce chicken rice and roast pork. The new premises may provide more space and seating but, just like back at the hawker centre, you’ll be sharing your table with others.

Name: Guan Kee Fried Kway Teow
Address: 20 Ghim Moh Road Market & Food Centre, #01-19, Blk 20, Ghim Moh Road, 270020, Singapore
Description: Serves only made-to-order fried Kway Teow. Sufficient ingredients such as cockles, fishcakes and Chinese sausages make the robust flavour.

Name: Joo Siah Bak Koot Teh
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The signature dish here is pepper-flavoured bak kut teh. The soft pork rib goes well with chilli soy sauce. Earlier closing hours on Sunday.

Name: One Prawn & Co
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The constant queue under the red awning is a sign that this shop serves good hae mee. The signature prawn noodles come in a set: a bowl of noodles alongside rich prawn soup in a claypot. There are four noodles to choose from, but the classic order is yellow noodles with thin bee hoon. The soup is loaded with flavours, especially from the tomalley of countless prawn heads. Also try their ngoh hiang – the crispy prawn cracker is too good to miss.

Name: Kelantan Kway Chap · Pig Organ Soup
Address: Berseh Food Centre, #02-39, 166 Jalan Besar, 208877, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Pork cuts and offal like belly, trotter, intestines and skin are cooked in a soy-based marinade with spices. The depth and rich flavours of the meat are the perfect accompaniment to the kway chap ribbon noodles.

Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-01, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Cooked-to-order, the noodles stir-fried with sliced fish, squid and prawn and served with homemade chilli sauce is a favourite.

Name: Yong Chun Wan Ton Noodle
Address: 115 Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre, #01-56, Blk 115 Bukit Merah View, 151115, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The owner has his springy eggy noodles tailor-made. They are best enjoyed in its “dry” form – blanched and dressed in a savoury sweet sauce. Wonton with minced pork is fresh and firm.

Name: True Blue Cuisine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: It’s less like walking into a restaurant, more like falling into the warm embrace of a much loved family member. Here it’s about nostalgia and paying homage to the food, history and customs of the Peranakans – you’ll find all the classic dishes, prepared in an authentic way, and the hard part is narrowing down your choice. The setting really is unique and on the way out it’s hard to resist buying a keepsake from the True Blue Shoppe.

Name: Kok Sen
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: In business for over 50 years, Kok Sen moved to another spot on the same street in 2022. Seats may be a bit cramped, but the new space has a nice feel to it. Round tables and green booth seats work well with a grey colour scheme and pale wood. Signature cze char classics are listed in colourful lightboxes – the prawn paste chicken is simply not to be missed; fish cooked in various ways is also popular. Seasonal dishes may need to be pre-ordered.

Name: Fei Fei Roasted • Noodle
Address: Yuhua Village Market and Food Centre, #01-28, Blk 254, Jurong East Street 24, 600254, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Popular stall for roasted meat and dumplings. Duck leg with shrimp wonton noodles is recommended. Come early before the food runs out.

Name: Anglo Indian (Shenton Way)
FacilitiesAndServices: Brunch,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: If there’s one dish that customers should expect to find in a restaurant called Anglo Indian it’s chicken tikka masala – and sure enough it’s a firm favourite of many here at this simply decorated spot in the heart of the CBD. The dining room may seat only 20, but there’s a large outdoor terrace where everyone congregates for the well-priced cooking. Other popular choices include butter chicken and mutton dum biryani.

Name: Cheok Kee
Address: Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre, #01-35, 69 Geylang Bahru, 330069, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Its famous soy-marinated duck boasts velvety flesh on a bed of steamed rice perfumed by duck scents. It comes with chilli vinegar that aptly cuts through the richness, plus an aromatic duck soup made with Chinese herbs.

Name: Singapore Fried Hokkien Mee
Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-32, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 91, 320091, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted
Description: Their famous Hokkien mee is made with rice vermicelli and yellow egg noodles, which are topped with prawns and squid for that umami flavour – even better with a helping of spicy homemade chilli sauce.

Name: Lai Heng Handmade Teochew Kueh
Address: Yuhua Market & Hawker Centre, #01-218, Blk 347, Jurong East Avenue 1, Jurong East, 600347, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted
Description: Handmade Teochew kueh with various flavours. Steamed or pan-fried versions available.

Name: Jian Bo Tiong Bahru Shui Kueh
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-27, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The rice cake with a sauce of preserved vegetables, sesame, dried shrimp and chilli is spicy and delicious.

Name: Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge
Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-20, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Fish porridge and fried fish bee hoon. The porridge is sweet with abundant fish fillets.

Name: Na Na Curry
Address: 115 Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre, #01-47, Blk 115 Bukit Merah View, 151115, Singapore
Description: The fish head curry with eggplant, okra and tofu puff stands out with its aromatic spice paste made from scratch, paired with a hint of coconut milk. The fish, lamb and chicken curry are also popular.

Name: Alliance Seafood
Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-27, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: BBQ seafood such as tiger prawn and cereal prawn. Don't miss the chilli crab or the black pepper crab made using the live crustacean.

Name: Ji De Lai Hainanese Chicken Rice
Address: Chong Pang Market and Food Centre, #01-152, 105 Yishun Ring Road, 760105, Singapore
Description: Hainanese chicken rice comes with options like roasted or steamed chicken. Sets with rice, soup and vegetables are reasonably priced.

Name: J2 Famous Crispy Curry Puff
Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #01-21, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: Curry puff is a hugely popular street food – curry chicken filling with potato, wrapped in a flaky, crispy pastry crust. The sweet taro filling and the chilli sardine versions are also recommended.

Name: The Blue Ginger (Tanjong Pagar)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This is one of the most popular little gems in Chinatown and it’s easy to see why. The narrow house offers dining on three floors; art by local artists add colour and character. In business for over 20 years, regulars keep returning for its aromatic cooking like Ngo Heong that delivers all the subtle and authentic flavours of Peranakan, as well as addictive sweets like Chendol. Better still, prices are as generous as the portions—that are great for sharing.

Name: Bismillah Biryani
Description: Biryani with fish or meat and flavoured with various Indian herbs.

Name: Sik Bao Sin (Desmond's Creation)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The second-generation owner-chef makes every dish according to traditional recipes for guaranteed authenticity. The concise menu only features 13 items, but seasonal dishes, not on the menu, are also available. The chef’s signature dish, sweet and sour pork, is made to order, so expect to wait. The ginger chicken is simply divine – tender chicken glazed in a mild chilli sauce alongside zesty pickled ginger shoots. Also, try the kale with prawns.

Name: Fu Ming Cooked Food
Description: Homemade black and white carrot cake is served. The black one with dark soya sauce is crispy and tasty.

Name: Muthu's Curry
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: ‘Muthu’ means pearl in Tamil, which befits this gem (with another branche) serving traditional dishes from both the Southern and Northern regions of India. Originally called Muthu Makkan, the owner expanded and renamed the restaurant in 1982. The signature fish head, South Indian-style, uses a secret blend of spices. Swimmer crabs, masala prawns, lamb rack and tandoori chicken are also big hits among diners. Ask about the monthly specials.

Name: New Lucky Claypot Rice
Address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-19, 44 Holland Drive, 270044, Singapore
Description: Cooked-to-order claypot rice. While waiting, try their long-boiled soups.

Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-46, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 91, 320091, Singapore
Description: The sliced fish bee hoon (rice vermicelli) comes in a flavourful, milky fish stock, with fried garlic bits for extra fragrance and crunch. Also worth trying are the tom yam soup, seafood soup and fried fish head bee hoon.

Name: A Noodle Story
Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #01-39, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: The stall has an interesting look and sells local, traditional noodles cooked in an innovative way.

Name: Hai Nan Xing Zhou Beef Noodle
Address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-06, 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, 310022, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Choose between blanched rice noodles tossed in a thick gravy, or soup noodles in a deeply flavourful ox bone broth. Then top with sliced beef, beef tripe, tendon, beef balls, or a combination.

Name: Sing Lung HK Cheong Fun
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The chef has years of experience in Cantonese cooking and his velvety Hong Kong-style rice noodle rolls are made to order. Come early for the century egg and pork congee or glutinous rice, as they tend to run out early.

Name: Koh Brother Pig's Organ Soup
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-29, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Provides a wide range of pork offal like liver, chitterlings and tripe in pepper-flavoured stock.

Name: Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-82, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: The rice that comes with the signature Hainanese boneless chicken imparts a mild turmeric aroma. Tender juicy meat, without too much fat under the bouncy, gelatinous skin. The roast chicken is also recommended.

Name: Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow
Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-12, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: Cooked-to-order black or white fried kway teow with varied ingredients and nicely balanced flavours.

Name: Chey Sua Carrot Cake
Address: 127 Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-30, Blk 127, Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, 310127, Singapore
Description: The pan-fried radish cake is hugely popular. Fried on one side until golden, it allows you to taste the caramelised crispy bits and the soft moist cake at the same time. The cakes are fried to order, so expect a longer waiting time.

Name: Cumi Bali
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Relocated to Tras Street in 2021, this friendly restaurant serves authentic Indonesian cooking in a room enhanced by artifacts and bamboo-styled furnishings. The signature whole grilled squid Cumi Bali – succulent and springy in texture – gives the restaurant its name. It is particularly delicious in their prized homemade sauce made with a myriad of natural spices. Nasi Kunyit is a rice dish jazzed up by 11 spices such as turmeric, cinnamon and pandan leaves.

Name: Lixin Teochew Fishball Noodles
Address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-20, Blk 19 Toa Payoh Lor 7, 310019, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The owner makes the fish balls by hand to ensure they are springy and bursting with umami. Blanched noodles tossed in chilli sauce with crispy cracklings are the perfect companion to the fish ball soup.

Name: Lagnaa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: You can specify the level of spiciness of your food at this three-storey restaurant in Little India, though many come for the Chilli Challenge on full moon nights simply to push their limit. But spiciness isn’t all that this chef has to offer – in fact, he balances it with sweet, sour, salty, bitter and astringent flavours. Choose between table seating downstairs and floor seating upstairs. Parties of two have a number of set menus to choose from.

Name: To-Ricos Guo Shi
Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-135/136, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: Trotter, pork intestine, pork tripe and Kway Chap are recommended.

Name: Indocafé - The White House
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,China UnionPay,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: Dark wood furniture and antiques add to the elegant colonial feel of this restaurant, which lodges within a bungalow and also goes by the name of the ‘The White House’. The menu is dominated by Penang-style Peranakan cuisine and, while the dishes look quite simple, their preparation involves the subtle blending of many spices and ingredients. The signature dishes include Wagyu beef rendang, assam laksa, and kueh pie tee (pastry with turnips, prawns and crab).

Name: Hjh Maimunah (Jalan Pisang)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Wheelchair access
Description: In a narrow street behind Masjid Sultan mosque is a simple Malaysian restaurant that’s always busy – and it’s easy to see why: the ingredients are fresh, the food is delicious and the prices are affordable. Around 70% of dishes are Malaysian and 30% Indonesian; it’s mostly self-service and the dishes to go for include Sundanese grilled chicken, beef rendang, lemak siput and tahu telur. The upstairs room is slightly more comfortable.

Name: TU.REStAURANT
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: After a striking, architect-led conversion, this historic military building now boasts a mezzanine, a feature wine wall and a cocktail bar with a communal table. This all adds up to a stylish and characterful restaurant; one which also features a wide-ranging, modern European menu that includes small plates, large dishes to share and a small pasta selection. Everything is well-priced and appealing, with crêpes Suzettes a must if you get the chance.

Name: MOLÁM
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: A fun evening out is on the cards at this lively spot inspired by the night canteens of Bangkok. An open kitchen and vintage vibe contribute to the party atmosphere, which is helped along by a range of Thai-inspired cocktails. The authentic menu covers all four regions of Thailand, with vibrant dishes delivering the hallmark blend of sweet, sour, spicy and salty. Sharing is encouraged and the dishes are well-priced, so don’t hold back when ordering.

Name: Fromażeria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: As the name suggests, cheese-lovers will be in heaven. To one side is a smart, bustling little bistro; to the other is a cheese bar with an admirable display of global varieties. A concise selection of carefully executed Polish and modern Mediterranean dishes offers great value; these, naturally, should be followed by a cheese course. If you’re just after a quick snack, pop in for a seasonal cheeseboard with alcohol pairings.

Name: Le Braci
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: There's a clubby feel to this intimate Italian restaurant thanks to its zinc-topped bar, high ceiling and dark green colour scheme. The appealing Italian menu covers all regions, while dishes are authentic and full of flavour. A superb range of wines includes those from small Italian producers and lesser-seen regions.

Name: Šug
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Away from the busy tourist centre of Split, this informal, attractive and relaxing restaurant, where the young, friendly staff greet guests with courtesy and a smile, offers a good selection of traditional meat and fish dishes from Dalmatia. A small pleasant outdoor space in the inner courtyard and excellent value for money complete the picture.

Name: Taj Mahal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: In memory of relatives in far-flung places, this restaurant’s menu and decor evoke the simple flavours and traditions of Bosnia, with a couple of pages on the menu dedicated to traditional dishes. There is a focus here on vegetables as well as grilled meats (chosen from the restaurant’s own butcher’s), while a choice of simple cocktails is available alongside the wine list. Situated in the heart of the old town, the restaurant gets extremely busy, so booking is recommended. A second restaurant with the same name can be found outside the town centre in the Hotel Leno.

Name: Beštija
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Occupying the courtyard of a building in the city centre, this pleasant bistro is simply decorated in a mix of traditional and contemporary styles and attracts a young, mixed crowd. The cuisine, heavily inspired by market availability and Croatian produce, showcases precise, aesthetically pleasing presentation and generous portions, using numerous yet carefully balanced ingredients.

Name: Konoba Škoj
Address: Stomorska, Veli Dolac 8, Isola di Solta, 21432, Croatia
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Run by its young female owner and chef, this quiet restaurant with just a few tables boasts excellent Mediterranean-influenced cuisine and an attractive outdoor dining area on a small terrace overlooking the town’s natural harbour. A good choice of cocktails and a small selection of cigars complete the picture.

Name: Batelina
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: Although advance booking is required and the restaurant doesn’t take credit cards, Batelina’s fame extends well beyond Istria, and for good reason as the fish served here is freshly caught and of the highest quality. In this simple, welcoming restaurant you’ll find a superb selection of fish, which is announced at your table and varies in line with the catch of the day.

Name: Konoba Malo Selo
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This typical Istrian restaurant occupying an old stone building has two dining rooms and an outdoor space, with a fireplace and grill used for traditional cooking. We recommend ordering half-portions here so that you can sample different specialities such as the excellent Istrian cured ham (unique in flavour thanks to the way it is aged in the Bora wind), home-made fuzi pasta with a mushroom sauce, and fillet steak grilled over the open fire.

Name: Alla Beccaccia
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: A family-run restaurant situated in a quiet village. The fireplace that dominates the cosy, rustic dining room is not merely decorative but is also used to cook much of the food served here. Although the menu often includes different types of game, the restaurant takes its name from the house speciality (“beccaccia” is the Italian for woodcock) – this takes a long time to prepare and so must be ordered in advance. Fresh pasta, home-made desserts and generous portions all add to the appeal.

Name: Konoba Vinko
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: It's worth heading a few kilometres inland to enjoy the flavoursome local cuisine served at this restaurant, where ham and suckling pig take pride of place on the menu alongside seasonal, traditional dishes and some truly memorable desserts. There’s also a charming outdoor space for summer dining. Booking ahead is recommended!

Name: Tač
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Despite its location in a residential district outside the city centre, it’s worth heading off the beaten track to eat in this restaurant with its welcoming dining rooms and attractive summer terrace. Meat and fish dishes feature on the menu – we particularly enjoyed the fish, which is of a very high quality and prepared in simple, traditional recipes.

Name: Konoba Mate
Address: Village Island, località Pupnat, Korcula, 20260, Croatia
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: It's well worth heading west to this family-run restaurant just over 11km from Korčula, where authentic cuisine full of flavour has been served to guests for over two decades. Much of the food is home made, including bread, the highly recommended pasta served with various sauces, goats' cheese, olive oil, home-grown vegetables and the traditional and more personalised desserts. Although the prices are reasonable, the grilled meat (priced per kilo) is a little more expensive.

Name: Dunav
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Garden or park,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: A small, family-run hotel-restaurant situated on the banks of the Danube with a simple yet well-kept dining room. The menu features fish from the “great river”, including catfish, perch and trout.

Name: Vuglec Breg
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Immersed in the countryside just a few minutes’ drive from the capital, this rural restaurant perched on the top of a hill also offers comfortable guestrooms and a modern swimming pool. The traditional regional cuisine includes local specialities such as Zagorska soup flavoured with mushrooms and bacon, and snails baked in the oven with butter and aromatic herbs. The wine produced by the family themselves is a must, as are the delicious desserts and ice creams.

Name: Izakaya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Although not in a central location, this modern restaurant serving delicious, carefully prepared Japanese cuisine is situated in an area that has a lively evening atmosphere. Don’t miss the chef’s signature rolls, including the excellent Kanji Uramaki (with swordfish tartare) and Age Lobster roll (with lobster in panko bread). The pleasant outdoor space is perfect for an after-dinner cocktail.

Name: Bugenvila
Address: Put dr. Ante Starčevića 9, Cavtat, 20210, Croatia
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: A walk along Cavtat’s promenade brings you to this long-standing harbourside restaurant with a delightful terrace covered in jasmine. Choose between the seasonal à la carte, a great value set menu and plenty of daily specials; whatever you decide on will be light and appealing, and demonstrate a good understanding of Mediterranean flavours. This restaurant – along with its delicious tiramisu and genuine team – is set to become one of your favourites!

Name: Allegrine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Set off the busy Sveavägen thoroughfare, this brasserie provides a hidden oasis. Sit on the attractive front terrace or in the chic dining room, where seats at the kitchen counter are in demand. Variously sized dishes are richly flavoured, with a French base, Scandinavian influences and subtle contrasts.

Name: Ruths
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: The open kitchen takes centre stage at this buzzy all-day café/bakery/deli, which has been wholeheartedly embraced by the locals. Lunchtime snacks and salads make room for generously sized, boldly flavoured Mediterranean dishes at dinner. Most of the wines on the concise list are available on-tap.

Name: Møf
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Ask for a seat at the counter to watch the young chef-owners cook in the open kitchen at this cosy, relaxed restaurant. The 3 different menus presented at dinner allow for some flexibility; dishes are Danish at heart and made with local produce. They offer an impressive selection of organic and natural wines.

Name: Norrlyst
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: An intimate basement bistro with a relaxing, neighbourhood feel. Lunch sees some delicious smørrebrød on offer, while dinner involves a set 4 course menu; seasonality is all-important so expect fresh, top quality local ingredients, accompanied by some interesting beers and an amazing array of schnapps.

Name: Nolla
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Nolla means ‘Zero’ and this incredibly friendly neighbourhood restaurant is all about zero waste. They don’t accept packaging from their suppliers; their uniforms are made from discarded bed linen; and they have their own composter and microbrewery. Original dishes showcase local ingredients and give a nod to Spain.

Name: Møntergade
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The charming team are a big part of the draw at this lively upmarket brasserie that offers generous, classic dishes at a reasonable price. While the chalkboard displays daily specials, there is always a place for a multitude of herring on the menu – curried, picked, marinated or fried, the choice is yours. Other dishes like a perfectly crisped chicken tartlet are equally appealing. There’s a cosy vibe to the place and a small drinks counter where you can chat away with the waiters.

Name: Babette
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Whether you are popping in for a glass of wine and a pizza or choosing a meal from the daily changing menu of small plates, this buzzy neighbourhood bistro is a great place at a great price. Dishes might be simple to look at but have bags of rustic flavour; sit at the counter to be served by the chef.

Name: Triton
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Charming in its lack of pretension, this bohemian neighbourhood restaurant has a homely feel. It’s simply furnished and the pared-back cooking has an unfussiness to match. Dishes show technical skill and provide some well-judged flavours using great Swedish ingredients. In an expensive city, the set menu presents good value for cooking of this quality.

Name: Bona Fide
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: Clean, natural and uncomplicated cooking is the big draw at this simple little restaurant. Welcoming, helpful service and a good atmosphere add to the appeal too, enlivening the modest surroundings. The chefs have a great understanding of their seasonal ingredients and treat them with care. Flavours are subtle but are put together in well-thought-out combinations, resulting in quality dishes at a reasonable price.

Name: Silberbauers Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Eponymous Danish chef Mathias has taken over the spot previously occupied by Manfreds to create a lively, friendly eatery with a focus on fish and shellfish. The day’s catch gives rise to the concise menu, and the emphasis on top quality produce ensures that the simple, well-priced dishes are full of flavour.

Name: Bar Agrikultur
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: A warmly run, intimate and cosy wine bar that is a perfect fit for Södermalm. The freshly prepared and delicious small plates are designed for sharing and showcase classic Swedish flavours. The three stainless steel tanks contain home-distilled gin – flavours are changed regularly using various herbs, oils or fruits.

Name: JH Matbar
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: You will find this bistro at the southern tip of Sweden, in the centre of a small town with picturesque streets that provided the setting for the Wallander detective TV series. The good value menu offers a wide choice of dishes, with vegetarians and vegans well catered for. Scandinavian produce powers many of the modern dishes, which are prepared and presented with real care.

Name: Enomania
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: A simple, bistro-style restaurant near Frederiksberg Park – its name means ‘Wine Mania’. The wine cellar comes with a table for tasting and there’s an excellent list of over 600 bins, mostly from Piedmont and Burgundy. These are complemented by straightforward, tasty Italian dishes from a weekly 4 course menu.

Name: Bjørnekælderen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The ‘Bear’s Basement’ has been a restaurant for over 130 years, and references to the furry creatures are legion in this cosy, characterful eatery. Smørrebrød are served at lunch, with more substantial dishes in the evening, and the carefully crafted plates have flavour, imagination and a modern touch.

Name: FAGN-Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This simple bistro is set on the floor above FAGN restaurant and uses the same top quality local produce as its Michelin-Starred sibling. The Norwegian dishes are rustic with punchy flavours; choose between an à la carte or tasting menus of 3 and 5 courses. The waiting staff and chefs add to the relaxed buzz.

Name: anx
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This nicely styled, well-run annexe to Frederikshøj serves sophisticated yet well-priced smørrebrød, which are classic in their ingredients and modern in their presentation. Contemporary art punctuates the walls and service is charming and efficient.

Name: Mêlée
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: You will quickly feel at home in this bustling neighbourhood bistro with a friendly, lively atmosphere. The uncomplicated spirit of the restaurant is reflected in modern, country-style cooking, generous portions and bold flavours. There is a French basis to the concise monthly menus, with some Danish influences. The excellent wine list offers an impressive array of vintages.

Name: Marv & Ben
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The young owners bring plenty of enthusiasm to this little restaurant, where dining is split over two dimly lit floors. Organic produce features in seasonal cooking which displays purity and depth of flavour. They produce 6 dishes each evening, which are priced individually or as 4 or 6 courses.

Name: Smalhans
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: A sweet neighbourhood café with friendly staff and an urban feel. Coffee and homemade cakes are served in the morning, with a short selection of dishes including soup and a burger on offer between 12pm and 4pm. In the evenings, they serve a set menu of rustic Norwegian dishes.

Name: Pondus
