He grew up in Miami, then apprenticed at a number of organic farms in Sweden, France and Israel before returning to his hometown to fulfill his culinary dreams. The crux of his menu is baked, as in breads and pastries, along with sandwiches, soups and salads. The "BLT" features salmon bacon, lettuce and tomato all stuffed into a deliciously flaky croissant. For something sweet, get the flourless dark chocolate cookie bursting with whole toasted almonds.This kosher bakery and café is located in hip Wynwood and welcomes diners with a color-splashed façade. Its breakfast and lunch hours are supplemented by an evening falafel service, so come and be ready to stay.

Name: Domu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Brunch,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Enter Chef/owner Sean "Sonny" Nguyen's trendy ramen haven and you'll find two rooms dressed with concrete floors, a marble bar and wood panels set aglow by a starburst light fixture. The second room cradles the bulk of the crowd. As the name illustrates, this chef makes his culinary "dreams come true" by dint of a classic-meets-creative menu. Beyond the small plates lies the star item—ramen. Creations, like the Ritchie Rich and Curry, are full of bold, memorable flavors and certainly worth a slurp. Tokyo ramen with shoyu chicken broth, fried chicken thigh and duck fat is a sensory feat. Couple it with blistered shishitos for a delicious touch—and bit of crunch.It's all in the family here as sib Tori Tori flaunts a similarly creative izakaya menu.

Name: Tinta y Cafe
Address: 1315 Ponce De Leon Blvd., Coral Gables, 33134, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Coral Gables is home to this original operation, happily christened with a name that translates to ink and coffee. Unsurprisingly, there are artfully arranged bookshelves that line its glass façade, while the interior design most certainly resembles that of a coffee shop. Guests may order at the window, grab a table either inside or out under a cluster of palm trees, and settle in for a litany of Cuban delicacies.The furniture is mid-century modern, but the sandwich-focused menu is as classic and comforting as ever. Deep-fried croquetas are not to be missed; and the pavo real with turkey and cream cheese is nothing if not satisfying. Our allegiance, however, is with the patria (their take on the Cubano with pork, ham, mustard and pickles.)

Name: La Natural
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: You wouldn’t think to make reservations for a pizza place in Little River, but think again. The crowds can be relentless at this popular hangout, which feels rather like an underground party by way of concrete floors and dim lighting.Creative toppings like za’atar and Sichuan peppercorns sing on stunning, picture-perfect pies zealously charred in a wood-burning oven hiding behind the bar. We’re partial to the classic burrata and basil pie, which arrives puffy and pillowy thanks to the signature crust that's cold-fermented for 48 hours. An astute selection of starters (try the papaya with kumquat) and one of the city’s longest lists for natural wines only add to the appeal of this essential pizzeria. A personable staff keeps a close watch on every table.

Name: Sai Kwan Lo Jo
Address: Shop B, 18 Man Yuen Street, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This takeout-only shop carries both traditional and novelty snacks. Try hand-made lai fun noodles in Sai Kwan style, deep-fried sticky rice dumpling with Iberico pork, or stir-fried turnip cake with XO chilli sauce.

Name: Ho To Tai
Address: 67 Fau Tsoi Street, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Traditional shops that make their own noodles from scratch are hard to come by. Founded in 1946, this household name is among the remaining few. Though the nostalgic two-storey shop draws a crowd with its signature wonton soup, zhajiang noodles and beef brisket noodle soup are also popular. Try braised white radish with shrimp roe for the deep umami and briny-sweetness. The owner also runs a dried noodle factory with retail outlets all over town.

Name: Tin Hung
Address: Shop D, GF, Yan Yee Building, 88 Kin Yip Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Popular with locals since 2001, this shop sells its signature roast goose in specific cuts, halves or whole. Geese are shipped from Foshan daily, marinated, roasted to perfection, and served piping hot. Other standouts include honey-glazed char siu, roast duck and drunken chicken. Those looking to pair the meats with a local drink should try their herbal tea. Given the reasonable prices and limited seats, it makes sense to arrive early.

Name: Tak Kee
Address: Shop G, 3 Belcher's Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: It started out as a street-side hawker stall in the 1990s and still retains the casual, vibrant vibe. The second-generation hands-on owner shops for groceries every day and sometimes helps the experienced chefs with kitchen chores. Pork tripe and peppercorn soup is a culinary highlight, using peppers from Malaysia and Indonesia. Regulars also come for its spiced marinated goose liver, crispy chitterlings stuffed with glutinous rice and oyster omelette.

Name: Din Tai Fung (Tsim Sha Tsui)
Address: Shop 306, 3F, Silvercord, 30 Canton Road, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: From the late Mr Yang’s first shop in Taiwan in 1958 grew a multinational chain with branches all over the world. It’s famous for good service, competitive prices and listening to its customer’s feedback, but mostly for its xiao long bao made on the spot. Even the vinegar, free of artificial colours and preservatives, is shipped from Taiwan. Seating accommodates different party sizes, from solo diners to parties of 12. Expect long queues at peak hours.

Name: Fisholic (North Point)
Address: Shop 14, GF, Victor Court, 14-28 Wang On Road, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Famous for snacks and noodles made with fish, this stall sells playful items like deep-fried minced fish in the guise of French fries, or fish skin nachos. Fishotto, where minced fish is shaped like rice grains, is also good.

Name: Ship Kee
Address: GF, Pao Yip Building, 7 Ship Street, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Ship Kee opened its doors in 2021 and prides itself on Cantonese classics from the old days. The barbecue chef honed his skills in some prestigious kitchens for over 40 years; his Master Woo’s honey glazed BBQ pork is seasoned perfectly, tender but springy. The dim sum chef has 30+ years of experience; his steamed rice rolls with shrimps and Chinese chives look like gems under a velvety, translucent skin. Call ahead to pre-order certain dishes.

Name: Congee and Noodle Shop
Address: Shop 2A, 2F, Kerry Centre, 683 King's Road, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Wheelchair access
Description: Hidden in a glass office tower, this simple shop may not have much ambiance or character, but everyone is here for the creamy congee made by a chef with over 30 years of experience. There are countless combinations of toppings and you can customize your own congee; bestsellers include fresh crab congee, and chicken congee with abalone. Deep-fried dough items, and pan-fried fish cake with fermented clam sauce, are also worth trying.

Name: Twins Liangpi Limited (Prince Edward)
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: (The restaurant has moved to Mong Kok in November 2023) Icy cold glass noodles dressed in a secret blend of chilli vinegar are topped with shredded cucumber, coriander, peas and ground peanuts. Try also spicy diced lotus root, and ice jelly in dark brown sugar syrup.

Name: Tim Ho Wan (Sham Shui Po)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The second branch of this famous dim sum chain is roomier than the original, but don’t be surprised to still find a queue of expectant diners at the entrance. Over 20 different dim sum are on offer, all skilfully made and reasonably priced. Some items rotate every two to three months to keep the menu fresh. Don’t miss their shrimp dumplings, baked buns with barbecue pork filling and steamed beef balls. Two rooms on the first floor offer more privacy.

Name: Tasty (Central)
Address: Shop 3016-3018, 3F, IFC Mall, 1 Harbour View Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Valet parking,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Be prepared to queue and share a table because over 1,000 customers a day, many of whom work in IFC, crowd into this Tasty. They mostly come for the trademark shrimp wonton or the much-loved beef and rice noodle stir fry; congee with prawns and dim sum are also recommended from the vast choice on offer. The last redecoration left the interior looking a lot more contemporary.

Name: Saya
Address: Shop G701, GF, Square Mile II, 18 Ka Shin Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: A turquoise colour scheme, rattan furniture and wall coverings impart a retro tropical vibe. The menu is dominated by Isan cuisine from Northeast Thailand, mindfully prepared by a Thai kitchen team. Khao Soy bursts with aromas from the coconut milk curry and chargrilled chicken. Pla Phao, salt-crusted grilled fish seasoned with lemongrass and pandan, is served with lettuce, rice vermicelli and a tangy sauce. Lunch menu offers great value.

Name: Ju Xing Home
Address: GF, 416 and 418 Portland Street, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This hole-in-the-wall is always jam-packed and that’s down to chef-owner Ng’s cooking, not the décor or service. Cantonese stir-fries prevail, alongside a few spicy options. The must-try salt-baked Wenchang chicken is succulent, flavourful and tends to run out early. Live seafood is also big on the menu, like lobster with pan-fried rice vermicelli. Reservations are recommended and it’s worth pre-ordering the chicken to avoid missing out.

Name: Tai Wing Wah
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: This bright, fresh and long-standing Cantonese restaurant serves dim sum and ‘Walled Village’ cuisine, alongside assorted Cantonese classics. Walled village-style five-flavour chicken boasts flavoursome, velvety meat. Other specialities include roast duck with bean paste and coriander; claypot rice with lard, premium soy sauce, steamed mullet with salted lemon; and, above all, the steamed sponge cake. Also check out the seasonal menu.

Name: Ding Ba (Choi Hung)
Address: Shop 2C, Kwai Chi Path, Ngau Chi Wan, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The Taiwanese owner and chef serve authentic street snacks from their homeland – oyster omelette, vermicelli soup, stinky tofu, pancake rolls, and braised minced pork rice, to pair with rice milk or winter melon tea.

Name: Both Street (Yuen Long)
Address: Shop 18, GF, Shun Fung Building, 5-7 Fung Yau Street North, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Come for the gua bao sandwiches, especially the traditional version with pork belly and yuja marmalade in fluffy buns made in-house daily. Deep-fried mochi balls and pressed cheese sandwiches are also worth trying. The shop closes when the food has sold out.

Name: Chiuchow Delicacies (North Point)
Address: Shop 4, GF, Gain Yu Building, 96 Wharf Road, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This shop isn’t particularly spacious, but that doesn’t stop customers from coming here for their authentic Chiu Chow cooking at wallet-friendly prices. Sliced goose steeped in signature spiced marinade is velvety without being greasy – refer to the mural for the spices used. The variety of chilled steamed fish on offer is quite a spectacle, all oily and delicious. Some dishes need pre-ordering and expect to share a table with strangers when it’s busy.

Name: Din Tai Fung (Causeway Bay)
Address: Shop G3-G11, GF, 68 Yee Woo Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The xiao long bao are good enough to justify the long queues – so worry not. Alongside the traditional soupy pork filling, they also come in novelty versions such as black truffle and angled luffa with shrimps. Ingredients are sourced from the same suppliers as its Taiwan flagship and the same kitchen team here delivers food in consistently high quality. Other standouts include double-boiled chicken soup and braised beef brisket noodle soup.

Name: Café Hunan (Western District)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The kitchen team of Hunanese natives boasts solid skills, especially in quick-fried dishes that sport exceptional wok hei. Ingredients such as chillies and smoked pork are sourced directly from farmers in Hunan. The speciality braised pork elbow involves four complicated cooking steps spanning over 10 hours to develop layered flavours and the right texture. Stir-fried pork with Youxian beancurd and spicy organic cauliflower are also worth trying.

Name: Sing Kee
Address: 2F, 1 Lyndhurst Tower, 1 Lyndhurst Terrace, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Sing Kee is a bright, tidy spot serving traditional, no-frills Cantonese food – something that’s increasingly hard to find in Central. Standouts include pan-seared salted chicken, and grilled tiger prawns in Malaysian curry sauce with crispy rice crackers. Specialities like double-boiled fish maw and pork lung in almond milk need pre-ordering. Come at lunch to take advantage of some reasonable prices.

Name: IFTM Educational Restaurant
Address: Pousada de Mong-Há, Colina de Mong-Há, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,China UnionPay,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Being part of the Institute for Tourism Studies means that some of the kitchen and front of house teams are students – and the pride they have in their work is palpable. The menu is a mix of European and Macanese dishes; the latter stand out in particular with their clean taste, deceptively effortless preparation and use of the freshest ingredients. The house-made bread is also good. Oenophiles should check out the exclusively Portuguese wine list.

Name: Cheong Kei
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: A family business since the '70s, this noodle shop sticks to its roots and its thin, fine noodles are pressed by bamboo pole in its own factory nearby. Their soup is cooked with dried prawns and dried plaice for 8 hours. The noodles with dried shrimp roe are great, but also try their wontons and dace balls that are served deep-fried or blanched; the fermented clam sauce is the perfect accompaniment to the dace balls.

Name: Takeya
Address: Shop 1, On Wah Building, 31C1 Tak Man Street, Whampoa Estate, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This intimate 15-seater yakitori shop is the brainchild of a Japanese engineer, now the chef, and his wife, now the maître d'. For over a decade, they’ve been feeding hungry diners in the neighbourhood with quality grilled food, with some ingredients flown in from Japan. Rare cuts such as chicken heart and hatsumoto (artery) are definitely worth a try. Pair them with their selection of sake or home-brewed umeshu. Reservations are recommended.

Name: Tai Wai Dining Room (Tai Wai)
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Valet parking,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The red lanterns at the entrance are a prelude to the nostalgic, Chinese-style interior. The experienced kitchen team shows respect to Cantonese traditions, but with a subtle sense of cheeky humour. Dim sum dominates the menu at lunch, and all-time favourites like duo sausage rolls and pan-fried chicken sticky rice dumplings particularly stand out. Portion sizes are generous, service is thoughtful – and the food is consistently good.

Name: Kung Wo Beancurd Factory
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This much-loved shop makes its own tofu that boasts a deep, rich soy aroma. As well as the renowned tofu pudding, it also carries other soy products like soy milk, fried stuffed tofu, tofu puffs and golden fish tofu.

Name: Samsen (Wan Chai)
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This casual Thai noodle shop next to the historic Blue House is aptly named after an area in Bangkok where the Chinese traded with the Thais. Rattan blinds, bare concrete walls and distressed wood furniture give off a street-stall vibe. The signature boat noodles are not to be missed – the flavoursome broth alone takes 6 hours to make. Those with a sweet tooth can round things off with young coconut ice cream. Come early to beat the crowd.

Name: Shek Kee Kitchen
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: During the day, this cosy joint in the heart of the city serves light meals and fried noodles. At night, the menu specialises in home-style Cantonese dishes. The owner-chef Mr Shek sources the freshest ingredients from wet markets daily and regulars also call him directly to pre-order certain dishes, such as fried chicken with toasted garlic which needs a day’s notice. The pan-fried hand-minced cuttlefish patties are springy and flavourful.

Name: Ah Chun Shandong Dumpling
Address: 60 Lai Chi Kok Road, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The shop has a traditional feel to it. Green wooden window frames on the wall are reminiscent of old-time Hong Kong. Dumplings are handmade daily and only the freshest ingredients are used in the fillings. Try their most-ordered item lamb and Peking scallion dumplings. Or surprise yourself with the specialty, such as mackerel dumplings and cuttlefish dumplings. Shandong roast lamb and meat pie are also recommended.

Name: Yi Jia
Address: Shop G04, Lime Gala, 393 Shau Kei Wan Road, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: A stark contrast of colours, neon lights and retro patterns make the room unorthodox but welcoming. On the menu, you can find Shanghainese and Sichuanese classics like Qili Zhuang drunken chicken in wine lees, and Sichuan boiled fish. But novelty creations such as deep-fried soufflé meringue with mango custard filling are also worth trying. The creator’s sense of humour comes through in the cheeky drinks menu. Set menus are especially well priced.

Name: Din Tai Fung (COD)
Address: SOHO, 2F, City of Dreams, Estrada do Istmo, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The second floor of COD plays host to a plethora of casual eateries – and in the corner you’ll find this sizeable branch of the international chain. Din Tai Fung is rightly known for its exquisite xiao long bao but also special here is the steamed crab roe and pork dumpling. Other notables from the 70-odd Shanghainese dishes on offer include the excellent braised beef noodle soup. To finish, try the red bean glutinous rice cake.

Name: Chan Seng Kei
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This semi open-air restaurant has stood next to an ancient church for over 70 years and the 3rd generation of the family still focus on traditional Cantonese cooking. Seafood is the highlight as the owner works closely with local fishermen to secure the best catch – he prefers wild-caught fish about 500 to 600g for their tender flesh. Also try stewed duck with tangerine peel which takes more than 10 hours to make, with only a few available each day.

Name: Tai Woo
Address: 9F, Causeway Bay Plaza 2, 463-483 Lockhart Road, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: One of the district’s most famous names, Tai Woo opened its door in the 80s and moved to this address in 2011 and, while the restaurant may be smaller than before, business is better than ever, with over 1,000 customers served every day. What hasn’t changed is the quality of the cooking – along with a menu of wallet friendly Cantonese seafood dishes, such as fish fried rice with ginger, are favourites like sesame chicken baked in salt.

Name: Kau Kee
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Kau Kee has been trading since the 1930s and has consequently built up such a huge following that you’ll probably have to line up in the street first to eat here. It’s all very basic and you’ll have to share your table but the food is delicious. Beef noodles are the speciality; different cuts of meat with a variety of noodles in a tasty broth or spicy sauce. Try the milk tea too.

Name: Po Kee
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: How far would you go for a bowl of Lai Fan noodles with roast duck leg? Every morning loyal fans line up at the door before this shop opens – that’s how good it is. A fixture in the neighbourhood for over 40 years, Po Kee is hugely popular among locals for its roast meats freshly grilled in the factory behind the shop. Time your visit as roast pork tends to run out before 2 pm and the goose before 4 pm; or you can pre-order to avoid disappointment.

Name: Sister Wah
Address: Shop A1, 13 Electric Road, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The legendary Sister Wah is no longer at the helm but her sons are running the shop just like she used to. The signature beef brisket in clear soup uses fresh local beef which is braised in a stock with over 10 different herbs. Popular items on the brief menu include homemade pork and cabbage dumplings, drunken chicken, Dan Dan noodles, and braised white radish in beef juices. With only six tables, it fills up as soon as it opens.

Name: She Wong Leung
Address: Shop A, GF, 298 Electric Road, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: In business for over 20 years, this shop is famous for its snake soup. While most people consume snake soup only in winter, the owner formulates a different herbal base for every season to make it a healthy tonic all year round. Set menus comprising of snake soup and home-style dishes offer exceptional value and cater for all tastes. Go for glutinous rice or lamb stew in winter. Double-boiled soups are popular but require pre-ordering.

Name: Eng Kee Noodle Shop
Address: GF, 32 High Street, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This family-run shop is always jam-packed with hungry locals craving Cantonese noodle soup. No matter for dine-in or take-out, expect a reasonable wait. It prides itself on its signature beef brisket – braised one night ahead and steeped in a spiced marinade overnight for silky tenderness and deep flavours. Their oven-grilled char siu is made with pork shoulder and pork neck and has a juicy, springy texture thanks to the fine marbling.

Name: Dragon Inn
Address: Miles 19, Castle Peak Road, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant is known by almost everyone in the neighbourhood and was revamped in 2017 to include more private rooms alongside the main dining hall. Most guests pick their seafood from the nearby wet market for the chefs here to cook up; others choose from the catch of the day without looking at the menu. Baked baby lobster with cheese and baked oysters with port are not to be missed. It also serves dim sum during the day.

Name: Shugetsu Ramen (Central)
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The queues form early for the ramen here, with many of the customers coming for the Tsukemen ramen, as well as the Abura and special soup ramen. The shop makes its own noodles – which you can have thick or thin – but it is the sauce at the base of the slow-cooked soup that really makes the difference: it’s fermented for 18 months in a 100-year-old wooden basket and adds richness and depth.

Name: Wing Lai Yuen
Address: Shop 102-105, 1F, Gourmet Place, Whampoa Plaza, Site 8, Whampoa Garden, 7 Tak On Street, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Originally a run-down shop in a squatter village, it moved to this airy and bright location in 2000. But one thing never changed – the food is as delicious and affordably priced as ever. The signature Dan Dan noodles come in two versions: a meat one with ground pork and a traditional one without, plus a spicy or mild broth to choose from. Shuizhu mandarin fish packs numbing heat and the portion size is big enough for a few to share.

Name: Wang Fu (Central)
Address: 65 Wellington Street, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Wang Fu is famous for its Pekingese dumplings – among the great variety of handmade dumplings on the menu, the green onion mutton one stands out most. Apart from dumpling soups, it also serves fried dumplings with light charred crispy skin and juicy fillings. Try also the tomato and egg dumpling, only available after 2 pm. If you fancy more variety, check out their noodles and cold appetisers as well, or ask about the daily special.

Name: Tsim Chai Kee (Wellington Street)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The long lunchtime queue happens for a reason – the noodles here are bouncy and the broth is flavoursome. Only three toppings are offered – springy dace balls, wontons generously filled with pork and shrimps, and sliced beef with a robust meaty flavour and tender texture. You can even choose a combination of any two or all three toppings. Expect to share a table with strangers when it’s busy or eat outside of peak times to beat the crowd.

Name: Lok Kei Noodles
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This busy shop next to the pier still kneads the noodles with a bamboo pole just like old times and the flavourful broth is simmered with an array of seasonal fish. The owner’s wife insists on making wonton wrappers and cooking noodles by herself and she’s very specific about both the cooking time and the consistency of the noodles. Other popular dishes include crab congee, tossed noodles with dried prawn roe, and deep-fried wontons with crispy dace balls.

Name: Megan's Kitchen
Address: 5F, Lucky Centre, 165-171 Wan Chai Road, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Visa credit card
Description: The menu offers many Cantonese dishes, but steamed minced beef patty with dried mandarin peel, and Yu Xiang eggplant in claypot stand out in particular. Better still, all mains come with complimentary rice, soup and dessert. Their famous hot pots spoil diners with an array of soup bases and good quality ingredients. Those who prefer a little privacy will appreciate the booth seating with sliding screens as dividers.

Name: Kwan Kee Bamboo Noodles
Address: Shop E, 1 Wing Lung Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: It’s inside a local market but easy to spot, thanks to the big yellow sign. Watch the kitchen at work through the glass wall as noodles are made the traditional way – with the chef seesawing on a bamboo pole to painstakingly knead the egg-rich dough for that stringy texture. Secret techniques are deployed to remove the soapy taste of lye and accentuate the eggy flavour. Don’t miss the signature noodles tossed in shrimp roe and oyster sauce.

Name: Glorious Cuisine
Address: 31-33 Shek Kip Mei Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Picking out live critters from the tank is part of the fun – Hokkaido scallops, Thai marble goby, and even Hanasaki crab if you’re lucky. As well as the signature braised chicken stuffed with abalone and sea cucumber, do try dishes made with chicken offal, such as stock-poached leafy greens with chicken liver. Double-boiled chicken soup with conpoy and Yunnan ham is available in limited quantities, so consider pre-ordering certain items.

Name: Sang Kee
Address: 1-2F, Hip Sang Building, 107-115 Hennessy Road, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Bring your own bottle,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Having stood here proudly for over 40 years, Sang Kee is a true symbol of Wan Chai and remains refreshingly impervious to modernisation. The owner insists on buying seafood herself each day and dishes are made the traditional way. You’ll find yourself thinking about their salt-baked chicken, pork liver and wolfberry leaves blanched in stock, and baked fish intestine with egg long after you’ve sampled them. Book a table and pre-order your favourites.

Name: Trusty Congee King (Wan Chai)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Wheelchair access
Description: As suggested by its name, you can really trust the quality of the food served in this long-standing congee shop. The menu has become more versatile in recent years with congee, noodles and snack sets available. All congee is cooked in fish broth that gives an extra dimension of flavour. Many rave about the pork liver and scallop congee, sticky rice dumpling with salted egg yolk and pork, and poached grass carp skin.

Name: Lou Kei (Fai Chi Kei)
Address: Shop H&M, GF, Vang Kei Building, 12 Avenida Da Concõrdia N, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: If you’re looking for a simple, good value supper, then Lou Kei may well fit the bill. Granted, it may not be in the centre of town, but every local and cab driver knows this lively place. For over 20 years, its sizeable selection of tasty noodles, congee and Cantonese dishes have won the hearts of countless diners. Sizzling Bombay duck with sand ginger delivers amazing 'wok hei'. Frogs' legs in claypot and crab congee are both highly recommended.

Name: Ancient Moon
Address: Shop A, 29 Kam Ping Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: On a trip to Singapore and Malaysia, owners Fanni and Lico fell in love with their street food which inspired them to open their fun little spot. The small menu lists about 12 items, but you won’t find typical national dishes here. Instead, it’s among the few places that offer Malaysian chilli pan mee (a flavoursome noodle dish with dried fish and chilli sauce) and free refill of Singaporean bak kut teh, a MSG-free, peppery pork rib soup.

Name: Ba Yi
Address: 43 Water Street, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Despite being somewhat out of the way, lamb-lovers gather here in numbers for items such as stewed lamb and mutton skewers, prepared by the Xinjiangese kitchen team. The signature roasted lamb leg is big enough to share between two and needs pre-ordering. Besides lamb, it’s also worth trying the chicken stew with potato and chilli, as well as the Ketik yoghurt drink. The dining room still features the map of the Silk Road on a stretched canvas.

Name: Brass Spoon (Wan Chai)
Address: Shop B, GF, 1-3 Moon Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Diners have been queuing up for the tasty pho here since Day 1. The chef learnt to cook in France, where his family had a Vietnamese restaurant, and has recreated the vibe of a little ramen shop in Tokyo here. He uses U.S. Angus beef and Danish pork and, for the noodles’ soup base, slow-cooks beef shank bone for more than 16 hours. On top of the signature raw beef variety, do order Vietnamese sausage, beef balls, tendon, or tripe.

Name: Nishiki
Address: Shop 103, 1F, Regal Kowloon Hotel, 71 Mody Road, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Valet parking,Visa credit card
Description: Despite opening over 20 years ago, the bustling atmosphere and tasty grill dishes of this izakaya-style place still shine. The Japanese owner-chef teaches his kitchen team the tricks for perfect barbecue – his famous tsukune, for example, is made with boneless chicken thigh from Japan and Brazil in a specific ratio. Grilled chicken liver from local farms is another speciality. Reservations are recommended; ask for counter seats to get close to the action.

Name: O Castiço
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Ownership of this simple, unassuming little place with just five tables has now passed down to the late owner's son – though his spirit is still honoured in the atmosphere of the restaurant, which is as friendly and as intimate as it ever was. The food is also just as good – the home-style dishes are authentic and carefully prepared, with recommendations being the stewed pork with clams and the oven-roasted bacalhau with potatoes.

Name: Hao Tang Hao Mian (Tai Wai)
Address: GF, 20 Chik Chuen Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: An owner-chef with over 20 years of experience in French cooking opened this 20-seater specialising in just 12 noodle soup items, each with a specific soup base and topping. The signature flat noodles in beef soup with Sichuanese beef cheek and French-style braised oxtail takes two days to make, involving eclectic techniques. The dessert menu is equally impressive – try the all-natural sorbets made in-house with fresh fruits.

Name: Fung Shing (North Point)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This long-standing heavyweight in Shun Tak cuisine has a traditionally furnished look and is spread over two floors. Guests come for dim sum in the morning while Cantonese favourites and painstakingly prepared Shun Tak specialities are served at lunch and dinner. Try fatty pork crabmeat fritters, Daliang-style scrambled egg white with milk, and crispy fried chicken, all showing astute techniques. Call ahead to ask about dishes that need pre-ordering.

Name: Sun Yuen Hing Kee
Address: 327 Queen's Road Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Located next to Sheung Wan market, this traditionally styled, simple but well- maintained Cantonese barbecue shop has been run by the same family since the mid-1970s. Over the years they’ve built up an appreciative following. After a renovation in 2021, the shop was downsized and its 12 seats fill up quickly. The appetising looking suckling pigs are not the only draw: roast pork, soft-boiled chicken and homemade sausages all have their fans.

Name: Putien (Causeway Bay)
Address: Shop A, 7F, Lee Theatre Plaza, 99 Percival Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The original restaurant was founded in Singapore in 2000 and named after a coastal city in Fujian province – the owner’s hometown. This branch comes with an easy-going atmosphere and its Fujian cuisine is respectful of tradition, with a focus on natural flavours. New items are added to the menu from time to time. Don’t miss their themed offerings that feature a particular seasonal seafood, such as razor clams or oysters.

Name: Kai Kai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Traditional Chinese sweet soups like tofu skin soup with ginkgo and Job’s tears, or black sesame soup boast rich flavours. Top it with glutinous rice balls or a hard-boiled egg for extra texture.

Name: Yue Kee
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Valet parking,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: From humble beginnings as a tiny countryside joint in 1958, this second-generation family business has gone big, but without losing its flair. Owning a farm that breeds Qingyuan black brown geese ensures quality and a steady supply. Chargrilled according to the owner’s family recipe and served after 11:45am, their goose is known for its distinctive smokiness, crispy skin and juicy meat. The menu also includes seafood and stir-fries.

Name: What To Eat
Address: Shop A, GF, Carfield Commercial Building, 75-77 Wyndham Street, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Two Taiwanese mums have revived the old name of their first bento shop. The menu is now bigger, but the food is just as good and the service just as warm and homely. Egg crepe roll is made with ingredients imported from Taiwan and the beef shin in the noodle soup is braised for more than five hours in a spiced broth. Bento rice boxes at lunch make for a balanced meal, while the Taiwanese snacks at dinner are definitely worth trying.

Name: Moon Tong Lok
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: For 25 years, the owner has been making cifan sticky rice rolls à la minute to ensure freshness. His hot and sour soup exudes a tomato tang, while savoury soy milk is made with dried krill that lends robust umami.

Name: Samsen (Sheung Wan)
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: Readers may recognize the name it shares with a noodle shop in Wan Chai – yes, this is a spinoff by the same owner-chef, Adam Cliff. While it shares almost the same menu as the Wan Chai branch, certain exclusive dishes stand out. For instance, its signature 11-spice Northern Thai curry takes up to eight hours to make and is the perfect companion to egg noodles. Desserts like young coconut ice cream or mango and sticky rice are also pluses.

Name: Eight Treasures
Address: Shop B, GF, Wing Wah Building, 124 Electric Road, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This noodle shop moved here from Hung Hom in 2018 and has a loyal following. Beef lovers adore its signature beef brisket in a tonic broth simmered with eight herbs (hence the name) and beef bones for over 10 hours. Alternatively, top your soup or tossed noodles with boneless short ribs, inside skirt, outside skirt or a combo of all three. Honeycomb tripe, sinew, tongue and beef balls are also great. Arrive early as certain cuts can run out before 1pm.

Name: Mak Man Kee
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: No one is here for the no-frills interior, typical of any noodle shop in Hong Kong. This 60-year-old establishment is all about Cantonese wonton soup noodles – firm and bouncy prawns, visible through the paper-thin translucent skin, with springy duck egg noodles swimming in a flavourful broth. The noodles taste equally great when simply tossed in oyster sauce or shrimp roe, the latter also available as a pre-packaged condiment to go.

Name: Lucky Indonesia
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The décor of the small dining room may feel a bit dated, but it’s the authentic, tasty middle-Javanese cooking that has kept regulars coming back for over 30 years. The signature chargrilled satay exudes an addictive smoky aroma – and it comes in lamb, beef, pork and chicken varieties. Other Indonesian specialities such as Nasi Kuning and Bandeng Goreng are also highly recommended.

Name: Lau Sum Kee (Fuk Wing Street)
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Since 1956, this branch (and the original shop around the corner) has been packed with customers buzzing in and out. The third-generation family business still kneads noodle dough with a bamboo pole, like it used to be done, for that springy texture. Wontons are made on the spot with whole prawns and pork; even the crunchy radish pickles are homemade. Wonton noodles are a must; you can choose one or two more toppings if you like.

Name: Lin Heung Kui
Address: 2-3F, 40-50 Des Voeux Road West, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This huge two-floor eatery opened in 2009 with the aim of building on the success of the famous Lin Heung Tea House in Wellington Street. It's modest inside but hugely popular and the dim sum trolley is a must, with customers keen to be the first to choose from its extensive offerings. The main menu offers classic Cantonese dishes with specialities such as Lin Heung special duck. Don’t miss the limited offered pig's lung soup with almond juice. The pastry shop below is worth a look on the way out.

Name: Kwan Kee Clay Pot Rice (Queen's Road West)
Address: Shop 1, GF, Wo Yick Mansion, 263 Queen's Road West, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Its red sign, basic interior and traditional stir-fries all point to an authentic Hong Kong food experience. Claypot rice is only served at night and takes time to prepare, so order it first as soon as you’re seated. The three-rice blend results in a chewy texture and appealing fragrance; the bottom crust is always perfectly scorched. The white eel variety is especially popular; pair it with claypot dishes with excellent wok hei.

Name: Eton
Address: 1-2F, European Asian Bank Building, 749 Nathan Road, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: In 2019, the long-standing household name Fung Shing closed its doors as the owner-chef retired. A regular customer and the staff then got together to re-open it as Eton in 2020. The room was renovated and about 80% of the kitchen and service teams returned. The menu is largely the same; dim sum, crispy fried chicken, deep-fried shrimp toast, scrambled egg white with milk in Daliang style, and Shun Tak fish tripe thick soup are still recommended.

Name: Yuan is Here (Western District)
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Decorated with memorabilia and evincing a night market buzz, this Taiwanese street food shop moved here from Sai Ying Pun in 2019. The owner and chef hail from Taiwan and make sure every bite they serve is as authentically Taiwanese as it could be. The signature braised minced pork rice has great depth and a melty texture. Deluxe seafood omelette is a variation of the oyster fritter, with shrimps and scallops. Round it out with taro balls for dessert.

Name: Chan Kan Kee Chiu Chow
Address: Shop 353B, Level 3, The LOHAS, 1 Lohas Park Road, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The third-generation owners of this 70-year-old household name decided to move from Sheung Wan to this shopping mall in 2020. Regulars would feel reassured finding the familiar gilded sign on black hanging over the semi-open kitchen where a dazzling spread of food is on display. The must-try signature marinated goose sports velvety, flavourful flesh and just the right amount of fat. Seafood like crabs and fourfinger threadfins needs pre-ordering.

Name: Bistro de Olliemölle
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This charmingly old-fashioned bistro, set in an old watermill, is a remarkable place. The water wheel still turns occasionally but the real treat is the idyllic terrace next to the water! Cooking is, in the main, traditional and generous, but you can also find some more contemporary dishes which demonstrate the chef’s experience.

Name: Blauw
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Tradition, a street food influence, authenticity and purity are the words that best sum up this popular restaurant, which showcases the full array of Indonesian cuisine. The rijsttafel (a medley of dishes with rice – also available in a vegan version) provides an excellent opportunity to discover the chef's talent for seasoning and balancing intense flavours. From the succulence of the lamb, the distinctly nutty flavour of the peanut sauce and the delicate spiciness of the gado gado, you can see that this is a chef who knows how to combine generosity with subtlety. Be sure to try the roast goat meat as well!

Name: Mijn Streek
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Cold or hot dishes, whether to share with your dining companions or go solo, to opt for one of the many vegetarian options or plump for fish or meat… In this convivial brasserie on the fifth floor of the Glaspaleis, there are plenty of choices to be made. Brace yourself for an international culinary adventure that takes in ceviche, ravioli, strawberry Romanoff and many other mouth-watering treats. A visit to the Schunck Museum in the same building is a must if you visit the area.

Name: Escobar
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: This colourful restaurant has a real holiday feel, with its lively Spanish ambience and friendly, enthusiastic staff. The menu features a wide selection of dishes, from well-known tapas to more unusual and less conventional options. An excellent restaurant in which to enjoy a Spanish meal with friends.

Name: Domenica
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Domenica is the place to come to experience the bustling Jordaan neighbourhood. Whether you are dining outside on the terrace or inside at the bar of this modern bistro, there is always a lively atmosphere here. Authentic Italian seasonal dishes are served up with great skill and a proper sense of generosity. Think octopus with crispy skin and tender meat served alongside robust bell pepper and broccoletti. Owner Flavio pays tribute to his heritage with every vibrant plate. Be sure to check out his French and Italian wine selections too.

Name: Harry's
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This luxury brasserie is as cosmopolitan as it is vibrant. French flair characterises both the ambience and the cuisine. On the menu, international flavours and vegetarian options show that the chefs are keeping up with the times, but not at the expense of the golden rules of superior brasserie cuisine. The kitchen garden is a manifestation of their sustainable approach (more details on the website). Creative, local, seasonal: Harry's ticks all the boxes!

Name: Zilt & Zoet
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: The refreshed interior of this countryside villa combines the modern and the vintage, and is a great example of cosy Dutch ambience. The extensive set menu (a choice of three, four or five courses) is impressive. It is created by a chef who creates modern, lavish dishes from largely seasonal produce.

Name: Hofstede de Blaak
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The charm of this authentic English country house (1907), the classic half-timbering and elegant details, the peaceful surroundings – it is hard not to be moved by this setting. The chef loves working with fine ingredients and accentuates their finesse with contemporary seasonings. He is fond of combining diverse flavours to create elegant nuances. Be sure to try the excellent set menu.

Name: Umami by Han
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: The smart interior of Umami creates the right atmosphere for enjoying delicious dishes from all corners of Asia. The chef uses fresh ingredients prepared with a light touch, without sacrificing flavour. The favourable pricing and shared dining concept allows diners to try plenty of different dishes.

Name: De Voorburcht
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Step across the moat, traverse the medieval fortifications and look for the building with a sloping wall. This place certainly makes a magical first impression! Inside, this historical setting has been given a splendid makeover. Here, familiar ingredients are used to produce creative dishes. For instance, the chef combines skate and scallops in a dish reminiscent of a choucroute garnie. This is carefully considered and rich cuisine. At De Voorburcht, new life is breathed into classic fine dining.

Name: Wils Bakery Café
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This laid-back establishment has the feel of a traditional bistro but with a Scandinavian twist. As you walk in, you will see the baker kneading dough and the odd customer coming to buy bread. Make no mistake, though: this place has a great menu of well-crafted dishes. This Amsterdam version of a French bistro honours classics such as snails in herb butter, wood pigeon pithivier, foie gras and tarte Tatin. It is rich in flavour, generous and inspired, and the fantastic value for money is an added bonus.

Name: Nova
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Located on the edge of the Bergse Bos forest, and featuring a romantic terrace, a pontoon on the River Rotte and a cosy interior ambience, Nova is a delightful restaurant where chef Martin Vaandrager offers guests a menu with a varied choice. His contemporary cuisine is teeming with flavours, combining amusing ideas and impressive expertise in his dishes. A fine example of value for money… and pleasure!

Name: L'Auberge de Neercanne
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Come for lunch beneath the vaults of Château Neercanne's old chapel – you cannot fail to be impressed by this charming historical setting that has been given a stylish makeover. The terrace affords spectacular views. Chef Remmen serves up his own modern spin on classic dishes, with a focus on quality. Delicious produce is sourced from the region and their own kitchen garden. Cod poached in butter with a delicate white wine sauce, a traditionally prepared rich tarte Tatin: food lovers will be in seventh heaven.

Name: De Uitkijk
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Garden or park,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: With its magnificent natural setting, a lavender-filled terrace with a southern feel, and a restaurant with a country estate atmosphere, De Uitkijk offers a winning combination. Guests can watch the seasons change on the plate, with herbs from the chef's own garden. The elaborate dishes here are full of fresh flavour and boast lots of variety.

Name: Herberg Stadt Stevenswaert
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Marcus Schmidt’s inn sits on a picturesque tree-lined square, at the centre of an island flanked by a canal and the River Maas. The menu changes frequently, with seasonal produce – including vegetables from their garden – harmoniously coming together in creative dishes; the desserts in particular are delicious. The restaurant also offers a great selection of German wines.

Name: Kasteel Elsloo
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Dining in a castle makes for a special experience. The surrounding natural beauty and centuries-old arcades beneath which guests take their seats cannot fail to impress. This fabulous setting inspires the chef to work with respect for the region, the seasons and sustainability. French and Mediterranean flavours dominate the appealingly updated menu, which now features occasionally innovative dishes. Wine lovers will delight in the enticing selection of wines sold by the glass.

Name: De Grote Frederik Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: In this cosy local bistro you immediately get the feeling that guests always come first. This is typified by the excellent front-of-house hospitality of host Marjon, who is delighted to offer advice on a superb selection of wines to accompany chef Arnejan’s unique dishes, which are playful and unpretentious, yet which feature wonderful and surprising flavours.

Name: Bouwkunde
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: A dining experience at Bouwkunde is one to be savoured. After being welcomed by the cordial hostess, you can soak up the warm atmosphere of this charming restaurant. Diners will see that wine plays an important role here. The ostensibly classic and simple cuisine proves to be full of surprises and bold flavours. For example, a beurre blanc with a judicious squeeze of lemon enhances a beautifully translucent fillet of skrei. And all at great value for money!

Name: Umami by Han
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Renowned chef Han Ji has created a recipe for success at Umami, a bright, contemporary restaurant in which he concocts high-flying Asian fusion cuisine. The range of tasting sensations is suitably impressive, ranging from sweet to savoury and crunchy and smooth in intense dishes full of flavour and colour. An irresistibly exotic experience!

Name: De Beleving
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This convivial brasserie boasts all the attractions that you come to expect from a true Bib Gourmand address: a varied choice of enticing yet unfussy dishes that are generous and tasty. The chef does allow himself a few modern touches in his textures, although his cuisine is firmly focused on top-quality traditional ingredients such as haddock and Iberico pork presa. A splendid experience!

Name: Chef aan de Werf
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Enjoy a local beer as an aperitif before discovering Charly de Wijs' selection of international dishes, which feature local, subtly flavoured and sustainably sourced ingredients and draw on inspirations from around the globe. His winning combinations include options such as harissa with a fillet of fish, flatbread with carrots, tahini and feta. Just bear in mind that the chef serves up very generous portions! Housed in an old industrial building, this lively restaurant with its vintage decor is bound to have you coming back for more.

Name: Groenewoud
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: A few authentic decorative features remind us that despite its comfortable and even trendy feel we are in one of the oldest cafés in Nijmegen. The experienced chef at the helm conjures up generous French cuisine with the occasional subtle and surprising touch. Dishes cooked to perfection, a mastery of acidic flavours, intense sauces, plus excellent value for money!

Name: Senang
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Chinese dragon heads and lanterns, Japanese sake boxes, photos of owners Jonnie and Thérèse Boer taken during their travels across Asia: this colourful restaurant embodies a melting pot of impressions, and that certainly goes for the food, too. The menu features dishes that are full of flavour and fresh nuances from the Near, Middle and Far East. Chicken yakitori, ceviche, ramen, wonton… This is a truly wonderful culinary adventure. Be sure to try out the generous "Senang Table"!

Name: Moustique
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This highly modern restaurant in the centre of Haarlem is open almost every day. Here, you’ll find an extensive menu on which the chef showcases his experience through cuisine with an Asian inspiration and modern presentation, including a choice of vegetarian dishes and plenty of intense and authentic flavours. An impressive new arrival on the city’s food scene!

Name: Bovenmeester
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The head teacher might have left a while ago, but it is still evident that this place used to be a school building – even the children's coat hooks remain. Nowadays, this is a warm and welcoming restaurant with a cosy lounge area. French cuisine unveils all its generosity here. Think unctuous duck liver terrine served with toasted brioche; sea bream on a bread crust and a spicy sauce with saffron… Unbeatable value for money!

Name: Gastrobar Ster
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Terry Priem is a man with two faces – on the one hand, he’s the graphic artist (aka Ster) who, using aerosol paints, decorated the dining room; on the other, he’s a chef who demonstrates his artistic creativity in bold dishes which add subtle innovations to classic favourites. Original cocktails and excellent wines complete the picture.

Name: Boompjes
Cuisine: Country cooking, Cuisine from the Marches
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: The use of trees, plants and wood add a natural feel to the interior decor in this restaurant. Chef Volman is an ambassador for Dutch cuisine, giving produce grown in the vegetable garden a prominent place in his dishes. He likes to surprise his guests with the many different ways he prepares vegetables, offering an experience which showcases Dutch produce to the full!

Name: Tabkeaw
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: With its bamboo panelling, “pagoda” bar and typical landscapes on the walls, Tabkeaw’s interior is a journey in itself, with the lively buzz of the Wyck district providing the backdrop. The cuisine here is as traditional as the decor, featuring the authentic aromas of a tom kha kai, and the spicy harmony of fresh fish, curry and coconut. A culinary adventure!

Name: Spandershoeve
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Spandershoeve has been showcasing traditional Indonesian cuisine since 1972. Here, Anita watches over her grandson Timo, ensuring that authentic flavours are still to the fore, despite the chef’s eye for new trends – for example, he flavours his different dishes with his own special mixture of spices. An excellent choice for anyone wishing to experience true Indonesian hospitality.

Name: Promessa
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: “Food is art” is the motto of this relaxed restaurant, a mantra that is evident both in the trendy decor and on the plate. Aesthetics are key here yet without neglecting flavour, with impressive creativity and a variety of influences forming the basis for cuisine that is full of unique character. The varied choice of dishes will rouse immediate interest and ensure that you won’t leave disappointed!

Name: Red Orchids
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: If you have a hard time making decisions, we suggest you head to this intimate, trendy restaurant where the menu brings together Japanese, Chinese, Thai and Indonesian specialities. The chef always manages to add just the right dose of spices, creating dishes full of rich flavours and crisp textures. Subtle Asian cuisine at reasonable prices.

Name: Bij Mette
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Picturesque Linschoten is worth a visit in its own right, but be sure to look out for this beautifully converted grocery shop with its distinctive spiral staircase located a stone's throw from the leaning clock tower. This is old Dutch charm at its best! Chef-patron Carel Alberts welcomes you personally before showing off his expertise in the French classics. Wonderful local produce, intense sauces, respect for tradition: it all makes for an enjoyable culinary experience. Feel free to ask the chef about his French wine list – he will be happy to tell you more.

Name: Landgoed de Holtweijde
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: This estate is a beautiful example of classic rural elegance, offering fine views of the surrounding meadows. The chef employs lavish preparation methods and regional produce to create delightful dishes full of strong flavours. A trip here is well worth the effort!

Name: De Watergeus
Address: Simon van Capelweg 10, Noorden, 2431 AG, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: The walk alongside the canals affords a foretaste of what you can expect in this refurbished restaurant that enjoys a superb waterside location. The chef mixes classical recipes with generosity and modern textures. His culinary palette is diverse and intriguing and the formula is highly recommended. Enquire about overnight stays and boat trips (with a picnic basket) on the Nieuwkoopse Plassen.

Name: De Knip
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: An idyllic spot on the Vliet canal with a superb view of the glistening water. The original, well-balanced dishes are equally easy on the eye, as well as being delicious and full of flavour.

Name: De Witte Gans
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This rustic restaurant is a favourite pit stop for walkers, cyclists and food lovers. The terrace is one of its main draws; another is the superb Bib Gourmand-awarded menu, which features local produce, nods to the East, and vegetarian options. The creative chef works his ingredients hard and prides himself on the presentation of his dishes.

Name: Umami by Han
Address: Kleine Berg 57 H, Eindhoven, 5611 JT, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: If you find it difficult to decide what to eat, then you will enjoy the shared dining concept in this modern Asian restaurant. It boasts an impressive selection of dishes at very good value. Each course consists of 2 small dishes prepared in Japanese, Chinese, Thai, Indonesian or Vietnamese fashion, with a Western twist.

Name: Umami by Han
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The trendy, modern interior with bright colours immediately catches the eye, but the trump card of this restaurant is its rock solid concept… a range of Asian dishes with a French twist from which you can choose your heart’s desire. A wonderful journey of discovery at amazing prices!

Name: De Beejekurf
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Mathijs Jacobs is a truly ambitious chef. If he’s brought a deer by a local huntsman or freshly harvested vegetables by a local farmer, his eyes light up. Whether he decides to cook his ingredients in a salt crust, grill them on the barbecue or use them in an ice-cream, he never lacks in inspiration and the result is always delicious!

Name: Asian Glories
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: The Peking duck that you see hanging in the kitchen are one of the highlights on the attractive menu at this restaurant, while the pancakes that accompany the dish are prepared in front of you. The culinary traditions of Canton and Szechuan are to the fore here, served in elegant yet unfussy dishes which are full of generous flavours. A real feast!

Name: Hof van Herstal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Hof van Herstal is an elegant restaurant with a decor that does full justice to its rich history. This establishment has bags of character. Chef Martin Bruggeman takes great pride in his work, proving every day that he is a true master of his trade. He slaughters his own game (venison is a must here!) and is happy to make judicious wine recommendations. His generous sauces are the best evidence of his culinary skill.

Name: Tante Kee
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: The back and forth of the ferry bringing guests to this magnificent establishment makes for a wonderful spectacle in the evenings. Inside, the decor has been given a makeover and creates a modern yet intimate atmosphere, with the surrounding water playing an integral part in the overall look. The intriguing flavour combinations in the modern, occasionally oriental dishes provide the basis for an exciting culinary experience. Think an exotic/fresh/zesty combination of mango, passion fruit, coconut and fried rice noodles. Dinner at Tante Kee is quite an adventure!

Name: Publique
Address: Anna Paulownaplein 4, The Hague, 2518 BK, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: The corner building where vintage and contemporary design merge with beautiful stained-glass windows is the place to be. This relaxed little place is popular with locals, who come for the market-fresh cuisine. Chef Plat gives vegetables (extensive vegetable menu available) pride of place in fresh dishes which he likes to give a Mediterranean twist. His choices are sometimes rather daring, but always hit the mark, like the amazing shallot and white wine vinaigrette with sweet/salty sea urchin he serves to accompany monkfish.

Name: De Basiliek
Address: Korte Houtstraat 4a, The Hague, 2511 CD, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: With its trendy, lively atmosphere, colourful decor and pretty terrace at the front, De Basiliek has a decidedly convivial atmosphere. The tempting menu features fresh Mediterranean dishes full of generous flavours, with vegetables playing an important role. The chef draws on his culinary expertise to deliver exciting cuisine brimming with clever combinations. The impressive wine list proposes plenty of options by the glass and in half-bottles. Excellent value for money!

Name: Brasserie BovendeRivieren
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: From this floating brasserie, you can enjoy spectacular views of the marina, the Merwede river and the Biesbosch nature and water reserve. In this delightful setting enjoy imaginative dishes with cosmopolitan influences and typical specialities created by a skilful and enthusiastic chef.

Name: Sukade
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Produce from all over the world, including succade (candied citrus peel), was once traded in this monumental warehouse dating back to 1860. Today, it is incorporated into contemporary cuisine served in an impressive setting that takes full advantage of its location on Stoombootkade (grab a table on the waterfront terrace if possible!). The dishes draw on influences from around the globe; succulent poussin breast, for instance, is given a twist with Asian spices. The chef finds creative ways to put vegetables and fruit in the limelight. The lunch and finger food options are slightly simpler, the evening menu more elaborate.

Name: Tapisco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: For centuries this was a famous bookshop; today this restaurant full of character and with a Mediterranean flair is regarded as the place to go for Spanish tapas and Portuguese petiscos. The experienced chef creates small typical dishes prepared with quality produce, not too complex but full of flavour, that take guests on an incredible Mediterranean journey.

Name: Vineum
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: The wine list is the heart and soul of this warm, aptly named restaurant with an intimate urban garden to the rear. Owner David van Steenderen is a top sommelier who is constantly discovering new wines, while the same quality is mirrored in the cuisine, which features attractively presented dishes full of flavour. Classic cuisine, original ideas and real expertise act as the perfect complement to the fine wines.

Name: Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This charming bistro occupies the front room of the farm that is also home to its older Michelin-starred sibling De Gieser Wildeman. The cuisine and name are perfectly matched: traditional, generous and quite simply delicious. One of the highlights on the menu is the crispy duck leg with cabbage. The attractive prices here are as tempting as the cooking!

Name: Le Vieux Jean
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Chef Robert-Jan Polman produces classic cuisine his way. Authentic flavours, precise preparation and strong stocks and sauces all combine to reveal his experience. The addition of an individual touch further elevates the harmony of flavours. The wine list is impressive and not to be missed.

Name: La Fleurie
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Connoisseurs will be in their element in this stylish restaurant, where chef Verbruggen offers a refined menu showcasing contemporary international dishes and ingredients. His cuisine, which features distinctive, rich sauces, is sophisticated and generous, allowing the chef’s passion and experience to shine through.

Name: De Lindeboom New Style
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: De Lindeboom boasts plenty of style both in terms of the charm of the building (1760), its typical Limburg hospitality, and its varied menu. Chef Jan-Willem demonstrates his preference for Mediterranean freshness and international inspiration on a menu ranging from traditional sole to vegetarian dishes, bringing together all the ingredients needed to delight his guests.

Name: Pouwe
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Walter and Vivian Pouwe bring flavours from around the globe to the sleepy town of Hoeven. In their modern lounge-style restaurant, ingredients such as yuzu, tandoori spices and vadouvan are incorporated into creative dishes that pack a punch. For instance, bavette steak really comes into its own in a Mediterranean concoction featuring an interplay with pesto and aubergine caviar.
