Description: In this white house in the heart of a village in the suburbs of Toulouse, the chef serves up generous traditional cuisine, including dishes such as fillet of duck with a spicy reduction or tournedos of beef with morel mushrooms. For dessert, a crunchy strawberry tartlet with home-made pistachio ice cream. In fine weather, enjoy your meal on the shady terrace.

Name: Au Pont du Corbeau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Experience local gastronomic specialities and traditional decor (Renaissance features, posters) in this restaurant next door to the Musée Alsacien, with its displays of popular art.

Name: Le Muratore
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: When it was established in 1870, this place with a superbly preserved Belle Époque decor was named after Mr Muratore, a liquor - maker and confectioner. It is now run by the engaging Marc Serres, who proposes delightful cuisine, starring fish from the lake (Arctic char, perch etc). Finally, let's not forget the gorgeous terrace beneath the boughs of the lime trees.

Name: Terrone
Address: Fort St. Angelo, Birgu Waterfront, Birgu, BRG 1734, Malta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Having started life a short 'pop up' down the road, Terrone is now settled in a waterfront residency within the walls of Fort St Angelo – and a spot on the terrace here is a must. Carefully prepared Maltese and Southern Italian influenced dishes burst with freshness; the Maltese lemon tart is a speciality.

Name: Rubino
Address: 53 Old Bakery Street, Valletta, VLT 1454, Malta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This sweet little bistro started life in 1906 as a confectionery shop, serving, among other things, cassata Siciliana – which it still offers today. Sit in one of three cosy, traditional rooms and receive hands-on service from the owner. The blackboard menu lists classic Maltese and Italian dishes.

Name: Grain Street
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace
Description: Situated on the main pedestrianised street in the centre of town, this restaurant with an attractive outdoor dining space serves simple, informal Mediterranean cuisine. Dishes include lasagne with squid, cuttlefish ink and nduja sausage as well as delicious desserts such as lemon meringue tart with olive oil and thyme ice cream.

Name: Commando
Address: Misraħ Iz-Żjara tal-Papa, Mellieħa, MLH 1080, Malta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This warmly run, honest little restaurant has been family owned since the 1930s; its name refers back to the time when the current chef’s grandfather provided hospitality to the Royal Marines. Fresh local ingredients are accurately prepared to create satisfying dishes with subtle modern twists.

Name: Specht
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Discover Card,JCB,Maestro,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This restaurant in a little side street in the city centre is a wonderfully cosy setting for a pleasant tête-à-tête or meal among friends. Diners can expect delicious traditional Viennese cuisine prepared using local ingredients. The pretty interior combining modern design, wooden floors, dark green wall panelling and partially vaulted ceilings creates a warm atmosphere. There is a U-Bahn station conveniently located close by.

Name: Mochi
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: A lively, informal restaurant serving authentic Japanese cuisine with some more modern twists, at very moderate prices. You can watch the chefs at work, preparing sushi rolls, yakitori or gyu don. At lunchtime, the food is served in bowls; in the evening the presentation is a bit more elaborate. Tables are much sought after, so book early! No reservation possible at lunchtime.

Name: Meierei im Stadtpark
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: One floor below the Reitbauer’s gourmet restaurant, you’ll find another upmarket eatery. Alongside some 150 wonderfully matured cheeses, it boasts delicious classics like Wiener schnitzel of suckling calf. Or perhaps you’d prefer a whole Arctic char or some venison goulash? Attractive terrace facing the Stadtpark.

Name: Vestibül
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: With a penchant for seasonal and regional produce, this restaurant serves flavoursome culinary delights such as freshwater fish dishes or classics like Wiener schnitzel. The imposing historical building, which also houses the famous Burgtheater, makes for a unique location with a stylish interior that has a typically Viennese feel with its striking columns and gorgeous stuccowork.

Name: Gasthof Auerhahn
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Run with great dedication, this friendly, family-owned restaurant is located at a slight remove from the city centre, close to the train station, but it's well worth making the detour for the excellent food – their appealing range of dishes includes the delicious Topfenknödel (curd dumplings). Dine in the inviting interior or out on the beautiful verdant terrace. For overnight stays, there are pleasant, well-kept guestrooms.

Name: MAST Weinbistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Set in a historical town house, this trendy place is a winning combination of modern wine bar and upscale bistro. It is very popular for its great food, is made with seasonal ingredients sourced from local producers – and at fantastic value for money. Organic and biodynamic wines are recommended to accompany your choice of dishes. There is an appealing outdoor dining area, too.

Name: Carnozet
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Garden or park,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Tastefully done out in a modern take on Alpine style, this restaurant provides both excellent food and friendly service. The menu features an appealing selection of seasonal dishes, mostly made from locally sourced produce. We highly recommend the grey cattle goulash with Walser Knöpfle (similar to spaetzle).

Name: ONYX
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: What was once the bar on the sixth floor of the DO & CO Hotel in the avant-garde Haas Building has been transformed into a trendy restaurant with a lounge feel and large floor-to-ceiling windows that afford a breathtaking view of St Stephen's Cathedral. Interesting Asian and Japanese dishes are served for sharing – including sushi and sashimi and specialities from the Robata grill.

Name: Woracziczky
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: Diners are given a warm welcome In this pleasingly informal inn (pronounced "Vorashitsky"). Both its laid-back atmosphere and Viennese cuisine are a hit, with house specialities such as beef tartare with avocado, or Tafelspitz (boiled veal) served with a creamy chanterelle sauce. The reasonably priced lunchtime set menu, which changes daily, is especially popular.

Name: Iva New Balkan Cuisine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: There’s great value to be had at this semi-basement level restaurant with a pared-back modern look. The extensive menu covers everything from breakfast to street food, and much more. Traditional Balkan recipes are subtly refined yet remain wholesome and comforting. They favour using smaller producers. A small, yet attractive, wine list is available and a smart service will welcome you.

Name: Busarin Cuisine
Address: 133 Rattanakosin Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Busarin, the new sister restaurant of Magnolia Café, has high ceilings, a collection of chinaware and leather green sofa booths that contrast with the light pink walls. When you dine here, it’s like being welcomed into Chef Noi’s home. They serve northern-Thai based on family recipes with noodles and roti instead of rice. The standout is a streaky pork that’s braised in a hung lay curry for two days and emits a powerful aroma of ginger and spices.

Name: O Pochana
Address: 252/21 Prasoet Som Road, Soi Wilai Sena, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This rickety but charming little wooden house that backs onto the River Noi is the perfect local pitstop. Their Thai menu is prepared in an open kitchen with a charcoal stove, mostly comprising local fish and river prawns, caught just behind the restaurant – as fresh as it can be. The wok produces a wonderful charcoal flavour in the stir-fried salt and pepper river prawns. Meanwhile, the deep-fried sheatfish with sweet fish sauce is succulent, with a crispy texture.

Name: Salaloy
Address: 52/2 Wiset Road, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The focus of this casual Rawai Beach eatery is on fresh, expertly cooked seafood. Among the highlights are shrimp paste dip served with vegetables, and soft-boiled wing shells and deep-fried Sillago fish with turmeric powder – dishes to inspire diners to return and explore the rest of the menu. The outdoor eating area, opposite the main dining room, is a well-shaded and relaxing spot to enjoy a meal. Be early or some seafood ingredients may run out.

Name: Aunt Aoy Kitchen
Address: 377 2 Chiang Rai Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The décor is simple, with a display of photos and messages on post-it notes from customers gone by. Aunt Aoy spent much of her career cooking in hotel kitchens. Her expertise is realised in the fluffy yet crispy Chef Omelette with stir-fried minced pork, salted egg and pork crackling.

Name: Pa Pu Boat Noodles
Address: 1 36 Mu 5 Chao Chet, Sena, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Octogenarian Pa Pu is the talent behind the recipes in this simple shop next to the local rice field. The signature boat noodles with shredded chicken or pork and soft eggs are a delicacy. There’s no need to add any condiments; Pa Pu produces the perfect blend of flavours every time.

Name: Dan Chicken Rice (San Sai)
Address: 45 Mu 3, Old San Sai Road (Opposite to PT Petrol Station, San Sai Branch), San Sai Noi, Chiang Mai, 50210, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: For over 20 years this local favourite has been serving tasty, wallet-friendly chicken rice, first in Sam-Yaek Market in San Sai and now at this larger branch on Old San Sai Road. Show up early, both to beat the crowds and because the food invariably runs out before closing time.

Name: Som Tum Jinda
Address: 63/1 Phichitrangsan Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only
Description: Chef-owner Jinda is a specialist in somtum dishes. She first plied her trade back in 1974 in the local university before moving downtown. The Isan-style spicy fish maw with bamboo shoot salad has a nice balance of herbs and its powerful aroma is punctuated by the intensity of the Tiliacora juice. The signature, somtum with crispy catfish, dispenses an impressive tang. Somtum Jinda is also famous over the border in Lao where they have another branch.

Name: Pae Araya
Address: Rim Khong Road, Khong Chiam, Ubon Ratchathani, 34220, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only,Great view
Description: Where the Mekong and Mun Rivers meet, this floating restaurant, whose name means ‘noble raft,’ serves central Thai and Isan fare featuring fish from both rivers. The Tom Yum redtail catfish and local roe served with herbs are both flavourful and recommended. They and everything else on the menu come with cooling river breezes and gentle undulations from passing boats. Arrive early for dinner to catch sunset views over the river and the Laotian landscape beyond.

Name: Pa Lek Boat Noodles
Address: Bang Lan Road (opposite to Maha That temple), Tha Wasukri, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This third-generation family street food spot has been selling flavourful boat noodles for more than five decades. The years of experience show in the boat noodles’ delicious broth, which demonstrates good balancing of flavours. Among the great value dishes, the pork or beef boat noodles are a highlight; the dry tom yum-style egg noodles with pork are also recommended. The owners’ friendly hospitality adds to the appeal, so it’s no surprise there’s such a big crowd at lunch.

Name: A Pong Mae Sunee
Address: 99 Soi Soon Uthit, Yaowarat Road, Talad Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Selling just the local snack Khanom A Pong, this street food stall was set up by Sunee more than 50 years ago. Now joined by her son Pui, she cooks her delicious coconut crepes in mini woks on charcoal stoves. What makes this delicacy so special is the extremely light, crispy texture mixed with a soft, slightly gooey inside – combined with a noticeable sweetness and rich coconut milk taste, it’s a guaranteed hit. Plenty of customers have caught on and Sunee always sells out before closing time, so go early to avoid disappointment.

Name: Khanom Bueang Wan Phueng Noi (Chok Chai 4)
Address: Chok Chai 4 Soi 54 Yaek 5, Lat Phrao, Bangkok, 10230, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This shop is entirely devoted to the delicious dessert known as Khanom Bueang. These crepes are crispy and topped with just the right ratio of aromatic coconut cream, sweet egg floss, and young coconut slices. Be sure to arrive near opening time to avoid a wait.

Name: Roti Chaofa
Address: 44 Chaofa Road, Talad Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: For over 35 years, the locals have flocked to Roti Chaofa for Thai-Muslim breakfasts, curries and Thai-style chicken biryani. The crisp, golden-brown rotis with a fluffy inner, are nicely salted and enjoyed with sweets or savouries. The tangy, juicy Beef Massaman curry is delightful.

Name: Takola
Address: Devasom Khao Lak Beach Resort & Villas, 79 Mu 3, Khuk Khak, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82220, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Valet parking,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in lush gardens by Khuekkhak beach, Takola is named after the Takua Pa city’s former title when it was a major spice trading port. Their ancient and original cooking methods produce intense traditional and southern Thai flavours. The fried fish fillet is a large seabass topped with a tamarind-based, sweet and sour sauce that works wonderfully with the freshness of the fish and the basil’s fragrance. The Thai crab dip with crab meat also gets the nod.

Name: Burapa
Address: 26 Soi Sukhumvit 11, Khlong Toei Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: This Orient Express-themed restaurant aims to take diners on a journey from east to north-east Thailand via flavoursome cooking that joins culinary elements from Isan and the province of Trat. The ground floor is designed to look like a luxury train bar – perfect for enjoying one of their many signature cocktails – then the 1st and 2nd floors resemble the business and first-class carriages respectively. The well-priced dishes use recipes from the owner’s mother and quality produce from Eastern Thailand. Booking is essential.

Name: Por. Pochaya
Address: 654-656 Wisut Kasat Road, Ban Pantom, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: For over half a century, unwavering quality and rare dishes have kept loyal fans visiting this traditional Thai-Chinese spot, which is now run by the third generation of the same family. Among the top-sellers are crab omelette and stir-fried beef with cumin leaves. Crowds are to be expected, so make sure you book to avoid disappointment. It’s closed on weekends and holidays.

Name: 100 Mahaseth (Si Phraya)
Address: 100 Mahaseth Road, Si Phraya, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This nose-to-tail inspired offal restaurant serves elevated Isan fare made from quality ingredients sourced from local Thai farmers. The chef puts great care into balancing flavours and presenting attractive plates – and this is evident with dishes like the aged beef tongue and the fried offal chips. Guests are served in a dining room that matches the rustic with the industrial; a dry-ageing meat cabinet adds a modern touch. Don’t forget to check the blackboard for aged steak specials.

Name: Krua Kampan Khao Yai
Address: Route no. 3052, Mu Si, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30130, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: The kampan (Thai for sailing ship) is an antique boat at the heart of the restaurant that has been transferred from Ayutthaya. The menu, designed by the owner, uses classic Thai recipes packed with intense flavours. The minced pork spare ribs with betel leaf is a signature dish; every meaty mouthful contains crispy cartilage in a spicy curry. Meanwhile, the red curry rice field snail with coconut milk is brought to life by the enlivening aroma of the betel leaf.

Name: Lab Somphit
Address: 169 Jant Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang,, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Granny Somphit has prepared her food from scratch every day for more than five decades. This is flavourful Isan food at its best – a lovely balance of intense local spices and Thai herbs. The carefully selected offal cuts are particularly fresh. The signature Isan spicy calf beef salad is delightful; tender meaty slices that are beautifully seasoned with a smoky aroma of rice powder that adds a crispy texture. The homemade beef sausage, fermented beef and pork are also good.

Name: Khaotom Chedi
Address: Rodjana Road, Phai Ling, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This well-known street food seller is an ideal spot for locals looking for a late-night bite. Check with the owner for the special ingredients on the day’s menu; the seafood is especially good, as the owner visits the market himself. Stir-fried dishes are a real highlight – try the shrimps with salt and pepper, or the seasonal clams with roasted chilli.

Name: Ket O Cha
Address: Soi Phatthanakan 53, Suan Luang, Bangkok, 10250, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Perennially crowded, this local favourite has a legacy spanning several decades. It specialises in aromatic noodle soup, with a peppery fragrance and mild sweet and salty taste. Diners can choose from tender slow-cooked beef, juicy blanched beef slices, and bouncy homemade beef balls.

Name: Khok Kloi Bami Tom Yam Khai
Address: 6 10, Khok Kloi, Takua Thung, Phang-Nga, 82140, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Their fresh tom yum noodles are accompanied by piquant spicy and sour flavours; dry or in an intense broth. They’re known for impressively sized portions at reasonable prices. The soft minced pork and healthy liver have a beautiful scent of fresh lime juice and chilli in a sweet broth.

Name: Kin Lookdeaw
Address: 35 Mu 9 Tambon Tha Chao Sanuk, Tha Ruea, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13130, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: The name of the restaurant asks guests to ‘focus on eating’ (Kin Lookdeaw) at this quaint house with an open-air pavilion above a serene pond. The chefs, veterans in the kitchen, cook simple Thai dishes and make their own chilli paste from scratch. The regular pounding of pestle in mortar reverberates through nature’s own soundtrack of birds and insects. Try the deep-fried boneless red tilapia with garlic and stir-fried green curry with clown featherback fish balls.

Name: Bangkok Bold Kitchen (Central Embassy)
Address: LGF, Central Embassy, 1031 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: Word-of-mouth inspired Chef Nhoi to take the leap from cooking studio in the old town to opening a restaurant in the city centre. Her aim is to preserve the heritage of Thai taste that’s ‘basic and bold’ with creative twists. Check out the unique stir-fried pork and shrimp, hummingbird flowers, fish sauce and scrambled eggs. And the spicy salted beef in coconut cream is tender with balanced flavours, enlivened by fresh shallots and bird's eye chillies.

Name: Fried Banana Rama 5
Address: 116 Soi 1, Bang Si Thong, Bang Kruai, Nonthaburi, 11130, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Every day, in a small alley in Nonthaburi, a long queue forms for the deep-fried battered banana with its crispy golden-brown texture. A special machine removes the excess oil to ensure the crispy finish. Other treats include taro and potato, and a deep-fried potato dough ball.

Name: Jao Nai Fish Ball (Ekkachai)
Address: 38/132 Bang Khae Road, Bang Khae, Bangkok, 10160, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This long-standing street food spot sits in an old townhouse and attracts many diners with its flavoursome fish balls in noodle soup. As it’s freshly made to order and regularly busy, you may have to be patient for your food – but it’s well worth the wait. The homemade seafood elements like fish balls, fish wontons and fish sausage slices are of good quality and provide a great umami flavour to the soup.

Name: Somsak Pu Ob (Charoen Rat)
Address: Soi Charoen Rat 1, Khlong San, Bangkok, 10600, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This cart serves some of the best steamed crabs or prawns on glass noodles at wallet-friendly prices. Make sure you stir the noodles to soak up the tasty juices. It has a few branches, but this is where it all started. Come early or the wait will be long.

Name: Kin Kub Koi
Address: 83/3 Phuttha Monthon Sai 2 Road, Sala Thammasop, Thawi Watthana, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: The chef-owner here knows seafood. Not only does her family run a wholesale seafood business, but she also ran the previous incarnation of this place in Samut Sakhon for years before moving it here. The results are skilfully cooked dishes made from choice seafood, like standouts grilled river prawns and stir-fried crab with bitter beans and shrimp paste. Two dining zones (with and without AC) are available; both face a leafy courtyard.

Name: Madam Pahtehh (Tumruaj)
Address: 34/1-3 Tumruaj Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Chef-owner Madame Mui merges cuisines from five countries—Vietnam, Thailand, Laos, France and China—to forge popular breakfast and lunch fare, including her signature sandwich, which features pâté. The setting is a wooden house with vintage vibes, with a sandwich and coffee-making setup in the middle, from where the chef serves and explains dishes with a smile. The Vietnamese sandwich set is a must and comes with three different sandwiches served with pork pâté.

Name: Roti Sai Mai Mae Pom (Mother's Branch)
Address: 51/1 Mu 2, Uthong Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Opened in 1985, this street food spot sits inside a wooden building near Preedee Thamrong Bridge and specialises in roti with candy floss. The freshly made plain and sesame rotis are thin, soft and based on a traditional recipe. They pair wonderfully with cloud-like cotton candy that provides all the necessary sweetness with a light touch. Due to their popularity, orders are taken in advance only – pre-order dates are announced on Facebook.

Name: Joong Borikan
Address: Prasoet Som Road, Sena, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: There’s a reason why this unpretentious-looking restaurant has been highly regarded among Thailand’s food connoisseurs for over eight decades: it serves appetising local river prawns and fish cooked using old-school techniques. Among their best dishes are fried river prawns with salt and spicy grilled river prawn salad, thanks to the impressive flavours, textures and aromas. A history-filled conversation with the owner is equally delightful.

Name: Konchong Konprung
Address: 109 Soi Inthamara 3, Sutthisan Road, Sam Sen Nai, Bangkok, 10400, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The menu at this Chinese comfort food spot traces back to family gatherings the owners attended in their youth. Cherished recipes from those gatherings, plus fresh creations from the chef, are served in a warm, inviting space accented with a homely décor and nostalgic Chinese posters. A highlight is the pickled plum and garlic soup with minced pork balls, which brings together enticing herbal aromas and complex flavours with satisfyingly textured pork balls.

Name: Here Klae Pork Satay
Address: Pamaprao Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Now run by the third-generation grill master, this humble shophouse is over nine decades old and is one of Ayutthaya’s most beloved spots for charcoal-grilled pork satay. The skewered meat is well-marinated and aromatic from the nine spices used. Do try the pork offal – it’s perfect with the accompanying peanut sauce. Since the pandemic, they have been serving their food for take-away only and run as a cash-only business – so come prepared.

Name: Maan Muang
Address: 165/7 Soi Ramkhamhaeng 112 Ramkhamhaeng Road, Saphan Sung, Bangkok, 10240, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This lovely wooden Lanna house with rustic charm will magically whisk you off to Chiang Mai. The dining area under the raised house is decorated with traditional Thai wooden furniture and earthenware. The staff too are dressed in Northern Thai fashions and speak in a regional dialect. But it’s the dizzying array of dishes and beautiful blend of northern ingredients that tops it off. The Thai curry soup with pork ribs and jackfruit hits the spot.

Name: Nong Rim Klong
Address: 51 Ekkamai 23 Alley, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: This former canal-side food stall found new life as a simply decorated shophouse spread across two floors. A semi-open kitchen lets you glimpse the chefs as they work on intensely flavoured, great value dishes based on prime quality ingredients. The sea bass tom yum soup has a wonderful herby flavour and a generous portion of fish, while the rather unique crab omelette offers fresh flavours and a natural sweetness.

Name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
Address: 29/1 Ratchaphruek Road, Chang Puek, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Believed by many to be the world’s favourite curry, this affordable street stall serves the famous khao soi. Their signature dish hits the spot with intense herbs, rich curry paste and tender braised beef. Also, don’t miss the vermicelli rice with northern Thai pork curry and tomato.

Name: Nai Ngieb (Phutthamonthon Sai 4)
Address: 125/21 Mu 6, Phutthamonthon Sai 4 Road, Salaya, Phutthamonthon, Nakhon Pathom, 73170, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only
Description: One of the best eateries in the area for noodle soup lovers, where the bouncy, MSG-free fish balls are made the traditional way from mackerel, yellowtail amberjack and wolf herring. The tom yum soup stands out; and the fish noodles are perfect for low-carb dieters as they go well with any soup.

Name: Mook Manee
Address: 1120 Wiset Road, Rawai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Located near Rawai beach, Mook Manee stands out for its array of live seafood for diners to choose from, from squid and tiger prawns to a variety of crabs and 3kg Phuket rainbow lobster. The restaurant holds up to 300, but the best seats have views of the vibrant seafood market trading outside. The menu highlights include Tom Yum soup, Phuket lobster with spicy dip and stir-fried mantis shrimps with garlic and chilli. A wooden terrace on the beach is also available.

Name: Roe Dang
Address: 55/15 Mu 1, Phet Kasem Road, Lam Kaen, Thai Mueang, Phang-Nga, 82210, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Roe Dang has basic furnishings with a polished cement floor, wooden tables and plastic chairs. The dishes, too, are modest looking. But locals recognise the great cooking technique and regularly pack the restaurant to enjoy fresh seafood and the nice balance of flavours. Our picks are the signature stir-fried crab meat with spring onion, and soup with sea bass, young coconut shoots and local vegetables. The wall of celebrity photos is testament to its popularity.

Name: Tune In Garden
Address: 139 Mu 3, Pong Yang, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is owned by the late National Artist of Thailand and his wife. She cooks delicious homestyle fare drawn from a cookbook she wrote based on her mother-in-law’s recipes. First-timers are served a fixed-price menu; returners can order from the cookbook. Roasted pork ribs with cabbage and fermented pork with fermented bean curd relish stand out. Booking is required.

Name: Hok Kee Lao
Address: 19 Senarat Road, Bang Nai Si, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The food at legendary Thai-Chinese Hok Kee Lao, beloved for four decades, is flavourful, affordable and the perfect banquet. The favourite is deep-fried shrimp rolls wrapped in tofu skins with pineapple. The southern Thai spicy and sour curry soup with seabass and coconut shoots is thick and tangy, while the chicken slices in their skins with morning glory, all steamed, are simply delicious – tender, juicy and a deep green colour that confirms freshness.

Name: Nai Mong Hoi Thod
Address: 539 Phlapphla Chai Road, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Chinatown is iconic for its street food and this is one of the most popular stands. Mr Mong has served Hoi Thod (fried oyster) for over 30 years. It’s only small and he’s busy at lunch, but the shellfish are well selected and fresh, and the fried mussels have a great crunch.

Name: K. Panich
Address: 431-433 Tanao Road, Sao Ching Cha, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This legendary shop by the Grand Palace uses an 80-year-old family recipe passed down the generations. The mango sticky rice is perfectly cooked and certainly hits the sweet spot. Meanwhile, the steamed sticky rice with banana or taro is succulent and accentuated by the coconut milk.

Name: Polo Fried Chicken (Soi Polo)
Address: 137/1-3 Soi Sanamkhli, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Run by the same family for three generations, this restaurant (actually two outlets in the same alley – one with air conditioning, one without) has been serving up affordable, delicious food for over 50 years. The draw is the deservedly famous fried chicken topped with deep-fried garlic, made from a secret southern-style recipe created by the first-generation owner. The generous som tam with seafood is also highly recommended, with a good balance between sweet and sour flavours.

Name: Guay Tiew Khua Gai Suanmali
Address: 266/1 Soi Thewi Worayat, Luang Road, Wat Dhebsirin, Pom Prap Sattru Phai (Khlang Hospital Intersection), Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Family-owned and managed, this small stall’s hallmark dish is roasted chicken noodles. The noodles have a crispy, non-oily texture and are rich in seasoning aromas. Khao Lao Haeng, the dry option, is served with a crispy omelette, chicken and squid: highly recommended.

Name: Go-Ang Kaomunkai Pratunam (Petchaburi 30)
Address: 960-962 Soi Phetchaburi 30, Makkasan, Ratchathewi, Bangkok, 10400, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This humble chicken and rice stall has drawn a devoted fan base of locals and in-the-know visitors for more than 60 years. The aromatic rice is cooked with chicken oil and perfectly matches the tender and juicy chicken. The soybean with ginger and chilli dipping sauce is the flavourful addition.

Name: Roti Sai Mai Abeedeen-Pranom Sangaroon
Address: Uthong Road, Pratu Chai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Much has changed in the last 70-plus years, but not at this popular place for roti with candy floss across from Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya Hospital. The same family still makes the same flawless rotis with fluffy candy floss that they always have. The aromatic green roti made with pandan leaf is particularly great, providing a proper gooey texture. The demand’s as high as it always has been too, so lines are common.

Name: Samlor
Address: 1076 Charoen Krung Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Samlor means ‘tricycle’ in Thai and a traditional one hangs outside this cosy restaurant. Inside the loft-style space, chef Napol creates flavoursome, well-presented elevated Thai cuisine inspired by local street food with specially selected ingredients. They also have a la carte menu, including cut of the day (main course of the day) and catch of the day (fish menu of the day) available. Guests need to check with the chef at the spot what they specially have on that day. The seasonal tasting menu (advance booking required) is also delightful.

Name: Krua Khun Nid
Address: 64 Soi Wat Pa Non Niwet, Udon Dussadi Road, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This spacious Isan restaurant has been a mainstay of local family dining for over 40 years. Known for fresh ingredients and sharing portions of both seasonal dishes and enduring classics, highlights include deep-fried salted carp and Lab Pa Tong, or fish cakes grilled in banana leaves. For more recommendations, the friendly staff are happy to make suggestions. Drinks are available from the café in front and homemade items like chilli paste are sold in the shop.

Name: Huan Soontaree
Address: 208 Patan Road, Pa Tan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Soontaree Vechanont doesn’t just own “Soontaree’s House” – the singer also performs here nightly. Set on the Ping River in an open-air, Lanna-style building with more tables outside, this charming restaurant can accommodate up to 350 guests. Among the Northern Thai cooking they serve is their signature boneless murrel fish stuffed with pork. It’s a creative dish, with the well-seasoned sausage proving suitably fragrant and spicy.

Name: Khon Kaen Grilled Pork Neck
Address: 77/4 Glang Muang Road, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This grilled pork spot is among the most popular street places in Khon Kaen, and its grilled pork neck with rice is the reason why. The tender, sweet and salty marinated meat perfectly matches the accompanying spicy tamarind sauce. Also recommended are the spicy salad and soup.

Name: Leng Yentafo
Address: Glang Muang Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: When Mr. Leng left Bangkok’s Chinatown for Khon Kaen in 1984, he brought a secret recipe for Yentafo, or pink noodle soup, and set up shop. His signature dish, which features toothsome noodles, fresh fishballs, shrimp balls and fish wontons, and a tasty broth, continues to delight.

Name: Penlaos
Address: 56 Mu 17 Thanaratch Road, Mu Si, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30450, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Penlaos started over a decade ago as a street stall. Today, it’s an altogether different operation offering a quality menu in a building with high ceilings surrounded by lush gardens and views of the mountains. They serve Isan food using homemade condiments – the spicy catfish salad is a must. The Laosian style spicy mushroom soup is made with Tiliacora juice, seasonal mushrooms and gourd which adds a natural sweetness. The Thai coconut milk custard rounds off your meal nicely.

Name: Krua Suwimol
Address: 1229 9 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: This simple, open-air restaurant serves Thai-Chinese fare. The food is distinctive for its simply cooking techniques yet quality dishes with extra-fresh ingredients and intense flavours. They offer a fantastic range, including several seafood and made-to-order options. The stir-fried crab with curry paste is a must for the succulently sweet crab meat. The spicy salad with mimosa is great too – the water mimosa are carefully selected, steamed and topped with a salad rich in Thai herbs.

Name: Indochine
Address: 170 Sappasit Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The name Indochine is derived from the connection between two countries - Vietnamese family recipes have been served here for over 50 years. And family is the key to this popular business where everyone pitches in. The restaurant boasts vintage décor, using old wooden furniture and tables made from defunct sewing machines. The Vietnamese rice cake with grille pork is highly recommended, while the signature namnueng comes in a big basket with a mix of fresh local vegetables.

Name: Go Neng (Wichayanon)
Address: 77 Praisani Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Go Neng has been serving deep-fried dough sticks for almost four decades. No matter what shape they take – crocodile, dinosaur, dragon or elephant – each one boasts the same puffy perfection and crispy texture. Other bites, such as the deep-fried bun and fried whole-wheat dough are also great.

Name: Khanom Chin Pa Son
Address: 3 Borirak Bamrung Road, Tai Chang, Mueang Phang-nga, Phang-Nga, 82000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: For over 30 years, this shop, across from a Chinese shrine, has drawn devoted fans for their four types of flavourful curry. Flavour combinations are endless, with well over 20 condiments, fresh vegetables, boiled eggs and crispy Thai anchovies. They’re particularly packed at lunch.

Name: Tonfon Bistro
Address: Krabi 1002 Rural Road, Bo Saen, Thap Put, Phang-Nga, 82180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: The tree in front of this roadside restaurant has grown a lot since this place opened in 1995. All the while, the chef-owner has been cooking flavoursome southern fare. Starting with local ingredients and authentic recipes, she prepares them carefully and presents them attractively. For a truly southern Thai experience, try stir-fried pork with shrimp paste and bitter bean, or curry with crab legs and betel leaves. Indoor and outdoor seating is available.

Name: Thien Duong
Address: Baan Dusit Thani, 116 Saladaeng Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,China UnionPay,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Thien Duong is a showcase of Vietnamese classical design; the antique artworks, mustard-coloured walls, rose-pink granite tables, shiny black floor tiles and exposed ceiling are an interior design lover’s paradise. The menu of Vietnamese dishes includes plenty of clean and fresh-tasting vegetables, with one eye often on health and wellness. The grilled lamb rack with mint-tamarind sauce is worth ordering, delivering a great balance of flavours.

Name: Phed Phed Bistro
Address: The Circle Ratchapruk, 39 Ratchaphruek Road, Bang Ramad, Taling Chan, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Phed Phed has many branches, but this one stands out for its minimalist wire mesh theme décor. The menu offers comforting Isan favourites steeped in flavour. Don’t miss the herbal pork soup with its tender, crispy cartilage and sweet pumpkin, while the green apple som tum and salty fish sauce with dried shrimp perfectly blends sweet with sour. Large groups of locals pack the place at lunch and dinner. As they don't accept bookings, arrive early to avoid a wait.

Name: Toh-Daeng by Baan Ar-Jor
Address: GF, Baan Ar-jor, 102 Thep Kasattri Road, Mai Khao, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Garden or park,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: ‘Toh-daeng’ translates as ‘red dining table’ – and you will find one here, running the length of the kitchen wing at this renovated manor house which serves as a window into Phuket’s past. The restaurant is surrounded by farmland, where they grow ingredients including mulberry and coconut. Well-balanced dishes allow the natural flavours of the produce to shine; rambutan red curry with grilled pork neck is a highlight, with the rambutan adding a natural sweetness.

Name: Gop Phochana
Address: 58/2 Mu 7, Phet Kasem Road, Thai Mueang, Phang-Nga, 82120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Now in its second generation, this popular destination attracts locals and tourists seeking comforting favourites with intense seasoning and spices. The stir-fried shrimp with coconut curry is the delicious signature; it’s creamy, the shrimps are plump, and it boasts natural umami.

Name: Lung Khajohn Wat Ket
Address: (Opposite to Wat Ketkaram), Charoenrajd Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: For decades, this place has been serving distinctive Khao Kriab Pak Moh, or steamed rice skin dumplings, opposite Wat Ket Karam. These contain a tasty salty-sweet filling wrapped in a coconut-infused rice flour sheet and a side of coconut cream. Tapioca balls with sweet pork are also offered.

Name: Tue Ka Ko Na Prince
Address: Kaeonawarat Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This Tue Ka Ko – or taro fritter – place has been open for over 20 years opposite The Prince Royal's College, hence the name “Tue Ka Ko Na Prince." Savoury and sweet, their version of the Chiang Mai snack is perfected textured and served with peanut sauce. Deep-fried tofu is also sold.

Name: Hong Seng Pochana
Address: 280 Mu 2 Chaeng Watthana Road, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, 11120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only,Terrace
Description: On the Chao Praya by the Rama IV Bridge, this renowned Thai-Chinese spot has been known for reasonably priced flavoursome fare since 1957. Its open-air dining room and wooden terrace set the stage for relaxed meals featuring highlights like grilled giant river prawns with spicy sauce and mini deep-fried crab meat wrapped in tofu skin. Open for lunch, the place extends its hours on weekends. Reach it by boat, or if driving, park in the public space under the bridge.

Name: Na Chantra
Address: Chantra Khiri Hotel, 49 Mu 3, Ban Pong, Hang Dong, Chiang Mai, 50230, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Set up in the hills inside the Chantra Khiri Hotel, Na Chantra offers gorgeous views of the national park and a menu that features central and northern Thai dishes. Vegetables and herbs come from their next-door farm and everything else – like the savoury northern sausage with chilli paste – is made from scratch. Don’t miss their signature minced pork with fresh veg and spicy sauce, or the piquant yellow curry soup with sea bass. Start your evening outside, with a seat by the infinity pool.

Name: Bokkia Tha Din Daeng
Address: 323 Tha Din Daeng Road, Somdej Chaophraya, Khlong San, Bangkok, 10600, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Tucked away in a small market stall, this family-run restaurant is famous for its sweet Bokkia. It's a unique treat: sticky egg noodles, topped with crushed ice and syrup, which is amazingly refreshing and not too sweet. The condimental options are also good quality.

Name: Thai Niyom
Address: Mahatun Plaza, 888/28-29 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Hidden in the shadow of skyscrapers is this gem of restaurant, which got its start serving family recipes, but now offers an array of Thai cuisine from Chiang Mai to Hat Yai. It is a great place to sample delicious Thai cooking from every region on the same table. Quality ingredients are sourced locally and turned into dishes like the recommended Phuket stir-fried pork belly with shrimp paste and the Chiang Mai Combo, a Northern Thai-style appetiser plate.

Name: Kin-Kub-Ei
Address: 81/9 Mu 7, Si Sunthon Road, Si Sunthon, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only,Terrace
Description: There is such a cosy and relaxed feel to this restaurant whose name translates as ‘Eat with Auntie’. That’s exactly what happens here, as veteran chef Tubtim cooks Southern Thai dishes that preserve her family’s recipes. Balanced flavours and quality ingredients help to make these great value dishes soar, with the deep-fried local fish and spicy curry paste a highlight. Dining in the garden, shaded by the trees, feels like you’re eating at your family home. Pre-booking is a must, and orders are taken in advance over their social media platform.

Name: Weng (Woeng Nakhon Kasem)
Address: 140 Yaowarat Road, Chong Nonsi, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This push cart on the main drag in Chinatown serves tasty crab fried rice, crab noodles and stir-fried fish maw. Chunks of crab cooked à la minute have a smoky aroma and could put many an upmarket Chinese restaurant to shame. Arrive early or be ready to queue.

Name: Jok Prince
Address: 1391 Charoen Krung Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Visit Jok Prince for a bowl of congee; the ultimate Asian comfort food. The porridge is smooth with a unique smoky aroma, topped with a raw or century egg and pork balls – made with good quality ham that’s minced and seasoned in-house. The pork offal is also fresh and well prepared.

Name: Baan Ta Ko Rai
Address: 112/941 Asian Highway 1 (Bang Pa in-Nakorn Sawan), Khan Ham, Uthai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13210, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only
Description: Here at this blue-roofed local favourite they prove there’s more to Ayutthaya than grilled river prawns. Ingredients are carefully selected from produce grown within the community and it uses fish from nearby rivers as the catch of the day. The herb-scented fish cakes are delectable, while stir-fried Chinese kale with deep fried salted fish is equally impressive and offers a pleasant balance of flavour. Portion sizes are generous, so check before ordering.

Name: Majchapasuk
Address: 166 Mu 8 Udon-Nong Khai Road, Mu Mon, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: A string of wooden pavilions skirts a tranquil pond to form this restaurant’s massive seating capacity. Among them, every seat offers lush scenery and naturally relaxing vibes in which to enjoy the food. Building on over 40 years of experience, the restaurant showcases local fish in traditional Isan recipes. The highlight among them is the spicy fried red tilapia fish salad but whatever you order, start with the excellent deep-fried spring rolls.

Name: Tek Heng (Mee Krob Jeen Lee)
Address: 326-330 Thoet Thai 18 Alley, Talat Plu, Thon Buri, Bangkok, 10600, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: History is on the menu at this legendary Thai-Chinese restaurant. Starting out as a floating shop on Klong Bangkok Yai before moving onshore in 1907, it’s now run by 4th generation descendants of the Thai-Teochew founders. It fills three shophouses adorned with articles, awards, and photos, including some of King Rama V. He is said to have enjoyed the Mee Krob, or crispy vermicelli – one of this place’s many classics based on 130-year-old family recipes.

Name: Lab Nua
Address: 24 Phachauthit Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: ‘Lab Nua’ means delicious Isan-style spicy salad and that’s certainly the focus here. Often featuring homemade fermented fish sauce, dishes like spicy seafood salad with Dong Daeng noodles and Isan soup with rice field snails attest to the chef’s skills. The lively open-air restaurant also sports pink wooden tables and chairs and is popular with friends and family groups who appreciate the friendly service, reasonable prices and late closing time.

Name: Han Thueng Chiang Mai
Address: 63/9 Soi Suthep 4, Suthep Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: Occupying gable-roofed houses near Chiang Mai University, this place may lack a sign but locals have been flocking here for its delicious, competitively priced Northern Thai fare for over a decade. The rustic décor echoes the no-frills food with delicate flavours and textures. Their steamed beef slices with galangal dip are recommended; and for a delicious off-menu dish, order the seasonal special made from ingredients like wild mushrooms. Service is friendly.

Name: Rote Yiam Beef Noodle (Saeng Tawan)
Address: 164/48 Chang Khlan Road, Chang Klan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: For over 30 years, this renowned shop has prided itself on serving some of the city’s best beef noodles, with mellow, tender beef and an intensely flavoured broth packed with Chinese herbs. The beef components are freshly prepared every morning, including homemade beef balls and beef offal. Non-noodle fans can opt for the rich and creamy beef yellow curry with rice. Either way, be sure to finish with coconut ice cream.

Name: Baan Heng
Address: 54/2 Glang Muang Road, Nai Mueang, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Baan Heng was born out of a souvenir and grocery shop the owners’ grandparents started in 1957 called Heng Nguan Hiang. It sold products like homemade Chinese sausage, pork floss and pork jerky. Now, the restaurant serves Thai-Chinese breakfast fare, like their signature Baan Heng sandwich and baked rice with sweet pork sausage in a remodelled wood-themed design that exudes old-school vibes. Add a classic hot Thai black coffee or milk tea for the full effect.

Name: Tumkratoei Sagate
Address: Airport Road, Baan Ped, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Garden or park,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The owner is from Roi Et Province (formerly Sagate Province). The place offers flavourful food, warm service and wallet-friendly prices in a relaxed setting. The signature spicy seafood salad with fermented fish sauce is recommended, and beyond the Som Tum dishes, standouts include fried sour fish and spicy chicken soup with glass noodles. Indoors and outdoor seating are available. Nightly live music adds to the experience.

Name: Huen Muan Jai
Address: 24 Ratchaphruek Road, Chang Phuek, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Headed up by former TV chef Charan Thipeung, this restaurant – whose name means ‘happy home’ – has been serving authentic Northern Thai food since 2011. Set in a Lanna house with a tree-lined garden, it’s a popular, wallet-friendly destination that offers hard-to-find traditional dishes alongside classic favourites. The uniquely flavoured spicy minced fish salad is highly recommended and if you’re unfamiliar with the cuisine, start with the excellent Northern appetiser sampler.

Name: Maadae Slow Fish Kitchen
Address: 86-88 Thapae Rd., Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Supporting the fishermen of Chumphon in the southeast, the chef opened this restaurant to deliver fresh seafood to the north. It’s caught close to the shoreline and transported within a day. The other seasonal and organic ingredients are sourced locally, while sauces are made in-house without preservatives. The dishes are simple, and the taste of umami features prominently on the menu. But the chargrilled catch of the day is the perfect marriage of flavours.

Name: Sanyod (Sathon-Bang Rak)
Address: 89 Soi Charat Wiang, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only
Description: For over 50 years, this tiny noodle stall tucked away in a small alley has served mouth-watering Thai-Cantonese fare to faithful regulars. The modern dining room is pleasantly appointed and located just opposite the original take-away shop. The star of the menu is chargrilled roast duck marinated in a secret sauce. The deep-fried shrimp balls topped with mustard greens, which are huge, crispy and perfectly paired with a sticky sauce, are also recommended. Meanwhile, meat-lovers will enjoy the tender beef braised in a clay pot.

Name: Sanguan Sri
Address: 59/1 Witthayu Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Surrounded by high-end businesses and embassies near Lumphini Park, Sanguan Sir still pulls in the international crowds. This legendary but simple Thai eatery began in 1970 and its chipped plates and simple cutlery all add to the feel. It offers small and large portions of signatures and alternating daily specials. The stir-fried crispy snake-head fish in red curry has a luscious amalgam of salty, sweet and spicy, with kaffir lime julienne adding acidity.

Name: One Chun
Address: 48/1 Thep Krasatti Road, Talad Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Merging her fashion design background with a love of food, owner Khun Prang has created a big hearted dining experience with a distinct vintage feel. The 19th century building sets the scene, as do antiquities from bygone days scattered about, while the food is authentically Phuket, comprising family recipes passed down over 3 generations. Shrimp paste dip served with vegetables delightfully starts the meal.

Name: Chom Chan
Address: 242/2 Yaowarat Road, Talad Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only
Description: Chom Chan has flourished with its own charming character and refreshing ambiance. Situated in a small white house with a leafy façade, the interior is a blend of modern Sino-Portuguese with antique decoration. Some dishes are shared with the otherrestaurants but do try the fried crab’s spawn with chilli, pepper and garlic; steamed minced pork with salty egg; and deep-fried pork belly with salt.

Name: Ann Guay Tiew Khua Gai
Address: 419 Luang Road, Wat Dhebsirin, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Fried noodles are a ubiquitous street dish, but here they take on another dimension, thanks to wok-fried crispiness and top-notch chicken, ham and seafood. The signature roasted chicken noodles are cooked fresh on a hot charcoal stove. Nibble on the tasty assortment of fried snacks while you wait.

Name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Dinsor Road)
Address: 115/5 Dinso Road, Bowon Niwet, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The aroma of sizzling pork will have your mouth watering before you even enter this funky eatery from chef Andy Yang. The pork – nicely char-grilled loin slices – tops savoury Pad Thai in their signature dish. Also recommended is the Pad Thai with fresh prawns, stir-fried while still in their shell and full of delicious, sweet meat. If you’re looking for quality Pad Thai and a mastery of wok-based cooking – all at a reasonable price – this is the place for you.

Name: Gorjan
Address: Kra Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This simple restaurant, in a family home, serves some local dishes that can’t be found anywhere else. Specials are written on a whiteboard up front. Select from the fish of the day or choose the delicious steamed yellow curry with crab meat and an intense turmeric aroma and flavour.

Name: Piya Radna
Address: 994 Mukkamontri Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: For over 20 years, this simple outlet has been popular with locals. It serves high-quality pad see ew and rad na with either fresh or deep-fried noodles. The delicious rad na is the signature, served with a homemade gelatinous gravy and tender pork slices.

Name: Krua Lawng Khao
Address: 18 Mu 2, Soi Sukhaphiban Mae Rim, Ban Duang Di 1, Rim Tai, Mai Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: Food and atmosphere are well-matched at this chill Northern Thai restaurant in Mae Rim. It’s in a two-storey wooden pavilion with regular tables downstairs and cushioned floor seating upstairs; both options offer relaxing rice field views and refreshing breezes. The food here is equally fresh, as well as flavourful and easy on the wallet; the Northern Thai spicy pork salad and the Northern Thai hot and spicy soup with fish and morning glory are recommended.

Name: Mae Khlong Hua Pla Mo Fai
Address: 198 Phran Nok-Phutthamonthon Sai 4, Bang Phrom, Taling Chan, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: Simple in its design with a white pavilion and modest dining tables, the restaurant has a small garden with some outdoor seating. The owners are hands-on, preparing every dish with care. The stir-fried crab has a naturally sweet meat and wok-fried aroma, and is served with glass noodles, spicy chilli and crunchy mimosa. The large butterfly-cut river fish is nicely char-grilled. The grilled river prawns, meanwhile, are clearly the people’s favourite.

Name: Arunwan
Address: 295 LGF, Park X Building, Ekkamai 15 Alley, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only
Description: Opened over 60 years ago and now run by the founder’s children, this spot specialises in a pork offal and pickled cabbage soup that they have honed over the years using a family recipe. It’s a fresh-tasting dish and the cabbage combines well with the sweetness of the pork consommé. The crispy pork wontons with sweet black sauce are well worth ordering while you wait for your soup.

Name: Khanom Ochin
Address: 91 Jomsurangyard Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Ochin is named after the owner's favourite Japanese film. This second-generation stall only serves takeaway – a range of homemade deep-fried buns presented on a trolley at the front. Their signature is the crispy bun which contains glass noodles, tasty seasoning and vegetables.

Name: Baan Ton Sai
Address: 189 Pratu Chai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Named after the banyan tree (ton sai) in the backyard, this local favourite offers tasty Thai-Chinese food at wallet-friendly prices. The chef uses fresh, quality ingredients to create dishes infused with herbs and spices. Tom yum with catfish and crispy pork with salt and chilli are standouts. Choose from two dining areas – one inside the traditional Thai house and the other under the open-air pavilion – and arrive early if you haven’t booked as it can get busy.

Name: Kor Chun Huad
Address: Soi Somdet Phrachao Taksin 34 (Kobo), Bukkhalo, Thon Buri, Bangkok, 10600, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: For more than five decades, Koa Chun Huad, with its simple interior, has been attracting throngs of locals. Named after the chef-owner who has worked in many a kitchen in Chinatown, it serves classic Thai-Chinese dishes at appealingly low prices. Each one impresses but the highlights are the boiled pork slices, perfectly complemented by a soybean sauce, and the intense stewed pork with sweet-salty five spice gravy.

Name: Roti Pa Day
Address: In front of Wat Mahawan, Thapae Road Soi 4, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: First-timers should order the plain crispy roti with condensed milk to start. The roti flour here is uniquely made without eggs. Instead, Thai-Pakistani owner Pa Day (Auntie Day) adds salt to the flour that’s cooked to a crispy-chewy perfection in coconut oil. Choose from 20 flavours.

Name: Chang-Wang-Imm
Address: 44 Mu 4, Soi Wat Bang Chak, Bang Tanai, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, 11120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Down by the banks of the Chao Phraya, enjoy affordable yet tasty Thai cuisine with relaxing river views from a charming 1950s house. Everything here is vintage, from the old-fashioned décor to the classic cooking techniques and flavours. The traditional Thai curry with pork, shrimp paste and basil is highly recommended. Book table #52 for remarkable private views from the upper deck. Live music adds to the ambience at the weekend.

Name: Grim Nguan Noodle
Address: 75/70 Soi Chom Thong 16, Chom Thong Road, Bang Kho, Chom Thong, Bangkok, 10150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Opened in 1999, this eatery down a small Bangkok alley is something of a hidden gem. They specialise in fish ball noodle soup, which they have down to a fine art. The fish balls are fresh and provide good umami flavour, the noodles are nicely al dente and the broth is aromatic and flavoursome. Toppings such as cheese and poached egg are available, and the generous portions served with plenty of condiments enhance the already great value for money.

Name: Sae Phun
Address: 112 Mahannop Road, Sao Ching Cha, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Opened since 1926, it has been relocated. This small shop is now run by the third generation. The owner has been cooking with her grandfather's recipes for many years. The signature dish chicken stew is juicy with chicken and rich in sauce. It can be paired with rice or deep fried egg noodles.

Name: Nai Muang
Address: 33/4 Mu 6, Soi Loma, Khuk Khak, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82190, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only,Terrace
Description: The nostalgic bric-a-brac, old tin mining memorabilia, record players and sewing machines exude a quaint retro charm. It’s all about the seafood here, guaranteed to be fresh, vibrant and big on flavour. Order the crab curry with rice noodles, or stir-fried shrimps with stink beans and shrimp paste. Another popular southern Thai dish is the signature spicy salad, served with crispy prawns, squid and taro, with diced lime and fried chilli for extra pep.

Name: Sawang Bami Kam Pu (Si Phraya)
Address: 264 Si Phraya Road, Maha Pruttaram, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This is the place to enjoy top-quality crab noodles in Bangkok. The sweet, succulent giant crab claw flesh is perfectly paired with sticky egg noodles and shrimp dumplings. Be sure to try their famous noodles with extra soup and barbecued pork on the side. Premium quality and fresh ingredients.

Name: Ruean Panya
Address: 1300/600 Soi Ekachai 13, Norarat Uthit Road, Maha Chai, Samut Sakhon, 74000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Open since 1995, this family-run restaurant – which blends food and art – is a hidden gem. Spread across four houses, it has a relaxed vibe that gives the impression of dining at a friend's, while painting-filled interiors add a gallery feel. Owner Prunhnee does all the cooking herself; her attention to detail and the complexity of flavours make her dishes memorable. Local seafood is a feature, and their signature mud crab coconut dip or ‘Lhon Pu’ is a must-have.

Name: Hia Wan Khao Tom Pla
Address: 816 Chan Road, Thung Wat Don, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Entirely focused on top-drawer seafood, this eatery offers a wide range of dishes. The soft-boiled rice with silver pomfret comes with a juicy fillet and fresh, clear soup. The baked mung bean noodles with prawns feature sticky mung bean noodles, underscored by a spicy-sour Thai seafood sauce.

Name: Pae Bronze Pot Porridge 38 Years
Address: 320 Pracha Rat Sai 1 Road, Bang Sue, Bangkok, 10800, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: 38 is actually the founder’s lucky number; the place itself has been around for considerably longer – since 1962 in fact. Three generations on, his family is still serving savoury congee boiled in its signature bronze pots – try it with oysters or minced pork and an egg.

Name: Guay Jub Ouan Pochana
Address: In front of China Town Rama Cinema, 408 Yaowarat Road, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This cart has been serving Guay Jub (rolled rice noodle soup) for over 50 years and there is always a long line. The noodles are tender yet chewy, the broth is aromatic and peppery, and the pork belly is juicy and crispy.

Name: Arunee Namnueng
Address: 36/8 Panprao Road, Makkaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This simple Vietnamese restaurant opened in 1988 and is now run by the owner’s offspring. The original recipes and bright, non-nonsense shophouse dining room continue to pack in big groups of locals. First among the offerings is Pizza Vietnam, made with a rice cracker base and topped with an omelette. It, along with everything on the menu, comes with homemade sweet and sour sauce and fresh vegetables, enabling you to pack in even more flavour into your meal.

Name: Here Hai
Address: 112/1 Soi Sukhumvit 63, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Good value, high quality seafood sent directly from Surat Thani is the draw here. Its prices may be considered high for street food, but portions are large and ingredients superb. Go for the fried rice with crabmeat and fried mantis with crispy garlic, both cooked with traditional technique and offer pleasant smoky aroma.

Name: Kai Yang Rabeab (Khao Suan Kwang)
Address: 99 Mittraphap Road, Kham Muang, Khao Suan Kwang, Khon Kaen, 40280, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Throw a stick in Khon Kaen and you’ll likely hit a street food place serving grilled chicken and Isan dishes. You’d be lucky if you landed on this one. Its secret is tender, juicy chicken from three local breeds. A second downtown branch offers the same menu minus grilled offal.

Name: Agave
Address: 153 Phalorangrit Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The owner is an avid collector of the agave plant; it decorates every corner of this homely space. Instrumental music drifts across a room with high ceilings which complements the smells of Vietnamese home cooking pepped up with local Isan spices. All of their ingredients are made in-house from a choice of pork or fish sausage for the namneung. The sticky rice waffle served with sun-dried pork, preserved with local Isan flavours, is a highlight.

Name: Mon Phochana
Address: 46/11-12 Mu 1, Phet Kasem Road, Lam Kaen, Thai Mueang, Phang-Nga, 82210, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: Ideal for groups, the open-air main dining area nods to the style of an old Thai-Chinese eatery. Mon Phochana is popular with divers after a trip to Koh Similan and offers fresh seafood, plenty of choice and generous portions. The intense flavours pack a punch and are a great representation of local cuisine. The stir-fried crab with lime is a must and don’t miss the southern curry with river snails and wild betel leaves for a truly local experience.

Name: Jeh O
Address: 113 Soi Charat Mueang, Rong Muang, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Jeh O might be known for her Mama Noodles Tom Yum, but her menu contains numerous other top-notch dishes. Many, including her delicious fried tofu with crispy garlic, boiled rice with duck, and signature crispy pork, are popular Thai favourites. Though the staff only speaks Thai, there’s an English picture menu for non-Thai speakers. Outside the shop, an eager crowd waits up to two hours for tables; to get in faster, arrive just before opening or near closing.

Name: Krua Luang Ten
Address: 160 Mu 2, Phet Kasem Road, Khuk Khak, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82190, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: An upgrade from street stall to restaurant endowed them with more space, with wooden dining tables on concrete floors and sand under a tin roof. Ask the staff for the day’s specials, not listed on the menu, as they use the catch of the day and seasonal ingredients. The chef produces a good balance of flavours accentuated with a southern Thai intensity that doesn’t compromise on spiciness. They close on the 10th, 20th and 30th each month.

Name: Lim Lao Ngow (China Town)
Address: In front of the building no. 299-301, Song Sawat Road, Maha Pruttaram, Samphanthawong, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: After 60 years in business, the family boasts multiple branches, but the original, in Chinatown, is our pick. The bouncy fish ball concept definitely lives up to its name. Made from fresh fish and no flour, they’re served with Chinese noodles and wontons, and leave a joyful aftertaste.

Name: Guay Jub Mr. Jo
Address: 86 Soi Chan 44, Wat Phraya Krai, Bang Kho Laem, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: From early morning until late afternoon, locals flock to the small room at the front and large dining area at the rear. Enjoy guay jub as an entrée or in a sweet, peppery rice noodle broth; rich layers of soft pork are encased in a crispy skin. Can be ordered with or without pork offal.

Name: Lai Ros (Rama 6)
Address: 122 Rama 6 Road, Sam Sen Nai, Phaya Thai, Bangkok, 10400, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Wheelchair access
Description: This small glasshouse is best known for its authentic royal Thai recipes and summer menu, including the carefully prepared Khao Chae or rice soaked in flower-infused water with 6 condiments. The good news is that this dish can be enjoyed year round! For coconut milk lovers, try the Kung Tom Ka Thi or coconut soup with prawns and cha om leaves; Khao Mao Nam Ka Thi or crispy green rice with coconut milk syrup is a perfect end to your meal.

Name: Pae Pochana
Address: 80/1 Rahaeng Market, Rahaeng, Lat Lum Kaeo, Pathum Thani, 12140, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This hidden gem in 100-year-old Rahaeng Market has been serving old-school Thai-Chinese dishes for over 50 years. The menu focuses on quality over quantity and ingredients are mainly sourced from the market. Some, like the minced featherback fish and minced pork in tofu sheets, are made inhouse. These, plus spicy stir-fried featherback fish with herbs and fried sun-dried snakehead fish, are recommended. Arrive early.

Name: Ruanthai Kungpao
Address: 1/2 Mu 4, Soi Thetsaban 10, Ratchakham, Bang Sai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13290, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: This riverside restaurant is a great place to stop for lunch after paying respects at Wat Choeng Len. Diners gather here for some of the finest fresh produce from the river, including grilled prawns and deep-fried sheatfish. The aromatic green curry with clown featherback fish balls is another highlight. Advance ordering of the huge river prawns – expertly cooked over charcoal – is highly recommended, as they are both popular and in limited supply.

Name: Peng Duck Noodles
Address: Nong Tao Lek Road, Ban Lueam, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The secret of this long-established duck noodle soup specialist near National Sports University is its succulent duck meat. The owners procure it from a local free-range farm and use it to elevate their signature soup; they also recommended duck rice with duck blood jelly.

Name: Tang Sui Heng (Banthat Thong Road)
Address: 649 Banthat Thong Road, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This iconic family-run shop has been packed with locals for more than 50 years. These days, the family’s second generation runs it, but the founder’s talent for cooking dishes like the signature claypot stewed duck with intestines, blood jelly, and feet clearly runs in the family.

Name: SP Chicken
Address: 9/1 Samlan Road Soi 1, Phra Singh, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: The sight of passers-by standing trance-like at the front, mesmerised by the plump birds slowly spinning on their vertical spits, is common at this authentic Isan eatery in Old Town Chiang Mai. Though other Isan classics are on offer, the aromatic and impossibly juicy rotisserie chicken is the jewel in the crown here.

Name: Yoong Khao Hom (Pathum Wan)
Address: 1F, I'm Park Chula, Soi Chulalongkorn 9, Charoen Mueang Road, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: From its longstanding stall in Samui, to Bangkok in 2017, they’ve reimagined their authentic southern cuisine, with Chef Aom Sujira at the helm. The meat of the charcoaled pork ribs falls away from the bone. Its southern red curry paste boasts a delightful blend of sweet, turmeric, chilli and coconut. Meanwhile, the coconut dumpling in a coconut milk and shell has a lovely aroma of roasted white sesame seeds.

Name: Kai Yang Saeng Thai
Address: 126 Rajadamnern Road, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: Since opening in 1967, they’ve marinated the rotisserie chicken with a peppery, herbal recipe. The farmed option is juicy and comes with a light crispy skin; the domestic-raised chicken has succulent tenderness. Enjoy it with the sweet chilli dipping sauces.

Name: Khanom Jeen Pradok Ban Kru Yod
Address: 628/8 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit card / Debit card accepted
Description: The former music teacher is an artist of many stripes. Artisanal souvenirs and musical instruments are on display at the entrance of this newly renovated shop. Their signature is a kanom jeen set with a choice of a range of curries. Chicken wing lovers should definitely order the deep-fried wings marinated in fish sauce and served with curry. If Kru Yod has time away from the kitchen, you may be treated to a rendition on one of his homemade instruments.

Name: Baan Pang Hom
