Description: Thick Sanuki udon and ingredients from Kagawa Prefecture are the hallmarks here. The izakaya represents the search for his roots of owner-chef Ryusuke Yamaji, who comes from Miki. Fish caught in the Seto Inland Sea, Cochin chicken from Sanuki and olive-fed beef are notable ingredients. The udon is a unique version, while the oden is flavoured with miso in the Sanuki style. For the signature finale, udon with shrimp paste and raw egg is a parting treat.

Name: idematsu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Wild game can be savoured year-round at this counter-service-style French establishment. An explorer of little-known foodstuffs, owner-chef Yasumasa Deguchi works with game ranging from the familiar wild boar and venison to masked palm civet, nutria and raccoon dog. Wild fowl is paired with classic sauces: cream sauces for white meat and salmis for dark. The wide range of spices used showcases their limitless possibilities. At lunch, the inventive curries earn popular appeal.

Name: MOTOI Gyoza
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Motoi Gyoza is a gyoza dumpling restaurant owned and operated by a French-trained chef. He first made dumplings to delight his daughter, because he saw so little of her due to his work. Two of her favourite ingredients are shrimp and chives, so they take centre stage in his ‘Papa Gyoza’, which uses no garlic. The crimped edges are crispy and fragrant, and the addition of ginger and coriander makes it even more nutritious. These gyoza dumplings are little parcels of love.

Name: Ramen Touhichi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: When rich, heavy ramen was in style, the owner-chef resolved to win diners over to Tokyo’s chintan or “clear-water” style of ramen. His motto is, “the goodness of the ingredients, simply conveyed”. To this end, he creates his dashi from just two ingredients: local, free-range chicken and water. The signature ‘Chicken-and-soy-sauce Ramen’ is prepared with raw soy sauce kaeshi. To ensure the rich broth does not steal the show, he pairs it with flat noodles of medium thickness.

Name: Az
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Interesting wine list
Description: This casual Chinese eatery wears two faces. At lunch it is called Bifun Azuma, serving specialities that have been around since the restaurant’s founding: the Chinese chimaki and fried rice vermicelli (bifun in Japanese). At night the name changes to Az (pronounced ‘Azoo’), evolving along the theme of wine and Chinese cuisine. The logo is an abbreviation of ‘A to Z’, signifying that the cuisine covers the Eurasian continent end-to-end, fusing local cooking in each country with Chinese cuisine.

Name: GANESH N
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Owner-chef’s eyes were opened to the wonders of curry on a trip to India, where she was captivated by its wonders. Home cooking is the theme of the restaurant, and Ieda conveys it authentically. The mainstay dish, bean and vegetable dal, is made all the more popular by pairing it with the curry du jour. Guests can choose between Indian basmati rice and Japanese rice. The restaurant is named after the Hindu god with the head of an elephant.

Name: Soba Rojina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: To convey the unique character of the soba, the owner-chef prepares juwari with no wheat flour. He made the stone mortar he uses to grind the flour himself, back when he was an apprentice. The entire shop reverberates with the sound of buckwheat being ground slowly so as to retain the fragrance. In addition to soba, Rojina offers items that pair well with alcohol. Tofu with yuba on top and manganji togarashi with jako are two typical Kyoto appetisers served before the soba.

Name: Watanabe Curry Honten
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining
Description: The owner-chef bills his fare as ‘curry you’ll want to eat every day’. The key to the taste is the dashi made from tai and chicken, combining its umami with spices to determine the flavour of each dish. Japanese and Indian rice are mixed and steamed together for the same reason. The mainstay Ganso Watanabe Curry is an assortment of chicken and mutton keema curries. The Tonkatsu Curry, piled high with pork loin cutlets, captures the heart of cutlet curry lovers.

Name: Bistro des Chenapans
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The restaurant’s famous steak frites is prepared with Omi beef from owner-chef Kawata’s native Shiga Prefecture. He favours aitchbone and rump cuts, as they are low in fat and rich in umami. Grilled in chunks of at least 200g, their innate flavour is presented without fancy additions. Kawata’s skill in preparing meat dishes, honed in France, is displayed to good effect. Portions for all dishes are generous, so diners can savour the meat to their hearts’ delight.

Name: Ramen Kuon
Address: B2F, Semba Centar Bldg Sangokan, 1-4-3 Sembachuo, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 541-0055, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Ramen Kuon delicately constructs its flavours as if solving a puzzle. The noodles, made with a high water content and three types of flour, and the soup made using a triple broth from fish, shellfish and chicken, support its unique character. There are two staples: ‘Salt Ramen’, distinguished by its shellfish dashi, and the ‘Chuka Ramen’, whose unique flavour derives from soy sauce from Shodoshima. Modulated with sea lettuce and slow-cooked pork, the noodles and soup become perfectly matched.

Name: Shunten Shin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: For this owner-chef, the tempura must have a refined aroma and not be oily, so the batter is applied thinly and the cooking oil used is mainly raw-pressed sesame oil. Ingredients like hamo and first-harvest onions come from his home island of Awaji. The meal ends with tendon, tenbara (mixed tempura on rice), or one of several other such dishes in his repertoire. The most famous among them is the bowl of rice topped with tempura made from egg yolk, and raw uni.

Name: Chinese Noodles ROKU
Address: 2F, Good Nature Station, 318-6 Inaricho, Shimogyo-ku, Kyoto, 600-8022, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Car park,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Ramen, soup and other Chinese foods are the soul of this ramen shop by Velrosier. The chef draws soup stock from bones of duck, chicken, venison, beef and pork. Clear soup owes its depth to umami from a medley of dried foods; dried longan fruit, a Chinese medicinal herb, is a touch only a gourmet of Chinese cuisine would think of. The manifold layers of flavour derive from Roku’s ‘add-on’ approach to seasoning.

Name: Pizzeria da Tigre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: A firewood oven made by a Neapolitan craftsman sits at the back of this authentic-feeling restaurant. The flour used for the dough, the tomatoes, the garlic and other ingredients are all from Italy, and the chef faithfully reproduces the tastes he learned there. Named after the chef’s teacher, the ‘Attilio’ is the speciality pizza and features ricotta, salsiccia and mozzarella.

Name: Le Caneton
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Owner-chef Tomokazu Yurikusa learned the appeal of duck and foie gras from the French-born chef who mentored him. The name of the restaurant means ‘duckling’, which is also the speciality of the house. Yurikusa’s use of Osaka duck is a tribute to the city that is his birthplace. His use of fruit and vinegar to add sourness while setting great store by classic culinary methods imparts a wonderful sense of lightness.

Name: Kasane
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The dish Toyama native Shinya Yamada offers as his speciality is oden. Typically for Osaka, his is salty, to make a fitting companion for sake. Ma-kombu and katsuo-bushi exude a rich umami. The sardine dumplings look like they belong in a kaiseki soup. The items are abundantly varied: potatoes are seasoned with soy sauce flavour, for example. To wrap up the meal, udon in oden dashi is served. Etchu sake is brought in from his native prefecture, showing his love for his hometown.

Name: Tonkatsu Ichiban
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The tonkatsu is savoured with demi-glace sauce. Though the tonkatsu gets top billing as the restaurant’s speciality, the demi-glace, simmered for a full 10 days, surely deserves equal mention. From his mentor, who trained in yoshoku, the second-generation owner-chef inherited not only the flavouring but also the old-school dining-hall feel. With the retro building, plate-glass windows and shop-worn chairs, time seems to have stood still. It’s no surprise that Tonkatsu Ichiban was founded in 1960.

Name: Osteria La Cicerchia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The chef went to the Marches in central Italy to learn local cuisine, and conveys its charms to her customers. She also has an extensive selection of wine from the Marches for pairing with vegetable and meat dishes. The standard offerings are minestrone and pasta made with cicerchia beans, an Italian legume. The presentation is simple and the portions plentiful for a real Italian-style atmosphere.

Name: Shibosai Sumiyoshi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The chef is skilled in a wide range of culinary traditions, including Sichuan and Cantonese cuisine. Hong Kong grouper is an ingredient always on hand and can be prepared in a variety of ways, including steamed and fried; so, diners can enjoy a range of Chinese culinary styles. We recommend the Hong Kong-style homemade dim sum. Seasonings are homemade, making the flavours of Shibosai Sumiyoshi not merely the restaurant’s but those of the chef’s own home cooking.

Name: Berangkat
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Berangkat means ‘beginnings’ in Indonesian, apt for a restaurant serving creative interpretations of cuisine the owner-chef studied in Southeast Asia. Consider, for example, shiraae dressed with coriander, pidan and Szechuan pickles, drizzled with homemade chilli oil. The grilled meat in cinnamon soy sauce borrows from the fare of the street stalls of Vietnam. The Okinawa cuisine, from the owner-chef’s experiences on Ishigakijima Island, is another of the restaurant’s fortes.

Name: Pontocho Masuda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Redolent with the ambience of the geisha district, this restaurant excels in Japanese dishes that pair nicely with drinks. It dates from 1952, when two sisters set out to serve honest home cooking. Today the third generation of the family runs the establishment, which is famous for its extensive list of obanzai, which include shimesaba sushi, ohitashi of Kyoto mizuna greens and herring with eggplant. It’s decorated with calligraphy and folding screens by the author Ryotaro Shiba (1923–1996).

Name: Sobakiri Karani
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Owner-chef Kiyoshi Hashimoto stocks his restaurant with a full complement of bar snacks, as well as seasonal local sakes. Duck with leeks and miso sauce, tofu marinated with barley miso, and soybeans and ume with chopped katsuo-bushi are standard appetisers before the soba. Tipping back cups of sake as you dine makes the evening fun. Diners can choose from either thin-cut or coarse-ground soba. It’s easy to understand why many guests start with shuko and wrap up with cold soba.

Name: Ramen Hayato
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The popularity of this ramen shop stems from its Miso Ramen, served with bean sprouts stir-fried in a column of fire. The experience of owner-chef Naoto Ishigaki, who apprenticed in Sapporo before moving to Osaka, can be appreciated in this speciality. The Shoyu Ramen, prepared with a combination of meat-based and seafood-based stocks, is a flavour that developed in Osaka. Be sure to check the Ura Shoyu on the back of the menu.

Name: Hachiraku
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The name combines the first character in ‘Yasaka’, where the restaurant is, and the character for ‘fun’, which is what the proprietors want you to have. With a temperament of a seasoned artisan, the owner-chef wields his wok in the kitchen while the proprietress, affectionately called okaasan (mother) by the geiko and maiko who dine here, attends to customers. The fare, a lightly seasoned version of Kyoto Chinese, eschews oil and garlic so that the smell won’t cling to kimonos.

Name: Sobakiri Gaku
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: For owner-chef Yuto Kuroda, the ideal soba has a smooth texture and pleasant aroma. After much trial and error, he says, he struck on the combination of flours for the nihachi soba he serves today. By blending buckwheat groats ground to different degrees of fineness, Kuroda hit upon a soba with both of the qualities he sought. The menu offers cold soba only, so customers can experience the true flavour and texture of buckwheat. They also often order the char-grilled sabazushi.

Name: Sakeya Sakana Yoshimura
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Notable sake list
Description: Certain snacks are essential to the mood of a traditional Japanese pub so the owner-chef always offers teppai, a regional dish of minced vegetables, seafood and vinegared miso; shiraae and ohitashi. The rope curtain and sugidama hang in the doorway for the same reason. The ‘Omakase SIX Dishes’ emphasises seafood dishes like sashimi and charcoal-grilled fruits de mer. The mild-mannered proprietor and graceful proprietress charm with their friendly, at-home service.

Name: RISTORANTE SPELLO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The stylish dining room has an urban feel and the tables and work stand were made to the chef’s orders. Using the cooking processes and recipes he learned in Italy while adding his own unique sensibilities, he has put together a menu that is refined in every way, including in the presentation of the food. There are a wide variety of dishes that include handmade pasta such as gnocchi and ravioli and meat dishes like wagyu tagliata and wintertime game.

Name: Kyoudon Kisoba Okakita
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Since its founding in 1940, this shop has been in the same family for four generations. The flavour of the dashi is drawn from Rishiri kombu and several types of dried fish flakes. The delicate, thin noodles go well with the broth, giving the bowl a sense of harmony. The ‘kitsune’, prepared with chopped, deep-fried tofu slices and Kujo leek, is a standard menu item. The ‘shippoku’, dressed with kamaboko (steamed fish paste), shiitake and yuba, is what Kyoto udon is all about.

Name: Washoku Haru
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Owner-chef Harutoshi Kikkawa says that ryotei cuisine should be more accessible. The “washoku” in the name was included to indicate that customers are not bound by a set menu but can choose whatever they like. The ‘Haru-fu Sabazushi’ and silky-smooth potato salad are staple fare. In winter, multiple items of oden are pre-cooked separately, then served on a single dish. Expect honest, straightforward dishes, accentuated by antique crockery, in an ambience that turns back time.

Name: Benikurage
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Notable sake list,Visa credit card
Description: The owner-chef and his wife serve appealing dishes that go with various kinds of Japanese sake. You can choose from an extensive selection of sake, or beer for toasts, and the menu is a choice selection of shuko and dishes made with seasonal ingredients. The focus is on fish and vegetables, which are used to highlight the season. The husband and wife prize their relationships with producers; so, many of the sake offerings are from breweries they’ve visited together.

Name: Oryori Maeshiro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: At this unpretentious eatery, guests can not only order à la carte but also specify portion sizes or ask for dishes adjusted to personal taste. The owner-chef’s training taught him the importance of dashi – he patiently prepares it to elicit the natural flavours of the ingredients. This is why boiled dishes dominate the menu here. The sata andagi, a kind of sweet, deep-fried bun served the moment it is done, is the specialty of the owner-chef, who hails from Okinawa.

Name: Souikufu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The name means ‘ingenuity’ as Souikufu is home to uniquely inspired creations offered in set menus that you won’t find anywhere else. Potatoes dressed in anchovy butter and fried rice paired with curry roux are staple offerings. The adoption of kaiseki-ryori-style presentation is an engaging touch, with offerings such as ‘O-wangushi’, fish skewers served in a small bowl; burdock wrapped in beef; and ‘Age-hassun’, a platter of stewed walleye roe.

Name: Kitashinchi Shien
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: A yakitori eatery with Wajima lacquered trays? The name ‘Shien’ combines the characters shi meaning ‘will’ and en meaning ‘connection to people’. It can also be read as shien, ‘support’, which Shunsuke Sato hopes his clientele will show him, he adds with a smile. The bowl of chicken soup in the set menu is a unique flourish. The yakitori is grilled over bincho charcoal and finished with rice cooked in an earthenware pot. The warabimochi and dampened chopsticks express the spirit of chakaiseki.

Name: Pizzeria da Ciro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The painting of the Gulf of Naples and the Maradona uniform decorating the wall exude the spirit of Naples, where the chef learned to make pizza. He pursues authentic flavours and puts much effort into procuring and using Italian ingredients. He even had the oven artisan from where he trained come over from Italy to install his oven. We recommend trying the skilfully baked margherita pizza first. Not putting out appetisers is in keeping with Neapolitan tradition.

Name: Tsuroku
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The name derives from an old Kyoto word meaning ‘balance’ or ‘harmony’. Simple arrangements and friendly service make for a pleasant experience. The decision to make all menu items à la carte was taken so customers could drop in casually. The head chef excels in wanmono (dishes served in small bowls) using shinjo, as well as fried foods. Guji knife-scored to look pinecone-like and grilled and bowls of white miso soup are standard fare and quintessentially Kyoto.

Name: Edobori Kida
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The owner-chef learned his craft from the pioneer who brought Sanuki udon to Osaka. He prides himself on creating udon that is smooth and never sticky. Be sure to try the signature dish, ‘Kijoyu’. Keeping it authentic, he gets his soy sauce from Kagawa and sudachi from Tokushima. “Don’t mix them, eat them two at a time”, he instructs novice diners. Serving oden with miso mixed with mustard, as an indispensable part of the meal, is a hallmark of Sanuki cooking.

Name: Okonomiyaki Mizuno
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Yoshiko Morikawa is the third-generation owner of this okonomiyaki emporium in the heart of Dotombori. The mainstay of the menu is the ‘Mazeyaki, with a batter containing a mixture of many different ingredients. The menu fairly bursts with variety: pork and generous amounts of seafood are the heart of the shop’s famous ‘Mizuno-yaki’. In its ‘Yamaimo-yaki’, yam is used instead of flour in the batter, while the ‘Yoshoku-yaki’ is a creation handed down from her grandparents.

Name: Hortensia Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: By the end of his training in France, the owner-chef was impressed above all by Bretagne. The name of the restaurant is another word for hydrangea, the flower that symbolises this region. Here in his Osaka restaurant he actively seeks out traditional Naniwa vegetables, as well as local meats such as Tsurumi pork. His gastronomic interests are broad, from bistro cooking that reveres tradition, to the gastronomy of his apprenticeship in Paris.

Name: Saikaku
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: It is said that to eat Sichuan cuisine is to consume Sichuan’s history. Chef Okubo cooks his sansho and chili chicken stir-fry with plenty of chili pepper and Sichuan pepper. The twice-cooked pork is left unskinned, to stick close to Sichuan practice. Saikaku focuses on popular dishes that have developed into home cooking, such as mapo tofu and dandan noodles. To get as many people as possible to appreciate Sichuan cooking, Okubo strives to make his shop welcoming to casual diners.

Name: YOSHOKU OGATA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Owner-chef Ogata is aiming for a yoshoku restaurant in the kappo style. To ensure that diners fully understand the deliciousness of the freshly prepared fare, counter seating is available. Ingredients are painstakingly selected only after Ogata has met with the producers multiple times. The famous hamburger steak incorporates aged beef from Shiga and name-brand pork from Kagoshima. The seafood delivered from Suruga Bay is used in deep-fried and charcoal-grilled items.

Name: Tsuneya Densuke
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This kappo izakaya is packed night after night. Its renowned sabazushi is prepared with mackerel cut so thick it makes up half the thickness of the sushi. Another popular item, the stir-fried lettuce, stir-fried with oyster sauce, garlic and chilli pepper, beguiles with its Chinese seasonings. Obanzai such as okara and potato salad are standard fare. With over 100 items on the menu, choosing what to eat can be a challenge, but being unable to try everything will make you want to come back.

Name: Kushi Tanaka
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Shoes must be removed,Visa credit card
Description: According to the unassuming owner-chef, the ‘Ippo Tsuko’ (“one way”) option refers neither to a traffic sign nor to unrequited love. Instead, it refers to how he serves it to the customer, in the way that he likes it. It comes with 20 items, but you can call a halt to the proceedings before you reach the end if you’re full. He won’t charge you extra even if you retrace your steps and add an item you enjoyed. The restaurant is down a narrow alleyway. Don’t worry, though, it’s not one-way!

Name: Izuu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Founded in 1781, Izuu takes its name from its founder, Izumiya Uhee, from a time when lightly salted mackerel from Wakasa was becoming popular in Kyoto, and the custom of eating sabazushi at festivals and ceremonies became common. Seeing an opportunity, Uhee began delivering these treats to the city’s geisha districts. The business passed from generation to generation, and the current, eighth generation owner-chef preserves the tradition of whole-mackerel sushi to this day.

Name: AKA to SHIRO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The chef uses two types of vinegared rice: red-vinegared rice for tuna and blue-backed fish, and white-vinegared rice for shrimp and white-fleshed fish. The red vinegar is a style popular in the Kanto region, while the ‘white’ vinegar (rice vinegar with sugar) is a Kansai speciality with strong roots in oshizushi. The combination of red and white, east and west, creates a dialogue between variations, respecting the spirit of each. Aka to Shiro also means ‘red and white’.

Name: Sushizen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The chirashi-zushi is as bright as a garden full of blossoms. The thin yellow strips of omelette cover it so extensively you can’t even see the seafood underneath. With doubt battling anticipation, you search the dish with your chopsticks, then your spirit leaps as you find it chock-full of hidden tai, squid, octopus, tuna and shrimp. The thick-cut ingredients are carefully selected for freshness and texture. No sugar is used; instead, salt is added to draw out the natural sweetness.

Name: Doshincho Washoku Zui
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The dashi created from dried tuna and Rishiri kombu that owner-chef Satoshi Kuwano learned in Kyoto are the decisive factors in his flavours, making his simmered and boiled dishes menu highlights. The signature dish, kamameshi simmered in dashi, testifies to his familiarity with the okudo cooking stove. He prepares classic à la carte dishes, and also interweaves creative dishes in set menus. Standing at the counter, he and his wife work in tandem like a finely tuned machine.

Name: Sobakiri Imose
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: ‘Imose’ refers to Mt. Imose in Wakayama Prefecture in the Manyoshu. The owner-chef chose it in tribute to his birthplace. This charming space with its sunken hearth recalls the rural scenes of his youth. Eager for customers to taste the differences in texture and aroma of soba types, he produces it in the nihachi, inaka and juwari styles. The kakinohazushi, sushi of shimesaba wrapped in a persimmon leaf, is hometown cooking in Wakayama ; order it with soba for a diverting pairing.

Name: Sobakiri Arabompu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Owner-chef Yoshio Hashimoto is charmed by the native cultivar harvested in regions bursting with rustic beauty. He chooses the most aromatic buckwheat and uses it to make his own soba until his stock runs out; he then relies on other regions as he waits for the next harvest. Nihachi, juwari and arabiki (coarse-ground) styles of noodle are on offer, with their different textures. ‘Arabompu’ means ‘free and ordinary’, reflecting the spirit of someone who tackles soba unpretentiously.

Name: il luogo di TAKEUCHI
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The name of the restaurant means ‘Takeuchi’s place’ and is where Keiji Takeuchi displays his skills on a colourful stage. His speciality is tomato sauce spaghetti with fruit tomatoes and mozzarella. The standard dish in the evening is char-grilled wagyu from Tottori prefecture. The tiramisu-style monte bianco floats in a sea of espresso and combines Mont Blanc, tiramisu and affogato.

Name: Bistro Yanagihara
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Enjoy à la carte dishes in the traditional style of French cuisine here at Bistro Yanagihara, where the generous servings are suffused with the spirit of Alsace. Faithful to tradition, the chef prepares a charcuterie of terrines and sausages. The focus on meat for the main course is also classic. Drawing on his experience apprenticing in France’s Alsace region, the chef offers choucroute, cabbage pickled in salt and fermented, as the house speciality.

Name: Grill French
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Greeting you from behind the counter at this restaurant, established in 1970, are the first and second generations of owner-chef, father and son. The menu is extensive and varied, ranging from favourite yoshoku, such as hamburger steak and fried shrimp, to French culinary items, like onion gratin soup and duck confit. The pride of the house are the dishes using wagyu, with seared aitchbone, steak, beef stew and other variations leaving the diner spoilt for choice.

Name: Chukasoba Mugen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Customers flock to this restaurant for its Chuka Soba. The chef is particular about his chicken dashi, carefully selecting a small number of brands of locally raised chickens. In the signature soup, dashi drawn from whole chickens, soy-based sauce of kombu and shellfish, and flavouring oils complement each other beautifully. The springiness of the noodles comes from the strength of sweet potato starch. This restaurant’s uncompromising approach makes each bowl immensely interesting.

Name: Kappo Takohachi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: This intimate kappo is in the bustling heart of Kyoto’s Shinkyogoku district. The owner-chef is the second generation, having inherited the business from his father. The menu lists ingredients only: choose the ingredients and he will choose an appropriate culinary approach according to taste. For example, select hamo and the chef may prepare it poached or Yanagawa style; greens may be dressed with sesame sauce or made into ohitashi. Signature dishes are shimesaba sushi and salt-grilled guji.

Name: Yoshokuya Fujiya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Founded in 1935, this ‘city dining hall’ has been in the same family for four generations. The shop is in an office district and feeds a mix of local office workers and long-time regular customers. There is a long list of comfort foods on the menu that go well with rice, including juicy hamburger steaks, and cream croquettes of scallops and shrimp. Season-limited fare, such as beef curry in summer and deep-fried oysters in winter, add to the eatery’s appeal.

Name: SEction D'or
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Hidetaka Nagamatsu keeps things very focused, with a menu solely of tandoori chicken. Traveling overseas, he noted that chicken and spices are familiar to people all over the world. He set his sights on the traditional cuisine of northern India and derived his recipes from the golden ratio, which is what the name of the restaurant means. His calculated technique is based on his experience with French cuisine. The Miyazaki brand name chicken is grilled to a golden colour.

Name: Honkaku Teuchiudon Taiga
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: This udon restaurant reflects the sensibilities of its owner-chef, Kyoto born-and-bred but who learned his craft in Kagawa Prefecture. The noodles are made using the Sanuki technique, but with added water to soften the texture. In a nod to Kyoto culture, the dashi does not use any dried sardines, deriving its flavour instead from kombu and katsuo-bushi. The speciality is the ‘Taiga-mori Udon’, topped with tempura. The kitsune udon, or udon with deep-fried tofu, is a fun dish.

Name: Eitaroya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This is a kappo izakaya with an abiding respect for dashi. The evening starts with appetisers bursting with the umami of kombu and katsuo-bushi. Dashi is used in the soup, the chawanmushi and the ohitashi of green vegetables. In each, the aroma soothes the soul. The sashimi is popular and rich in variety, and the sight of the sliced fish atop crushed ice is entrancing. Simple fare, like steamed fish with grated turnip, or vegetables with vinegared miso, makes a fitting accompaniment to sake.

Name: Unagiya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: This restaurant is famous for its unagi grilled in the well-known style of the Kansai region, without prior steaming as is done in Tokyo. This gives the skin side of the fillet an unforgettable fragrance and flavour. The owner-chef’s primary focus in purchasing unagi is not where it is from but how good the quality is. The fish are still swimming when customers place an order. He skilfully skewers the unagi and roasts it over red-hot bincho charcoal, which he tends as he roasts.

Name: PIZZERIA MARITA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: A large masonry oven sits to one side of the entrance. Clad in his crisp white uniform, the owner-chef stokes the firewood as he bakes authentic Neapolitan pizzas. The extensive menu includes a full list of famous pizza types. The speciality flavour of the house is ‘Regina’. Named from the nickname of where the owner-chef apprenticed, this style is a combination of smoked mozzarella, tomato and basil. The smoky aroma of burning firewood whets the appetite.

Name: La bonne tâche
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The restaurant’s name is ambiguous, meaning either ‘the good job’ or ‘the good stain’. Chef Tamura has been preparing many of the shop’s dishes, including red bell pepper mousse and beef stewed in red wine, since his apprentice days. His awareness sharpens with each passing day, he says, refining his cuisine. There are flavours that only come after ten, or even twenty, years of work. The recipes he’s inherited and the work that stains his soul will never fade.

Name: UDONZIN Beat
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The owner-chef’s idea was for an udon restaurant where customers can also enjoy sake. He serves shuko like roast duck and nama-fu with dengaku miso, and elaborate noodle dishes. The thin udon is homemade style. To give it just the right elasticity and body, he takes the extra step of aging it. The specialities are kamaage and zaru udon with 10 kinds of vegetables and condiments. Add the colourful ingredients of your choosing to enjoy different tastes.

Name: Sushidokoro Kaihara
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Prone to silent absorption in his work, owner-chef Yoshimichi Kaihara is a self-taught craftsman. Preferring to yield the limelight to his sushi, he works diligently in the background. Fatty tuna brushed with foamy soy sauce and uni with nori soy sauce create unique flavours. Decoratively cut squid and oysters cooked on low heat attest to his focus on ingredients. Diners are advised to start by enjoying the eight-piece omakase and adding items according to season and taste.

Name: Jukuseibuta Kawamura
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The tonkatsu is fried in a mix of canola oil and lard. Diners can choose from a number of brands of aged pork, which has been left to sit to enhance the umami. The meat is wrapped in low-carb breadcrumbs and fried slowly at low heat for a nicely browned, fluffy batter. The chef’s pride comes out in how the fried cutlets are served with the cut side up, showing the pink flesh. The pork boiled down in soy and served with rice can be considered a Japanese-equivalent of pork rillettes.

Name: Kyogoku Kaneyo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The restaurant retains the look and feel of the early 20th century, when it was established. Old-school pride of workmanship shows in the sign boasting ‘Japan’s best eel’ and the passion of the artisans at work. This restaurant’s trademark dish is ‘Kinshidon’, a bowl of rice sprinkled with sauce, topped with kabayaki and covered with a large dashimaki tamago. À la carte dishes such as chawanmushi, grilled eel liver and uzaku are also available.

Name: Teishokudo Kongoseki
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The self-taught owner-chef aims to create curries that you could eat every day and still maintain nutritional balance. Side dishes of several kinds of vegetable accompany the hearty curry. He doesn’t make dashi, but brings out the flavour of the ingredients by limiting the number of spices. Enjoy unique menu items like beef offal curry and buttery chicken marsala with chicken gizzard.

Name: Hachidori
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Notable sake list
Description: Food that pairs well with drinks and the ‘Steam-Warmed Sake’ are popular items at this izakaya. The cheerful couple who run it hail from a line of liquor-store owners. The bill of fare includes sashimi and charcoal-grilled items, with the emphasis on the quality of the ingredients, as well as dishes of Shōnai vegetables the chef procures from the production areas. The type of salt used varies, with some items seasoned with ishiru fish sauce for a twist that makes for a pleasant aftertaste.

Name: tanpopo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The iron and copper grilling plates behind the counter spark interest. Ask him and the owner-chef will tell you that he installed them to study how they heat different ingredients. He does not just grill the ingredients, but puts his own original touch on them. The diverse menu includes homemade satsuma age, omelettes and tonpeiyaki – cabbage and pork wrapped in an omelette. Standard offerings to end the meal after you’ve tried several snacks are okonomiyaki and stir-fried noodles, as you would expect in Osaka.

Name: DEUX FILLES
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Owner-chef Daisuke Iwata bills his fare as ‘modern French’. His purpose in using generous portions of vegetables is to showcase the bounty of Kyoto. The salad with 30 kinds of vegetables is a perennial favourite. Selecting a white plate as a canvas, he colours it in with vegetables he buys himself in places such as Kameoka and Kamigamo. His skill in déclinaison – taking a single ingredient and turning it into sauté, sauce and powder, then serving it as a single dish – is unique.

Name: Kikunoi Mugesambo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted
Description: This bento and coffee shop was opened to introduce people to the taste of Kikunoi. The menu was created mindful of the refreshments served at a tea ceremony. In addition to appetisers, tsukuri and nimono soup, there is a rich variety of side dishes in the bento box. At the end come seasonal vegetables and tai takikomi-gohan. Relax while gazing at the mossy garden. After lunch, it operates as a shop for modern-style Japanese sweets.

Name: Kosai Fukumimi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The enduring appeal of Cantonese cuisine stems from its breadth, in terms of both ingredients used and how it is prepared. The chef’s forte is seafood. Hong Kong grouper and filefish are steamed or stir-fried. The stewing of ‘ham yui’, fish pickled in salt and dried in the sun, together with chicken and tofu is trademark Guangdong. In a unique touch, mapo tofu is combined with shirako and oysters. Eager to reproduce the flavours of Hong Kong, the owner-chef uses jasmine rice.

Name: KARA-KUSA curry
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: European-style curry serves as the base for this eatery’s ‘Red’ and ‘Black’. Both of these dishes strive for mild spice and depth of flavour. The ‘Red’ is stewed in vegetable broth and tomato sauce, while the ‘Black’ is an Italian style of curry in which beef is stewed in red wine. The keema curry is made Chinese-style by preparing it like mapo tofu and seasoning it with minced meat and Szechuan pepper. It is curry as only a chef steeped in both Italian and Chinese cooking could conjure it.

Name: BOCCA del VINO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Cash only - lunch,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: What Chef Nomiya conveys through his restaurant is the spirit of Italy. In the evening, the concept is ‘enoteca’, with wine flowing and local-style dishes to be shared. The assaggini features a number of seafood items. Milk-fed lamb is prepared differently by cut. At lunchtime, Bocca del Vino switches to Roman diner mode, as tonnarelli, amatriciana and tiramisu show Nomiya’s nostalgia for the land in which he apprenticed.

Name: en
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The sensibilities of owner-chef Yoshito Tanaka live in every item of the inventive menu. In the noodles with duck and Kujo spring onion, truffles replace the sansho, enhancing the aroma. The fare reflects the arrival of each season without show or fanfare. An appetiser of root vegetables enrobed in yuba ankake sauce, for example, represents autumn leaves. One nice touch is that portions are adjusted and divided according to each diner’s preferences.

Name: au soleil couchant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only - lunch,Visa credit card
Description: The couple who run this bistro learned their craft in France. The chef dedicates himself to the cooking, while the proprietress tends to the baking and customer service. The fare runs to traditional favourites such as smoked salmon and roast pork. To aid digestion, meals are served with lashings of vegetables in season. With the emphasis firmly on freshness, the couple source vegetables from a farmers’ market on the outskirts of the city.

Name: KOBUSHI Ramen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The owner-chef created his menu by trial and error, driven by the search for ingredients that are quintessentially Kyoto. Turning his eye to locally raised duck, he conceived his renowned ‘Kyoto Duck and Dried Nodoguro Soba’. The soup is prepared with dashi of duck bones and tai heads and enriched with dashi of venison bones; the garnish of Kujo green onions is a consummate Kyoto touch. Those who lean toward lighter flavours should try the ‘Rausu kombu Kake Soba’.

Name: Sumiyakisosaitoriya Hitomi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Baby chicken, local chicken, brand-name chicken and chicken from the Kyoto vicinity are all here. The owner-chef keeps a finger on the pulse of his customers’ likes and dislikes. Working the kishu-binchotan according to the characteristics of the chicken, he deftly brings out the native flavour of each morsel. The secret to the restaurant’s nightly success is the sincerity conveyed by every skewer and the good-natured character and hospitality of the owner-chef.

Name: Tonkatsu Daiki
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: ‘Daiki’ was the full name when the owner-chef’s parents ran it as a teishoku restaurant. The second-generation owner-chef switched to specialising in tonkatsu. Pork from Kagoshima is deep-fried in salad oil to provide the batter with just the right crispness. His experience in Chinese cooking comes to the fore in the piquantly spiced mustard sauce He pays special attention to the rice, too, cooking it in small batches.

Name: Naniwa Menjiro
Address: Inside of the Kintestu Osaka Namba Sta, 4-1-17 Namba, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 542-0076, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: Naniwa Menjiro is located inside Osaka Namba Station on the Kintetsu Namba Line, so you need to purchase a platform ticket with a discount coupon at the station to enter. The marquee dish is ‘Ohgonkai Ramen’. The golden broth of freshwater clams and locally raised chicken dashi, finished with light soy sauce, catches the eye. Toppings of yuzu and seared onions add depth to the flavour. Also popular is the ‘Oigatsuo Ramen’, topped with generous amounts of katsuo-bushi for enhanced umami.

Name: Yakitori New Yachiyo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Brand-name chicken from Tottori is swathed in the fragrance of Kishu-binchotan. A Chinese-style dish, chicken breast in Sichuan sauce, is beguiling. But why are the famous deep-fried chicken wings called ‘Mao Zedong style’? Because Hunan province is known for the Middle Kingdom’s spiciest cooking: it is said that ‘the Sichuanese do not fear spices, but the Hunanese fear the lack of them’. That said, the chef goes easy on this dish, wanting to focus on the ingredients.

Name: Soba Takama
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: There is much more to making soba than meets the eye, and just one step in the process can change everything. The owner-chef prefers the buckwheat variety from Maruoka, Fukui, with which he makes thin juwari soba. The basic offerings are mori soba, which emphasises the feel of the noodles going down, and fragrant inaka soba. The coolness of the pungent daikon, myoga and kinome create a sense of oneness in the myoga oroshi soba. Made with kombu, the dipping sauce brings out the flavour. The thick sobayu with plenty of flour is another example of how things are done here.

Name: Udondokoro Shigemi
Address: B2F, Semba Center Bldg Yongokan, 2-1-4 Sembachuo, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 541-0055, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The owner-chef puts to work his experience in both Kagawa and Osaka. The flavour of the Kansai-style white dashi makes all the difference in the dipping sauce. To fully tease out the natural umami, the chef uses kombu as well as dried flakes of round herring and mackerel. Typical Sanuki items such as kake in dashi broth and bukkake with a smaller amount of rich broth dominate the menu. For this owner-chef, harmony between the two udon cultures is vital.

Name: Gion Yorozuya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: For most customers, the draw is the restaurant’s signature ‘Negi Udon.’ Tender yet springy udon is topped with a generous helping of Kujo leek. ‘Kaho’ (udon with sour pickled ume and shredded kombu), ‘Momiji’ (udon with Pacific herring), and other dishes found their way onto the menu after celebrities requested their favourite ingredients. In summer, the restaurant is decorated with fans used by geisha and maiko, so really exudes the air of the Gion pleasure quarter.

Name: Nonkiya Mune
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: In picture-perfect Kyoto style, Nonkiya Mune is tucked away at the end of a long blind alley. As you enter, the friendly owner-chef and his mother greet you. The heart and soul of the menu is fish and shellfish in season. The preparation of the fish as sashimi, grilled, sakamushi or other style is tailored to each type. Friendly service makes this restaurant easy to love, so naturally many of the customers are locals. Enjoy the harmonious atmosphere that enfolds you in this izakaya.

Name: Gombei
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: The menu is called shitadai, an old-time word that seems somehow fitting. The nuance seems to be, ‘this is our way of welcoming you’. Soba dishes get top billing because Gombei was originally founded as a soba restaurant. Udon dishes, such as the ‘Shippoku’ with lashings of simmered vegetables and ‘Keiran’ with egg-drop and ankake sauce, are typical Kyoto fare. The oyakodon (a bowl of rice topped with chicken and eggs) is also famous. Gombei operates throughout the day, so it’s easy to drop in.

Name: Kitahama Anagoya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The owner-chef first encountered the larger ‘densuke’ anago while training. Astounded by the umami of the flesh and the distribution of the fat, he decided to open a shop specialising in these densuke anago. He prefers using thick anago from Tsushima. In sashimi, the ‘Sanshu-mori’, a combination plate of three cuts (thin, chunky and scorched) is popular. It’s also fun to compare shirayaki with sauce-grilled anago. To end, items such as anago on rice and steamed sushi of nianago are served.

Name: Taiho
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: A father-and-son team mans the woks at this Chinese restaurant. The father’s offerings, which have pleased the locals for generations, sit side-by-side with authentic Szechuan cuisine from the son’s gastronomic studies. One dish for which Taiho has been renowned since its opening is the ‘Teridon Kinshi’. This quintessentially Kyoto dish consists of rice topped with pork and kinshi tamago (ribbons of omelette). Also recommended is the ‘Yodaredori’, steamed chicken with a spicy sauce.

Name: Hommachi Seimenjo Chukasobakobo
Address: B2F, Semba Centar Bldg Nigokan, 1-3-2 Sembachuo, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 541-0055, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: This katsuo-bushi shop opened with a mission to bring to the world the joys of dashi. The flavoursome soup of the shop’s ramen is a combination of seven types of shaved bonito, kombu, seafood such as grilled hamo, and chicken bones. The noodles are made on the premises, with whole wheat flour kneaded into the dough for smoothness and texture. It’s great to get to choose between round and flat noodles. A shake or two of sansho adds a refreshing fragrance to the meal.

Name: Yakitori Matsuri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The chef here took over a restaurant that his old mentor had once run. Here he can be found at the grill, mindful of the heritage he’s acquired. He uses the same breed of Hinai chicken, as when he apprenticed. The same is true of his choice of kishu-binchotan, prized for its consistent flame. The focus at Yakitori Matsuri is the omakase, but he includes single-dish items in the mix, too, such as mizutaki, plain-boiled ingredients served with dipping sauce, and duck sukiyaki.

Name: Yakitori Minami
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining
Description: During his apprenticeship, the owner-chef focused his attention above all on the internal organs of chickens, which is why he is so intent on freshness in the local, free-range chickens he handles. Keen to regale patrons with as many different flavours as possible, he prepares an incredible variety of cuts, including the rarest. Great effort is expended on surprising the guest’s palate at every turn, with the dressing alternating between salt and sauce.

Name: Fuyacho Honda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The owner-chef of this kappo visits the market every morning to ensure that his menu conveys the changing seasons. The appetiser, a combination platter of several aemono and nimono, enhances diner satisfaction. The character of the ingredients comes first, so he goes light on creative touches. Katsuo is seared or soy marinated on a bed of rice; hamo is stone-grilled or served as bozushi. The way he adjusts portion sizes according to the preferences of each customer is also a plus.

Name: Sobashubo Ichii
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining
Description: The marquee dishes here are hand-made soba and duck preparations. The basic seiro (soba noodles served on a wickerwork tray) is the kyuwari type (10% flour) for suppleness and flavour. Coarse ground nihachi and juwari, from different regions, are also used. For added enjoyment, try comparing the various sobas. Osaka Kawachi ducks are used, a good fit due to their tender flesh and sweet fat. Sample the duck seiro or the kamonanban to taste how well the soba dipping sauce goes with the fat.

Name: Shokudo Akari
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining
Description: The visitor’s eye is drawn to key points that highlight owner-chef Fumimasa Minamimoto’s creativity and love for his hometown. The cedarwood decorating the ceiling is modelled after the noboriko torch-bearers procession in the Oto Fire Festival of Minamimoto’s native Wakayama Prefecture. Items grilled over Kishu binchotan are the highlight. The creativity of the spring rolls is a triumph. The meal ends with a croque monsieur, served with fava beans in spring and figs in autumn.

Name: Ayamedo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Pass through the noren and a ‘Showa modern’ style space opens up before you. In this nostalgic atmosphere, customers can enjoy everything from appetisers to soba. A full menu of shuko, such as stewed soybeans with sakura ebi and salt-grilled duck, makes you want to tip back a cup or two of sake. A choice of two thinly cut noodles is available: juwari with its smooth finish and arabiki (coarse ground) with the buckwheat chaff ground into the noodles. Soba in hot broth is offered in the winter.

Name: Omoni
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only
Description: Omoni has been a beloved fixture on the edge of Tsuruhashi Korea Town for over half a century. Commemorative photos celebrities attest to its popularity. ‘Omoni’ is the Korean word for ‘mother’, and while the matriarch has passed it to her eldest son, she remains on hand. The okonomiyaki is grilled with loads of cabbage but relatively little batter, creating a dish that is pleasingly light. In the kimchi-stuffed okonomiyaki, the cuisines of Japan and Korea open their hearts to each other.

Name: Comptoir15
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Interesting wine list,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Tsuyoshi Inoue has an unbridled love for French cuisine and wine. He visits production areas almost every year and sometimes even participates in the harvest. The numerous signatures on the wall speak of the support he has earned from makers. The menu is primarily of authentic traditional cuisine. In particular, the main dishes are local ones from various regions. If you sit at the counter, you can also enjoy chatting with the chef about wine and memories from his trips.

Name: HUNTER
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Chef Imai is as obsessed with meat as a hunter stalking his game. Putting his experience with French cuisine to work, he grills his meat-centric menu on a charcoal grill. In addition to duck, pork and beef, in autumn and winter Imai serves game meats such as boar and deer. Charcuterie such as pâté and rillettes are arranged on plates that look like stumps for a natural look. If you sit at the counter, you’ll have the pleasure of chatting with this personable chef.

Name: Sambongi Shoten
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Notable sake list,Visa credit card
Description: Charcoal-grilled treats, wine and sake are the signature fare of this izakaya. “It’s primitive, but it suits the ingredients”, says the owner-chef as he starts the fire. The menu is centred on meat, such as venison, duck and beef, though the grill also enhances the flavour of seafood and vegetables. The meat is grilled slowly so enjoy the wait with a glass of organic wine or local sake. Many appetisers are French in origin, such as paté of pork and tapenade-dressed vegetables.

Name: Shichiku Kiko
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: As a student, the owner-chef used to entertain his friends with his cooking and he established his restaurant where he spent those youthful days. Simple arrangements such as anago tsukuri with the skin charred and garnished with salt, and rice cooked in earthenware pots make for comforting dishes. Rice and vegetables from Shiga and ayu from Lake Biwa testify to his love of his hometown. A ceramic Shigaraki-ware racoon seated on the floor greets the diner on entering.

Name: ortensia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Owner-chef Nasu incorporates the seasons of two narrow countries that stretch from north to south, Italy and Japan. To study hometown cooking, Nasu apprenticed in multiple parts of Italy. In spring, he offers baked edible wild plants and scamorza cheese; in summer, fritters of hamo and dry-cured ham. Each dish has a unique character. Nasu feels a strong emotional attachment to the Puglia-style spaghetti with karasumi, a speciality he learned from his local mentor.

Name: Pizzeria Napoletana Da Yuki
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Impressed by pizza baked by Neapolitan chefs, owner-chef Yuki Kamada devoted himself to learning the craft in Naples. The wood-fired oven he uses was imported from Italy and the dough is baked at high heat for fragrance and light texture. There are always about 30 types of pizza on offer – and you can order half-and-half if you have trouble deciding on just one. Drawing on his experience working at a Neapolitan trattoria, he also offers a copious line-up of appetisers.

Name: kushiage 010
Address: 4F, Tanaka Bldg, 1-1-41 Sonezakishinchi, Kita-ku, Osaka, 530-0002, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: These creative kushiage incorporate culinary influences from many countries. The sheer variety is endlessly fun. For your first skewer, you might start with angel shrimp from New Caledonia. The samgyeopsal (grilled pork-belly slices) wrapped in perilla and Korean lettuce is spiced with gochujang for a real Korean treat. With the tandoori chicken in curry and yogurt sauce, the fragrance of India floats in the air. An excursion through the flavours of the world through kushiage awaits.

Name: Kushiage toshico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The music that plays in the background here is borderless: rock, jazz and techno. Having previously worked at a record shop, the head chef works to the rhythm of the sizzling oil as he lightly fries the skewers. The standard items are shrimp and beef, and he mixes in creative ones like scallops wrapped in kombu and salmon with salmon roe. The sense of anticipation as you bring the food to your mouth is like when waiting for the needle to hit the record.

Name: Suigyo Murabayashi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Diners Club credit card,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: The name Suigyo, roughly ‘pure fish’, announces this restaurant’s devotion to conveying its pure flavour. The owner-chef uses fish sent directly each morning from fishermen and fishing ports. The signature dishes are tsukuri and simmered fish. The sashimi is cut thick, while the simmered fish is seasoned only with water and soy sauce. The seafood nabe with added fruit or mochi is recommended. This dynamic cuisine overflows with the restaurant’s passion for fish.

Name: Koneser Grill
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: This redeveloped former vodka factory to the east of the city comes with an industrial look and a laid-back vibe. It’s all about steak here, with a focus on Polish beef, aged in-house, and then cooked over a wood-fired grill. Prices represent good value and the steaks to share are a great option.

Name: alewino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Spread across various rooms, this starkly decorated bistro started life as a wine shop. There’s still a range of bottles for sale, along with a wine list that offers plenty of younger and lesser-known producers. The well-priced menu includes more starters than mains, which allows guests to order a few plates to share. Traditional Polish flavours and dishes are approached with a modern sensibility and prepared with plenty of care.

Name: Kieliszki na Próżnej
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Bring your own bottle,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: A huge, gravity-defying rack of wine glasses is the first thing you notice when you arrive at this friendly wine bar and bistro. Next, it’s the striking black and white wildlife mural filling one wall. The appealing menus represent good value, especially at lunchtime, and include hearty dishes that are bursting with bold and punchy flavours. An extensive wine list offers plenty of great quality choices to fill all those glasses with, but ‘bring your own’ is welcome too.

Name: Choy (Phuttha Monthon Sai 2)
Address: 9/19 Phuttha Monthon Sai 2 Road, Bang Khae Nuea, Bang Khae, Bangkok, 10160, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only
Description: A little out of the way but this is one of the best kept secrets for roast duck with egg noodles. Try the signature duck noodles with shrimp wonton in Tom Yam soup. Choy is named after the owner; the duck recipe came from his father.

Name: Magnolia Café
Address: 131/70, 131/82 Rattanakosin Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 503200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: With just four large communal tables, Magnolia is a simple, cosy spot enlivened by bold colours, vintage décor, and chandeliers. Their à la carte menu offers tasty, well presented fare from across Thailand. Dishes are distinguished by vivid, gutsy flavours; fried sun-dried squid with peanut sauce and fresh watermelon with desiccated salmon are exemplars. In lieu of a dessert menu, they serve lovely complimentary pandan pudding. Do visit their wine shop next door.

Name: Sri Trat
Address: 90 Soi Sukhumvit 33, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,China UnionPay,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Valet parking,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’ve been to the coastal province of Trat on the border of Cambodia, you’ll doubtless recall its fiery seafood and curries. At Sri Trat, the owners bring the province’s famed cuisine to Bangkok via their mother’s favourite recipes. They also honour her, not only with a funky mural, but also by expertly crafting eastern dishes like savoury stir-fried tiger prawn with garlic, chilli, and fish sauce and spicy sea bass soup with salacca and shrimp paste.

Name: Baan Landai
Address: 252/13-14 Phra Pok Klao Road, Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Don’t let the slightly unkempt exterior keep you from visiting Chef Landai’s eponymous restaurant, where he practises the craft he learned from his mother. The interior exudes charm with its eclectic adornments and window to the kitchen where chefs whip up pan-Thai dishes like flavourful pork ribs with red wine sauce (plus several veggie offerings). Pair with flower tea, mocktails, or cocktails, and finish with mung bean marzipan and egg yolk in coconut milk.

Name: Coscolo
Address: La Magdalena 1, Castrillo de los Polvazares, 24718, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This delightful village is famous for its “Cocido Maragato”, a dish that for centuries has, against convention, been served here in reverse order (first the meat, then the chickpeas, followed by the soup at the end). At Coscolo, the special feature of this legendary recipe is that it is prepared with products that are smoked, cured and prepared on the property using ingredients sourced from the local area. To this stew the Navarra-born chef here likes to add tiny details that add even more personality, hence the change of name of the dish on the menu to that of his restaurant (“Cocido Coscolo”). Leave your car in the car park at the entrance to the village as only local residents are allowed to drive in.

Name: El Chaleco
Address: Avenida Costa del Sol 37, Almuñécar, 18690, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: A restaurant with a good reputation, now run by the daughter of the previous owners, who has managed to maintain its essence but with a fresher and more modern perspective. In the attractive dining room, divided into two separate spaces, guests can savour French-inspired cuisine which is unusual for this area. The cooking is mainly focused around a single set-price menu, although this is complemented by several chef’s suggestions and the occasional special dish at a supplement. Keep your eye out for El Chaleco’s frequent themed menus (lobster, seafood special, anniversary, Belgian etc).

Name: Casa Pedro
Address: Poeta García Lorca 5, Puente Genil, 14500, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: Named after its owner, the Casa Pedro has been taking orders for over 30 years, during which time it has developed the secret to ensuring its customers always leave happy, based around consistent and professional family-style service. Choose between the tapas bar at the entrance, where you can select from a varied daily menu, the more classically inspired dining room, or a slightly more contemporary private dining space. Traditional, market-inspired cooking of a very high quality, featuring a choice of cured and red meats, fish, seafood and seasonal vegetables, many of which come with a “media-ración” option.

Name: Zabala
Address: Mateo Benigno de Moraza 9, Vitoria-Gasteiz, 01001, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Visa credit card
Description: Zabala is situated in the district of Los Arquillos, popular with tourists, just a few metres away from the Plaza Mayor. Behind its attractive stone façade, you’ll find two highly distinct spaces: one, at street level, with a meticulous contemporary look that includes a striking wave-like wood decor; the other, upstairs, home to carefully appointed dining rooms, a private section, plus one room crowned by a large vaulted ceiling. The dishes on the traditional à la carte, prepared using ingredients of the finest quality, is embellished with the occasional contemporary touch. The set menu is only available on weekdays.

Name: S.B.L.
Address: 710-714 Maha Chai Road, Wang Burapha Phirom, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Open since 1954, this Chinese restaurant is currently run by a second-generation family member who is keen to make every aspect of the dining experience pleasurable. The menu features mostly traditional Chinese fare with a few creations that show novel twists. The X.O. scallops are a must-try, as is the expertly-steamed snow fish with soya sauce. Quality ingredients handled with skill and experience is the formula that guarantees a good meal here.

Name: Saiyud and Doctor Sai Kitchen
Address: 32 Chotana Soi 12 Road, Pa Tan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,JCB,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Since 2004, Doctor Sai has been serving pan-Thai dishes, including royal fare, following recipes from her mother, Saiyud, a former cooking instructor, in a setting reminiscent of dining at home. Start with an elegant appetiser like fried prawns and peanuts in an egg net, flower dumplings, or deep-fried pork wrapped in egg noodles. By dessert – try the sweet potato in syrup – you’ll guess this home, with its warm service, belongs to a royal from a bygone era.

Name: Kha Mu Boran (Kathu)
Address: 17/11 Mu 6, Wichit Songkhram Road, Kathu, Phuket, 83120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Cash only
Description: This long-standing street food spot specialises in Kamu, braised pork shanks with a five-spice sauce. It may be a common dish, but the version they serve here is head and shoulders above the average. The shanks are of good quality and are braised for six hours until the meat is falling off the bone. They can be served with a well-balanced sipping broth which comes with meaty bones to be gnawed on. They’re clearly doing something right, because both locals and tourists flock here for lunch.

Name: Meena Rice Based Cuisine
Address: 13/5 Mu 2, San Klang, San Kamphaeng, Chiang Mai, 50130, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Don’t be alarmed when you pass through a rice field driving here, as this hidden gem is worth it. As its name suggests, this alfresco restaurant specialises in rice, alongside new spins on Thai classics. Most are garnished with fruits and edible flowers, giving them bursts of colour. Along with the five-colour rice balls, northern-style spicy minced fish salad is a delight. Vegans will enjoy their many options, including the spicy stir-fried eryngii mushrooms.

Name: Baannai
Address: 102/13 Soi Kamphaeng Phet 5, Set Siri Road, Sam Sen Nai, Phaya Thai, Bangkok, 10400, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Valet parking,Visa credit card
Description: Baan Nai, or ‘inner house’ in Thai, is so called because the owner’s great grandfather built it on the innermost part of his land. The house, and recipes cooked by its occupants, have passed down through the family to the present day where, as a boutique hotel and homely restaurant, it serves delicious time-tested dishes like Taengmo Pla Haeng (watermelon with dried fish flakes) and Khanom Pra Paii (sweet mung bean dumplings). Booking is required.

Name: La Mundana
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: Located in a residential neighbourhood in the Sants district, La Mundana is a former “vermutería” (vermouth bar) converted into a gastro-bar… and one that is always full! Here, chefs Alain Guiard and Marc Martin enjoy toying with flavours from around the world to create dishes with plenty of culinary personality and creativity, most notably through the flavours of the Mediterranean, France and Japan. In this relaxed atmosphere, with tables set close together and an open-view kitchen, choose from a menu designed for sharing, on which two “absolute musts” stand out: the Mundana “patatas bravas” and the Asian calamares. The extensive choice of vermouths is equally impressive.

Name: Divinis
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Booking essential,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: You’ll find this intimate, homely restaurant tucked away on a side street; it’s run with great passion and has a friendly feel. Rustic, seasonal Italian dishes have original touches and are cooked with flair. The perfect accompaniment comes in the form of a large collection of wines from Italian growers.

Name: Dejvická 34 by Tomáš Černý
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Chef-owner Tomaš Černy worked in the best Italian restaurants in the city for many years before opening his own charming neighbourhood restaurant north of the river. The menu mixes Czech and Italian dishes and showcases some top quality imported ingredients. Dishes are robust and packed with flavour.

Name: The Eatery
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Interesting wine list,Mastercard credit card,Visa credit card
Description: This highly regarded restaurant in the suburbs delivers much more than its name and industrial styling first imply. The menu evolves from day to day, in line with the latest seasonal produce, and is accompanied by a superb wine list. Ask for a seat at the counter to witness the efficiency of the kitchen team.

Name: Na Kopci
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Booking essential,Car park,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: Leave the city behind and escape to this buzzy bistro, whose name means ‘on the hill’. The wallpaper is a montage of pictures of the owner’s family and the atmosphere is warm and welcoming. Classic Czech and French dishes are packed with flavour and the local beers make a great accompaniment.

Name: Eska
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Visa credit card
Description: A café, bakery and restaurant in a converted fabric factory. The dining room has a stark, industrial feel with exposed bricks, pipework and girders, and the open kitchen adds to the buzz. Old family favourites are given modern makeovers; much use is made of traditional techniques like marinating and fermenting.

Name: Casa Santo Antônio
Address: Avenida João Carlos da Silva Borges 764, São Paulo, 04726-001, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,American Express credit card,Credit card / Debit card accepted,Diners Club credit card,Mastercard credit card,Terrace,Valet parking,Visa credit card,Wheelchair access
Description: A perfect example of how a dream between friends – now co-owners – can become a reality. In Granja Julieta, a quiet district in the south of the city, you’ll find this pleasant 1960s style chalet, where guests can choose from an impressive classic Italian menu featuring specialities such as burrata with tomatoes, olives and slivers of Sicilian lemon, or the superb brie tortelli with a truffle-flavoured sauce. Some of the tables on the terrace enjoy views of the glass-fronted kitchen. (Last update: September 2020).

Name: Nit
Address: Rua Oscar Freire 145, São Paulo, 01409-003, Brazil
